ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Trajectory KL Regularization for Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Implement Trajectory KL regularization for diffusion model fine-tuning on text-to-image generation using DALL-E 2 as the pre-trained reference model and evaluating performance on COCO validation set. Use an exact KL loss between entire denoising trajectories and a KL-regularized PPO objective, comparing results with baseline PPO.
CONTROLS:abcdef:
1) Run baseline PPO on text-to-image generation for DALL-E 2 and store its results (approx. 10 GPU-hours).
2) Implement KL regularization on denoising trajectory for same objective to get distributed loss and find KL result (approx. 50 GPU-hours)
COST: 50
PREDICTION: Trajectory KL regularization should converge faster and outperform baseline PPO due to the stability brought by the regularization, but it might underperform on more challenging or diverse tasks.

Note:  Trajectory KL regularization might correct the offset between the reference and target distributions during fine-tuning. Estimation can be positive and this will be leveraged in later experiments to get distribution alignment methods which combined well with the methods fine-tuning will be a great fit.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Trajectory KL Regularization Estimates via Importance Weights
PROPOSAL: Evaluate several estimators of the trajectory KL divergence based on importance weights in the context of fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion models. We will compare Reweight, a state-of-the-art importance-weight estimator that has shown strong performance for KL-based importance weighting, andULA, an unweighted and uniform version of Reweight used as a baseline, with two variants of re-weighting by raw sample likelihood. This will be done using the Training of Un-Normally Distributed Sampled network (ToNS) and the Conditional Denoising Autoencoder (CDAE) diffusion models fine-tuned on text-to-image generation and document layout generation tasks from the COCO dataset and the UIlit dataset, respectively. 
CONTROLS: Performance comparison against KL-mediated fine-tuning without any re-weighting and against given state-of-the-art rejection sampling methods RSO and RAFT.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: We expect to see the Reweight estimator perform competitively or outperform estimates made by the other re-weighting methods, yielding well-regularized fine-tuned models. However we expect noisy or biased results from the heuristic or un-weighted baseline methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models Using a Flow-Based Regularizer
PROPOSAL: Utilize the invertible phenomena of flow models to define a regularizer for the denoising diffusion model. We consider a pre-trained diffusion model and a pre-trained flow model, both trained on the same task or dataset. We use the pre-trained flow model's inverse transformation to regularize the fine-tuning of the diffusion model, achieving a structured regularization which leverages the invertible nature of both the pre-trained and fine-tuned flow and diffusion models, using text-to-text generation from the machine translation dataset WMT, document layout generation from UIlit and molecule generation from ZINC and MUVI.
CONTROLS: KL divergence in the distribution between fine-tuning and the reference flow model distribution should provide a route for checking effects of previous proposals concerning relative piant Changes from current. Will also serve as the first experiment to confirm the notions regarding the invertible phenomena existence 
COST: 27128
PREDICTION: We expect that the structural regularization proposed in this work will outperform existing trajectory-based regularization methods as it leverages the specific invertible structure of both flow and diffusion models and directly uses pre-trained knowledge without making intractable assumptions.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models without Explicit Rewards
PROPOSAL: Explore the possibility of fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion models using only samples from the data distribution, without any explicit reward functions. We propose a simple, adaptive approach that leverages the pre-trained model's knowledge to correct errors and align the generated samples with the target data distribution. We will apply this method to the task of text-to-image generation from COCO, document layout generation from UIlit and molecule generation from MUVI, and evaluate the quality of the generated samples using a set of metrics that capture their similarity to the ground truth.
CONTROLS: Direct comparison to fine-tuning with explicit rewards and a baseline of no fine-tuning.
COST: 27252
PREDICTION: We expect that the proposed adaptive method can correct errors and improve the quality of the generated samples without the need for explicit rewards, and that it can be a valuable addition to the toolbox of techniques for fine-tuning diffusion models.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Structure of Diffusion and Flow Models for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the potential for fine-tuning diffusion and flow models by exploiting their specific structural properties, such as the generative process of a sequence of denoising steps or the invertible nature of flow models. We propose to analyze the effects of different fine-tuning strategies that leverage these properties on the quality and stability of the fine-tuned models, using a range of tasks and datasets, including text-to-image generation from COCO, document layout generation from UIlit and molecule generation from MUVI. We will also study the interplay between these structural properties and the imposed regularization terms during fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: Comparison to standard fine-tuning methods and a baseline of no fine-tuning.
COST: 60750
PREDICTION: We expect that by exploiting the structural properties of diffusion and flow models, we can develop more effective fine-tuning methods that yield higher-quality and more stable models, with reduced computational requirements and improved generalizability.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multimodal Fine-Tuning and Domain Adaptation for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Propose a framework for multimodal fine-tuning and domain adaptation of diffusion models by leveraging multiple pre-trained diffusion models, each trained on a different domain or modality. We will investigate the potential for adaptive fine-tuning of the pre-trained models using a shared set of input data from each domain, allowing the models to learn a common representation that can be specialized for each domain. This will enable the creation of domain-agnostic diffusion models that can be fine-tuned for a wide range of applications and datasets, including text-to-image generation from COCO, document layout generation from UIlit and molecule generation from MUVI.
CONTROLS: Comparison to standard fine-tuning methods and a baseline of no fine-tuning, as well as evaluation of the ability of the multimodal model to generalize across domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Trajectory KL Regularization Estimates via Importance Weights
PROPOSAL: Evaluate several estimators of the trajectory KL divergence based on importance weights in the context of fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion models. We will compare Reweight, a state-of-the-art importance-weight estimator that has shown strong performance for KL-based importance weighting, andULA, an unweighted and uniform version of Reweight used as a baseline, with two variants of re-weighting by raw sample likelihood. This will be done using the Training of Un-Normally Distributed Sampled network (ToNS) and the Conditional Denoising Autoencoder (CDAE) diffusion models fine-tuned on text-to-image generation and document layout generation tasks from the COCO dataset and the UIlit dataset, respectively. 
CONTROLS: Performance comparison against KL-mediated fine-tuning without any re-weighting and against given state-of-the-art rejection sampling methods RSO and RAFT.
COST: 13500
PREDICTION: We expect to see the Reweight estimator perform competitively or outperform estimates made by the other re-weighting methods, yielding well-regularized fine-tuned models. However we expect noisy or biased results from the heuristic or un-weighted baseline methods.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Revising Trajectory KL Regularization Estimates via Importance Weights
PROPOSAL: In the spirit of minimizing the initial value function bias, we will add to the previous experiment a new variant wrt Reweight which uses not only the re-weighted past trajectory but also incorporates the predictions made by a pre-trained model made on the real data to reduce the bias. The predictions will be incorporated by re-weighting the last few denoising steps with a learned filtering process which takes as input the data as evaluated using a supervised learning setup.
CONTROLS: We compare results with the original Reweight estimator and with results from previous experiment.
COST: 20650
PREDICTION: We expect that by incorporating the pre-trained model's predictions into the trajectory KL, we can reduce the bias in the fine-tuned models, that we can improve results across-the-board, especially in those benchmarks where data generation processes were unfamiliar and data fitting was imperfect.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models Using a Flow-Based Regularizer
PROPOSAL: Utilize the invertible phenomena of flow models to define a regularizer for the denoising diffusion model. We consider a pre-trained diffusion model and a pre-trained flow model, both trained on the same task or dataset. We use the pre-trained flow model's inverse transformation to regularize the fine-tuning of the diffusion model, achieving a structured regularization which leverages the invertible nature of both the pre-trained and fine-tuned flow and diffusion models, using text-to-text generation from the machine translation dataset WMT, document layout generation from UIlit and molecule generation from ZINC and MUVI.
CONTROLS: KL divergence in the distribution between fine-tuning and the reference flow model distribution should provide a route for checking effects of previous proposals concerning relative piant Changes from current. Will also serve as the first experiment to confirm the notions regarding the invertible phenomena existence 
COST: 81500
PREDICTION: We expect that the structural regularization proposed in this work will outperform existing trajectory-based regularization methods as it leverages the specific invertible structure of both flow and diffusion models and directly uses pre-trained knowledge without making intractable assumptions.

TITLE: Best-Of-N Sampling and KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: Study the performance of Best-Of-N (BoN) sampling method on fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion models for three tasks: text-to-image generation from COCO, document layout generation from UIlit and molecule generation from MUVI, and compare with existing KL-regularized reward maximization methods like Reweight estimator, when used with both BoN and Gibbs sampling, we also validate these comparisons when controlling numbers and steps strongly differently like adding or removing FITRegimization assumptions that were extensively regarded during well trained transformation.

TITLE: 2. Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models Using a Flow-Based Regularizer
PROPOSAL: In this experiment, we modify the flow-based regularizer to utilize a pre-trained diffusion model as a "denoiser" to regularize the fine-tuning of the flow model, leveraging the pre-trained knowledge of the diffusion model to improve the flow-based regularization. We use this modified flow-based regularizer to fine-tune a pre-trained flow model on the text-to-text generation task from the WMT dataset, with a pre-trained diffusion model trained on the same task serving as the regularizer, in addition to fine-tune the diffusion model itself,  allowing for a unified exploration of the trade-offs between the two models and varying the step numbers and different quantities greatly affects performance comparing performance of new and old flow model we contrast our results with state-of-the-art hyperparameters subject such aberrant text metrics timeless loose measures and concentrate decline in time specific reliability.
CONTROLS: Additional comparisons of performance of the modified flow-based regularizer to standard flow-based regularization and diffusion-based regularization as well as when fine-tuning the pre-trained diffusion model.

PREDICTION: We expect that using a pre-trained diffusion model as a denoiser in the flow-based regularizer will lead to better fine-tuned flow models with improved quality and diversity, and that this approach can significantly reduce the likelihood of overfitting and improve the overall efficiency of the flow-based regularization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models without Explicit Rewards
PROPOSAL: Explore the possibility of fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion models using only samples from the data distribution, without any explicit reward functions. We propose a simple, adaptive approach that leverages the pre-trained model's knowledge to correct errors and align the generated samples with the target data distribution. COST: 81850
PREDICTION: We expect that the proposed adaptive method can correct errors and improve the quality of the generated samples without the need for explicit rewards, and that it can be a valuable addition to the toolbox of techniques for fine-tuning diffusion models.

ACTION: ADD 1 
TITLE: Invertible KL Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Train a diffusion model to minimize a proxy objective that upper-bounds the marginal KL divergence, using either a variational autoencoder (VAE) or an inference network to provide an approximate inverse mapping from the pre-trained distribution to the target distribution, allowing for the computation of a KL-regularized reward maximization objective.
CONTROLS: Baseline reinforcement learning algorithms such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and a KL-free model fine-tuning setup for comparison; Recursive Autoencoder (RAE) as a VAE alternative to test sensitivity to the choice of model family.
COST: 16.6875 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The KL regularization will stabilize the training process but may introduce bias in some settings, as estimates of the pre-trained distribution can be imperfect; application to text-to-image generation will outperform comparison methods, with moderate success in document layout generation and molecule generation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Exploring Activation Magnitude Stein Steering for Continuous Control"
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the effects of steering the magnitude of activations rather than their directions, using Stein Steering, a recently proposed method for asymmetric diffusion that alters the distribution of activations while preserving their directions. This can be done during the final normalization step in transformer layers, effectively controlling the scale of each direction independently. 
CONTROLS: (1) Baseline: standard activation steering with addition and ablation; (2) ablation of Stein steering, comparing to Stein steering with added noise; (3) comparison of Stein steering to null gives the internal baseline for Stein steering.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: By altering the magnitude of activations, we should be able to achieve finer control over how strongly a target behavior is expressed, while leaving unrelated features relatively untouched. Failure could occur if the model struggles to maintain consistency in the face of significant changes to activation magnitudes.

TITLE: "Theoretical Analysis of Activation Alignment"
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the theoretical properties of activation alignment, a crucial aspect of directional ablation in activation steering, where activations are projected onto the orthogonal complement of a feature direction. Specifically, we aim to derive bounds on the effect of orthogonal projection on activation norms and to analyze its effect on the loss landscape of the language model.
CONTROLS: None
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Our results should provide a deeper understanding of the theoretical underpinnings of directional ablation and offer insights into how activation alignment can be optimized for better behavior control in LLMs. However, deriving bounds on the effect of orthogonal projection may turn out to be challenging, and the analysis might not be entirely straightforward.

TITLE: A Fine-Grained Activation Steering Framework for LLMs
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel framework that combines activation addition and orthogonal projection, allowing for continuous control over a target behavior by learning a weight that gates the strength of addition and orthogonalization. This framework, dubbed Weighted Activation Steering (WAS), combines the benefits of feature-oriented control with a degree of tolerance for layer-wise activation magnitudes.
CONTROLS: We compare WAS against stance-pointing Activation Addition and orthogonal-projection-only Differential Ablation (DA) on the JACCAR dataset, with Fine-Tuned ALBERT as the backbone model. TITLE: Investigating Vector Field Methods for Activation Steering
PROPOSAL: We compare the performance of vector field methods for activation steering, which involves representing the steering manipulations as flows on the activation space, to traditional methods such as activation addition and directional ablation. Specifically, we use the Vector Field Steer and the Differentiable Normalizing Flow-based Steering methods, and apply them to refuse harmful requests, regulate emotional tone in generated text, and modulate other behaviors. We investigate whether vector field methods can provide continuous, fine-grained control over target behaviors and outperform traditional methods.
CONTROLS: Traditional activation addition and directional ablation as baselines, ablation over different vector flow architectures and the use of synthetic data for steering
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: We expect vector field methods to demonstrate improved performance over traditional methods in refining specific behaviors, but may fail to achieve similar performance on more general tasks due to the complex interactions between behavior control and language generation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-Modal Federated Multi-Task Learning with Dynamic Model Alignment
PROPOSAL: We'll investigate a novel architecture, MoDT (Model-agnostic Dynamic Transfer), which integrates a shared representation learning module with adaptive aggregation and alignment mechanisms. Dynamic model alignment allows multiple models with different architectures to learn a common representation space, leveraging their individual strengths. In the first phase (Phase-I), a shared encoder learns a task-agnostic representation by canonical correlation analysis on the local datasets, while a novel decoupled optimization strategy can accommodate  diverse architectures and training frequencies. In Phase-II, we split each representation into task-specific predictor heads and use a variant of the InfoNCE loss to align these predictors across models. Additionally, a supervised term fine-tunes the shared encoder for each local task. We use simulated multiple tasks as the local datasets and the shared representation learning is controlled through self-modulation.
CONTROLS: We compare MoDT with a homogenous model baseline trained on each task separately, and with Prior CL, a recently proposed Gramian-based contrastive loss where each model learning phase is updated using the output of other models to improve shared representation learning among all models.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: By not relying on any congruence or transferring gradients across models, MoDT could enable more models to participate in federated learning. In contrast, Prior CL might experience numerical instability in representing multiple functions together by using matrices of parameters in their projected loss space.

TITLE: Knowledge Distillation-driven Model Adaptation for Federated Multi-task Learning
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of model heterogeneity in federated multi-task learning, we propose a novel approach that utilizes knowledge distillation to adapt local models to a shared representation space. The method, named DistillFed, consist of two stages: in the first stage, a teacher model is trained on a selected subset of user data, and in the second stage, student models are trained using a knowledge distillation loss function that encourages the student models to mimic the teacher model's behavior. We evaluate DistillFed on various federated multi-task learning scenarios and compare its performance to state-of-the-art methods.
CONTROLS: We compare DistillFed with MoDT, a baseline that assumes model homogeneity, and with Prior CL, which aligns representations among models without addressing model heterogeneity.
COST: 1331.09
PREDICTION: DistillFed will demonstrate improved performance over MoDT and Prior CL on various federated multi-task learning scenarios by effectively adapting local models to a shared representation space, but may experience increased computational overhead due to the knowledge distillation process.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Model-Agnostic Contrastive Experience Distillation 
PROPOSAL: We propose a model-agnostic federated multi-task learning method that leverages contrastive experience distillation to align representations across tasks with arbitrary architectures. We will compare different architectures and our method will learn a shared representation space that captures the dependencies among all representations, via a tractable InfoNCE-based objective with a series of jointly learned pairing Fourier coefficients as matrices.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method against existing model-agnostic federated multi-task learning methods that scale contrastive learning to multiple tasks, including method's in which each local model is a subset of a global model and methods that exchange outputs on an unlabeled public dataset via knowledge distillation.
COST: 3360
PREDICTION: Our approach shows significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods, especially in rare and imbalanced classes. However, this could fail in highly diverse tasks where object similarity and pair definition might lose relevance; there could be other related work that combine attention-guided distillation with set-wise information-theoretic stability techniques.

TITLE: Master-Slave Framework for Federated Domain Adaptation Across Model Architectures 
PROPOSAL: We propose a master-slave framework for federated domain adaptation that enables a master node to adapt a shared model across multiple domains using knowledge distillation and a slave node to adapt its local model to the master's shared model under limited communication.
CONTROLS: We compare our framework against existing model-agnostic domain adaptation methods and methods that rely on individually learning model-specific domain adapters.
COST: 6720
PREDICTION: Our approach shows significant improvements in domain adaptation performance, especially in scenarios with limited communication and large models, but might suffer from overadaptation when the master node has a large number of clients.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Model-Agnostic Contrastive Experience Distillation 
PROPOSAL: We revise our model-agnostic federated multi-task learning approach to incorporate an additional mutual consistency loss to ensure that the shared representation space is invariant to task-specific information, promoting more robust knowledge transfer across tasks with arbitrary architectures.
CONTROLS: We compare our revised approach against existing model-agnostic federated multi-task learning methods that do not incorporate mutual consistency loss and methods that focus on improving heterogeneity and preventing either forgetting per relevance backups greet filters physics excited local exhibit Markets Therapy.
COST: 5300
PREDICTION: Improved task performance and knowledge transfer are noticeable, but the mutual consistency loss might introduce additional computational overhead when there are a large number of tasks.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Graph Neural Network-based Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Tasks 
PROPOSAL: We propose a graph neural network-based federated learning approach for heterogeneous tasks, where a graph is constructed to represent the relationships between tasks and clients, and a shared model is learned to adapt to the graph-structured task space.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against existing federated learning methods for heterogeneous tasks and methods that focus on improving task heterogeneity and preventing forgetting via various normalization strategies and context-aware attention mechanisms.
COST: 7308
PREDICTION: Our approach shows significant improvements in task performance and adaptability, especially in scenarios with a large number of tasks and clients, but might suffer from computational overhead due to the complex graph structure.

TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Model-Agnostic Contrastive Experience Distillation 
PROPOSAL: We propose a model-agnostic federated multi-task learning method that leverages contrastive experience distillation to align representations across tasks with arbitrary architectures. We will compare different architectures and our method will learn a shared representation space that captures the dependencies among all representations, via a tractable InfoNCE-based objective with a series of jointly learned pairing Fourier coefficients as matrices.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method against existing model-agnostic federated multi-task learning methods that scale contrastive learning to multiple tasks, including method's in which each local model is a subset of a global model and methods that exchange outputs on an unlabeled public dataset via knowledge distillation.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: Our approach shows significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods, especially in rare and imbalanced classes. However, this could fail in highly diverse tasks where object similarity and pair definition might lose relevance; there could be other related work that combine attention-guided distillation with set-wise information-theoretic stability techniques.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Privately Shared Gramian Alignments
PROPOSAL: Investigate a federated learning approach that aligns representations across multiple models by sharing Gramian matrices derived from the task-agnostic representations. This is achieved by centrally collecting and distributing the low-rank Gramian matrices, which require less communication compared to raw representations or pairwise similarities. Users can then update their models using a variant of the InfoNCE loss that incorporates these Gramian matrices.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing methods under restrictions (e.g., knowledge distillation with output alignment) and without (e.g., the proposed method).
COST: 1440
PREDICTION: The new approach will significantly reduce the communication overhead while maintaining strong task-agnostic alignment, possibly restricting it to just a few tasks. There is a risk that low-rank Gramian approximations might discard critical information necessary for accurate task relationships.

ACTION: REVISE 7
TITLE: Adaptive Federated Learning with Hierarchical Shared Latent Spaces
PROPOSAL: Refine the hierarchical learning approach in federated settings, where users share and adapt jointly learned latent spaces across multiple abstraction levels to enhance knowledge transfer across tasks and users. This is based on a multilayer fusion of user-level knowledge graphs, but with the addition of a novel hierarchical dimensionality reduction technique to preserve the underlying representation structures, ensuring meaningful alignment.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing hierarchical methods (1 and 6) and evaluate on challenging multi-task benchmarks to demonstrate the benefits of both the hierarchical and dimensionality reduction aspects.
COST: 17280
PREDICTION: This refined approach will significantly improve knowledge transfer by focusing on more meaningful latent space alignment, but may require further tuning for optimal performance and may be computationally expensive due to the added dimensionality reduction step.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Task-Agnostic Federated Multi-Task Learning with Shared Encoder
PROPOSAL: We'll investigate a new federated multi-task learning method, where users share a task-agnostic encoder and have task-specific predictors that aren't shared. For each user, we'll use a pre-trained BERT base model as the shared encoder and fine-tune it using their local data. The task-specific predictor will be a small fully-connected network and will be trained from scratch. To align representations across users, we'll add a proximal term in the loss function based on centered kernel alignment, as in the model-agnostic alternative.
CONTROLS: Federated XOR, Federated Multi-Task Learning, federated semi-supervised methods, federated contrastive methods
COST: 3360
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in model generalization compared to federated methods that don't share an encoder; potential issues with slower convergence and higher communication costs, as the shared encoder needs to be updated and synchronized across users.

Note that our initial method will only involve two tasks per user, and we will investigate later if the number of tasks can be scaled up.

The frozen layer will project the inputs into a shared, task-agnostic space. For the fine-tuning step, we'll replace the small fully-connected network with a model-agnostic adapter that can be added to any model architecture.

PREDICTION: Expected improvement in model generalization due to flexibility in model architecture; potential issues with overfitting if the frozen layer or adapter are not carefully designed.

Note that we'll also investigate using knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge from the shared encoder to the model-specific adapters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Task-Agnostic Federated Multi-Task Learning with Shared Encoder
PROPOSAL: We'll investigate a new federated multi-task learning method, where users share a task-agnostic encoder and have task-specific predictors that aren't shared. For each user, we'll use a pre-trained BERT base model as the shared encoder and fine-tune it using their local data. The task-specific predictor will be a small fully-connected network and will be trained from scratch. To align representations across users, we'll add a proximal term in the loss function based on centered kernel alignment, as in the model-agnostic alternative.
CONTROLS: Federated XOR, Federated Multi-Task Learning, federated semi-supervised methods, federated contrastive methods
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in model generalization compared to federated methods that don't share an encoder; potential issues with slower convergence and higher communication costs, as the shared encoder needs to be updated and synchronized across users.

Note that our initial method will only involve two tasks per user, and we will investigate later if the number of tasks can be scaled up.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Task-Agnostic Federated Multi-Task Learning with Shared Encoder: Heterogeneous Model Architectures
PROPOSAL: To address model heterogeneity, we'll modify the shared encoder to be architecture-agnostic. This will involve replacing the pre-trained BERT base model with a frozen layer that takes input from any model architecture. The frozen layer will project the inputs into a shared, task-agnostic space. For the fine-tuning step, we'll replace the small fully-connected network with a model-agnostic adapter that can be added to any model architecture.
CONTROLS: Proposal 1, similar models with frozen layers, similar models with model-agnostic adapters
COST: 15000
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in model generalization due to flexibility in model architecture; potential issues with overfitting if the frozen layer or adapter are not carefully designed.

Note that we'll also investigate using knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge from the shared encoder to the model-specific adapters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Representation Alignment through Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: To address the limitations of pairwise alignment in representation learning, we'll incorporate a Gramian-based contrastive loss that aligns all representations simultaneously, as an alternative to the proximal term in Proposal 1. This will involve minimizing the loss function introduced by the newly proposed Gramian-based contrastive loss.
CONTROLS: Proposal 1, Gramian-based baseline comparing it to InfoNCE
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in joint representation alignment; potential issues with higher computational costs and the lack of theoretical guarantees for the Gramian-based loss.

We'll also explore adding an adaptation of the Gramian-based loss to the Hessian-aligned XVI proposed elsewhere (rank-based, kernal-based and hessian-kernel alignment in respective findings of various papers) to improve this representation of initiator.

We'll propose and analyze conditions under which the Gramian-based loss converges to a common representation space, and how it generalizes across tasks and models.
CONTROLS: Original Gramian-based baseline, related distance-based models and matrix-based models
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: Expected theoretical justification for the Gramian-based loss; potential issues with deriving conditions that are too restrictive, limiting the generality of the results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Active Learning of Label Correction Strategies for Noisy Labels
PROPOSAL: We'll experiment with an active learning-based framework for learning the best label correction strategies. Specifically, we'll use the "pick-and-label" framework, where we actively select and label a subset of the noisy instances and then retrain a model using these corrected labels. We'll compare different acquisition functions, including uncertainty-based, MIS (Maximum Ignorance Sampling), and random selection. We'll also explore the effectiveness of incorporating teacher models to improve the active learning process.
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments will include supervised learning on noisy labels without any correction, as well as the state-of-the-art methods for noisy label correction (e.g., MentorNet and Co-teaching).
COST: 4,000
PREDICTION: We expect to see a significant improvement over the baseline methods, with the active learning framework identifying the most informative instances for correction. However, the performance might degrade when the noise level is extremely high, as the active learning process might struggle to identify the correct instances to correct.

This proposal involves experimenting with a new approach to noisy label correction using active learning, and comparing it to existing state-of-the-art methods. We expect it to provide insights into how to effectively select instances for correction and how to improve the robustness of models trained on noisy data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Label Noise Distribution on Noisy Label Correction Methods
PROPOSAL: We'll investigate how different label noise distributions (e.g., class-conditional noise, instance-dependent noise, and mixtures of both) impact the performance of various noisy label correction methods. Specifically, we'll use the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets with added label noise to simulate different noise distributions. We'll compare the performance of state-of-the-art methods (e.g., MentorNet, Co-teaching) and also evaluate the robustness of these methods against out-of-distribution (OOD) noise distributions.
CONTROLS: We'll compare the performance of correction methods under different noise distributions and also evaluate their robustness against OOD noise distributions. The control experiment will be to compare the performance of correction methods when labels are perfectly clean.
COST: 12,000
PREDICTION: We expect to find that instance-dependent noise distributions pose a significant challenge to noisy label correction methods, and that adapting correction methods to specific noise distributions will be essential for achieving robust performance. However, the results may reveal that some correction methods are able to generalize across different noise distributions better than others.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Guided Noisy Label Filtering using Ensembled Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: We'll explore the use of ensembled neural networks to filter out noisy labels. Specifically, we'll train multiple neural networks on the same dataset, and then use their confidence scores to identify instances with high uncertainty. We'll filter out these instances and retrain the neural networks on the cleaned dataset. We'll evaluate the performance of this approach on multiple datasets with added label noise and compare it with vanilla training and existing noisy label filtering methods.
CONTROLS: The control experiments will include training on clean labels, training with no label filtering, and training with state-of-the-art noisy label filtering methods (e.g., MentorNet).
COST: 18,000
PREDICTION: We expect this approach to be effective in filtering out noisy labels, particularly in cases where the noise is instance-dependent. However, it may not perform well when the noise is class-conditional, and the confidence scores of the ensembled network may not accurately capture the uncertainty associated with the instances.

This proposal involves investigating an uncertainty-guided noisy label filtering method using ensembled neural networks. By leveraging the diversity of the ensembled networks, we expect to identify instances with high uncertainty and filter them out to improve the overall performance of the neural networks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semi-Supervised Learning with Noisy Labels using Variational Autoencoders
PROPOSAL: We'll propose a semi-supervised learning approach that utilizes Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to learn a latent representation of the data. The VAE will be trained on both labeled and unlabeled data, using a combination of supervised loss and reconstruction loss to encourage the model to capture both the class-prior and the underlying structure of the data. We'll then use the learned latent representation to denoise the labels and improve the performance of the model on the noisy labeled dataset.
CONTROLS: The control experiments will include training on clean labels, training with no semi-supervised learning, and training with existing semi-supervised learning methods (e.g., the mean teacher).
COST: 54,000
PREDICTION: We expect the semi-supervised approach to be effective in reducing the impact of label noise, especially in scenarios where a large amount of unlabeled data is available. However, the performance might degrade if the model is not able to capture the underlying structure of the data, or if the label noise is too severe.

TITLE: Learning to Correct Labels with Reinforcement Learning
PROPOSAL: We'll propose a reinforcement learning-based approach to learn a policy for correcting noisy labels. The policy will be represented as a neural network that takes in the instance features and outputs a correction probability for each label. We'll define a reward function that encourages the model to correct labels that are noisy and penalizes incorrect corrections. We'll train the policy using a combination of supervised learning and reinforcement learning, where the model learns to correct labels online and adapt to the changing data distribution.
CONTROLS: The control experiments will include training on clean labels, training with no label correction, and training with existing noisy label correction methods (e.g., MentorNet and Co-teaching).
COST: 81,000
PREDICTION: We expect the reinforcement learning approach to be effective in learning to correct labels, especially in scenarios where the label noise is changing and the model needs to adapt quickly. However, the performance might degrade if the reward function is not well-designed or if the model is not able to capture the underlying structure of the data.

PROPOSAL: We'll investigate how different label noise distributions (e.g., class-conditional noise, instance-dependent noise, and mixtures of both) impact the performance of various noisy label correction methods. Specifically, we'll use the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets with added label noise to simulate different noise distributions. We'll compare the performance of state-of-the-art methods (e.g., MentorNet, Co-teaching) and also evaluate the robustness of these methods against out-of-distribution (OOD) noise distributions.
CONTROLS: We'll compare the performance of correction methods under different noise distributions and also evaluate their robustness against OOD noise distributions. The control experiment will be to compare the performance of correction methods when labels are perfectly clean.
COST: 36,000
PREDICTION: We expect to find that instance-dependent noise distributions pose a significant challenge to noisy label correction methods, and that adapting correction methods to specific noise distributions will be essential for achieving robust performance. However, the results may reveal that some correction methods are able to generalize across different noise distributions better than others.

We'll filter out these instances and retrain the neural networks on the cleaned dataset. We'll evaluate the performance of this approach on multiple datasets with added label noise and compare it with vanilla training and existing noisy label filtering methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Active Learning-based Noise Correction for Instance-dependent Noisy Labels
PROPOSAL: We propose a model-agnostic noise correction method that actively selects samples for correction using a Bayesian neural network, where the noise level of each sample is modeled using a probabilistic output layer. The target is to minimize prediction loss on clean samples while ignoring noisy ones, incorporating the uncertainty inherent in the noisy predictor. We will select a fraction of samples to correct using the uncertainty and prediction loss as selectors. During training, we use a regime where labels are updated according to the correction proposal and a Monte Carlo type retraining of the model on the reweighted samples, accounting for the uncertainty about the corrected labels.
CONTROLS: We will control for baseline noise correction methods, including reweighting samples based on noise likelihoods and using a confidence-based sampler. For comparison, we will also implement a passive noise correction approach similar to the state of the art in the area that simply updates labels based on model predictions. Additionally, we will compare to a state-of-the-art dyamic sampling approach that updates labels and samples based on model predictions and loss during training. 
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: We expect the active learning-based noise correction approach to outperform the passive baseline by dynamically selecting the most useful samples for correction, and possibly even surpassing the state of the art through its ability to account for the model's uncertainty in its correction decisions. However, we may struggle with failure in highly imbalanced datasets where there is not enough clean data to learn from.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: CELO: Certifiably Learning from Noisy Data with Exploratory Boundary Smoothing
PROPOSAL: We introduce CELO, a novel noise correction method that integrates exploratory boundary smoothing with robust learning objectives to certify that the clean labels have been accurately recovered. Our method estimates the noise levels of the training data and computes a noisy-to-clean mapping using a smooth, piece-wise linear relationship. The goal is to find the optimal set of clean labels that minimize a robust loss function while remaining within a pre-defined margin. This is achieved by propagating the smoothness of the boundary through an iterative algorithm that uses self-concordance properties to find a sharp minimum. CELO can also be seen as a method for learning the reliability of noisy labels.
CONTROLS: We will compare the CELO method to several baseline methods, including a popular robust loss formulation called CORAL, as well as a label filtering approach that aggregates label estimates over local neighborhoods. For the second part of the evaluation, we will test CELO on a variety of models trained using different loss functions and on datasets with different levels of label noise.
COST: 14000
PREDICTION: We expect CELO to be particularly effective for instance-dependent noise where the noisy labels reflect a nuanced local relationship, and the boundary smoothing can effectively uncover the relationships governing the noisy labels. However, estimating the noise levels in CELO might be computationally expensive, making it lose out to more efficient methods such as our active learning-based approach.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Task Learning of Noise Maps and Prediction Models
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel multi-task learning framework that jointly trains a noise map predictor and a prediction model. The noise map predictor is designed to estimate the noise levels of each sample in the dataset, while the prediction model is tasked with learning a robust classifier. The two tasks are connected through a shared latent space, where the noise map predictor is learned using a regression objective and the prediction model is learned using a classification objective. This approach allows the model to adaptively select the most reliable data points for training, and to learn a more robust classifier that is less affected by noisy labels.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to several baseline methods that either ignore the noise levels (training a vanilla classifier) or rely on fixed noise levels estimates (reweighting samples based on noise likelihoods). Additionally, we will evaluate our approach on different datasets with varying levels of label noise and different noise types.
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: We expect our multi-task learning approach to outperform the baselines by learning more accurate noise maps and improving the robustness of the classifier. However, it may require careful tuning of the hyperparameters to balance the two tasks, and it may not generalize well to datasets with unseen noise distributions.

TITLE: Meta-Learning for Noise-Robust Models through Instance Distribution Mixture
PROPOSAL: We propose a meta-learning approach that learns to select the optimal mixture of instance distributions, where each distribution represents the data points of a specific class with a given level of noise. The model is trained on a set of task-specific datasets, each with a known noise distribution. During testing, the model selects the most suitable instance distribution mixture for the given test dataset and adaptively adjusts its prediction model accordingly. This approach allows the model to learn to handle varying levels of noise and improve its robustness.
CONTROLS: We will compare our meta-learning approach to several baseline methods, including a popular robust loss formulation called CORAL, as well as a label filtering approach that aggregates label estimates over local neighborhoods. For comparison, we will also implement a meta-learning approach without instance distribution mixture.
COST: 28659.2
PREDICTION: We expect our meta-learning approach to outperform the baselines by adaptively learning the optimal instance distribution mixture and adjusting the prediction model accordingly. However, estimating the instance distribution mixture might be computationally expensive, which could impact the scalability of the model.

PROPOSAL: We propose a method that uses conditional variational autoencoders (CVAEs) to track and correct noisy labels in a dataset. This approach allows the model to learn to handle varying levels of noise and improve its robustness.

TITLE: Meta-Label Learning with Score Calibration
PROPOSAL: We develop a meta-learning approach to discover a simple, unified scoring metric to calibrate label confidence across various tasks and datasets. TITLE: Pollution-based Sampling for Noisy Datasets
PROPOSAL: We introduce an efficient yet effective self-aware sampling method to identify and focus on the most impactful noisy samples in the training dataset. This approach models the dataset as a pollutant having adverse effects on model performance, aiming to maintain a delicate balance between accuracy and overfitting. Evaluation involves assessing the impact of our sampling method on the performance of Self-Analysis Augmented Label Correction, Meta-Label Learning with Score Calibration, and Meta-Learning to Discover Noise-Specific Dynamics.

PREDICTION: Our sampling method will offer a substantial improvement in accuracy and robustness for models trained on noisy datasets, particularly when combined with more efficient correction methods. However, effectively capturing the dominant noise patterns might be challenging for complex or multi-modal noise distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tri-Loss Minimization for Robust Learning from Noisy Labels with Instance-Dependent Noise
PROPOSAL: This experiment extends the classic cross-entropy loss by adding a novel tri-loss term, designed to mitigate the impact of instance-dependent noise on the model's ability to generalize to clean test data. By simultaneously minimizing the soft entropy loss over three components: (1) the true labels; (2) the noisy labels; and (3) an ensemble distribution learned by averaging predictions over multiple iterations with distinct weights for each noise regime, we effectively balance the model's preference for clean and noisy labels. Our tri-loss objective is then combined with industry-standard Adam optimizer.
CONTROLS: (1) The classic cross-entropy loss; (2) A variant that optimizes using solely the soft entropy loss component 1 (true labels)
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: Expected results: our proposed tri-loss minimization technique achieves higher accuracy on clean test data compared to both the control groups, demonstrating its effectiveness in better handling instance-dependent noise scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploration of instance-aware label cleaning through an ensemble learning framework
PROPOSAL: Develop a generic framework that employs multiple supervised and unsupervised noise models to identify potentially noisy instances in the training set. The framework will leverage different techniques, such as k-nearest neighbors and dimensionality exploration, to increase the accuracy of noise detection. This will empower the algorithm to learn from noisy data while reducing its impact. A further innovation will be the dynamic self-updating mechanism for identity and continuously reassessing noisy labels throughout the training process.
CONTROLS: We will examine the effectiveness of different individual components within the framework and, when reintroducing the confidence-weighted noise estimation algorithm, explore its power when used in connection with this new label cleaning strategy. PREDICTION: The adaptive ensemble approach for instance-aware label cleaning should demonstrate significant performance improvements on multiple noisy instances, although challenges may be encountered in higher-dimensional data due to the known dependence of nearest-neighbors-based variation methods on data point density.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Joint RGB-Event Representations for Dense Semantic Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose the EventBridge model, a novel architecture that jointly learns to predict high-frame-rate semantic maps from low-frame-rate RGB frames and asynchronous event streams. EventBridge combines a 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) for RGB features and a 1D ConvGRU for event features, using a learnable joint embedding space to fuse information from both modalities. We leverage the output of the 2D CNN to condition the ConvGRU, enabling it to effectively capture and propagate temporal context from past events into the RGB embedding space. The fused representation is then passed through a series of transposed convolutions to produce a dense semantic map at a target time within the perceptual gap. 
CONTROLS: We consider two strong baselines: (1) independent fusion, where the RGB and event features are separately processed and then concatenated before prediction; and (2) a classic video semantic segmentation model that relies on a dense, high-frame-rate RGB video stream as input. We also evaluate the impact of factorizing the joint embedding space into two separate latent spaces, one for each modality, and ablating the ConvGRU component to understand its role in effective event-RGB fusion.
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: EventBridge outperforms the baselines and factorized variant across various metrics, demonstrating the effectiveness of the joint RGB-event representation in predicting dense semantic maps. However, we expect challenges in handling highly dynamic scenes and long prediction intervals, where objects may move or become occluded after the last frame was captured.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-Conditioned Temporal Networks for Causal Dense Semantic Prediction
PROPOSAL: We propose Event-conditioned Temporal Networks (ETNs), a class of neural networks that leverage event information to condition the flow of temporal context in dense semantic prediction tasks. ETNs consist of a set of temporal convolutional layers, each of which is conditioned on the input event stream. This conditioning enables ETNs to selectively capture and propagate relevant temporal context from events into the prediction. By injecting causal information from events into the network's flow of temporal context, ETNs can make informed predictions for any arbitrary target time within the perceptual gap, satisfying the anytime prediction constraint. 
CONTROLS: We compare ETNs to a variant of EventBridge, where the 1D ConvGRU is replaced by a set of unconditioned temporal convolutional layers, demonstrating that event-conditioning is crucial for enforcing causality in the network's flow of temporal context. We also consider a naive concatenation of event features with RGB features, showing that ETNs outperform this baseline by effectively leveraging event information to guide the flow of temporal context.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: ETNs achieve state-of-the-art performance on the causal dense semantic prediction task, but may struggle with highly dynamic scenes and long prediction intervals where objects move rapidly or become occluded after the last frame was captured.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Impact of Sensor Noise and Artefacts in Asynchronous Event Streams
PROPOSAL: We investigate the impact of sensor noise and artefacts in asynchronous event streams on the performance of dense semantic prediction models. We introduce a new dataset, SynEv, which includes artificially introduced event noise and artefacts that mimic real-world scenarios. We then evaluate the robustness of two strong baselines: EventBridge and ETNs, to these distortions. Our results demonstrate that while both models are relatively robust to event noise, they are severely affected by artefacts, particularly those that alter event timing or spatial location. We identify key factors contributing to this sensitivity and propose several strategies for mitigating their impact, including event denoising, temporal event augmentation, and artefact-aware loss functions.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of EventBridge and ETNs on SynEv with and without artefacts, demonstrating the severity of artefact-induced degradations. We also evaluate the impact of artefacts on model interpretability, demonstrating a significant increase in model uncertainty and confidence under artefact-present conditions.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: By understanding and mitigating the impact of sensor noise and artefacts, dense semantic prediction models can achieve more robust performance in real-world scenarios, but may require significant training data and computational resources to adapt to new artefact patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Importance of Spatial Alignment for Event-RGB Fusion
PROPOSAL: We investigate the importance of spatial alignment between event and RGB information for effective fusion and dense semantic prediction. We propose a novel spatial alignment module that aligns the event stream with the RGB feature map in both spatial and temporal dimensions. Our spatial alignment approach leverages a set of spatial transformers to re-project the event stream to the optimal spatial location within the RGB feature map, while also adjusting the event timestamps to match the timing of the corresponding RGB frame. We demonstrate that spatial alignment significantly enhances the performance of EventBridge and ETNs, leading to more accurate and robust dense semantic predictions.
CONTROLS: We compare the impact of spatial alignment on EventBridge and ETNs, evaluating both methods with and without the spatial alignment module. We also investigate the effect of alignment errors on model performance, demonstrating that misaligned event-RGB fusion leads to significant degradations in model accuracy and robustness.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Our proposed spatial alignment module improves the performance of dense semantic prediction models, but may require significant computational resources to perform temporal adjustments and re-projections of the event stream.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Joint RGB-Event Representations for Dense Semantic Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose the EventBridge model, a novel architecture that jointly learns to predict high-frame-rate semantic maps from low-frame-rate RGB frames and asynchronous event streams. EventBridge combines a 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) for RGB features and a 1D ConvGRU for event features, using a learnable joint embedding space to fuse information from both modalities. We leverage the output of the 2D CNN to condition the ConvGRU, enabling it to effectively capture and propagate temporal context from past events into the RGB embedding space. The fused representation is then passed through a series of transposed convolutions to produce a dense semantic map at a target time within the perceptual gap. 
CONTROLS: We consider two strong baselines: (1) independent fusion, where the RGB and event features are separately processed and then concatenated before prediction; and (2) a classic video semantic segmentation model that relies on a dense, high-frame-rate RGB video stream as input. We also evaluate the impact of factorizing the joint embedding space into two separate latent spaces, one for each modality, and ablating the ConvGRU component to understand its role in effective event-RGB fusion.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: EventBridge outperforms the baselines and factorized variant across various metrics, demonstrating the effectiveness of the joint RGB-event representation in predicting dense semantic maps. However, we expect challenges in handling highly dynamic scenes and long prediction intervals, where objects may move or become occluded after the last frame was captured.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-Conditioned Temporal Networks for Causal Dense Semantic Prediction
PROPOSAL: We propose Event-conditioned Temporal Networks (ETNs), a class of neural networks that leverage event information to condition the flow of temporal context in dense semantic prediction tasks. ETNs consist of a set of temporal convolutional layers, each of which is conditioned on the input event stream. This conditioning enables ETNs to selectively capture and propagate relevant temporal context from events into the prediction. By injecting causal information from events into the network's flow of temporal context, ETNs can make informed predictions for any arbitrary target time within the perceptual gap, satisfying the anytime prediction constraint. 
CONTROLS: We compare ETNs to a variant of EventBridge, where the 1D ConvGRU is replaced by a set of unconditioned temporal convolutional layers, demonstrating that event-conditioning is crucial for enforcing causality in the network's flow of temporal context. We also consider a naive concatenation of event features with RGB features, showing that ETNs outperform this baseline by effectively leveraging event information to guide the flow of temporal context.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: ETNs achieve state-of-the-art performance on the causal dense semantic prediction task, but may struggle with highly dynamic scenes and long prediction intervals where objects move rapidly or become occluded after the last frame was captured.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Impact of Sensor Noise and Artefacts in Asynchronous Event Streams
PROPOSAL: We investigate the impact of sensor noise and artefacts in asynchronous event streams on the performance of dense semantic prediction models. We introduce a new dataset, SynEv, which includes artificially introduced event noise and artefacts that mimic real-world scenarios. We then evaluate the robustness of two strong baselines: EventBridge and ETNs, to these distortions. Our results demonstrate that while both models are relatively robust to event noise, they are severely affected by artefacts, particularly those that alter event timing or spatial location. We identify key factors contributing to this sensitivity and propose several strategies for mitigating their impact, including event denoising, temporal event augmentation, and artefact-aware loss functions.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of EventBridge and ETNs on SynEv with and without artefacts, demonstrating the severity of artefact-induced degradations. We also evaluate the impact of artefacts on model interpretability, demonstrating a significant increase in model uncertainty and confidence under artefact-present conditions.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: By understanding and mitigating the impact of sensor noise and artefacts, dense semantic prediction models can achieve more robust performance in real-world scenarios, but may require significant training data and computational resources to adapt to new artefact patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Importance of Spatial Alignment for Event-RGB Fusion
PROPOSAL: We investigate the importance of spatial alignment between event and RGB information for effective fusion and dense semantic prediction. We propose a novel spatial alignment module that aligns the event stream with the RGB feature map in both spatial and temporal dimensions. Our spatial alignment approach leverages a set of spatial transformers to re-project the event stream to the optimal spatial location within the RGB feature map, while also adjusting the event timestamps to match the timing of the corresponding RGB frame. We demonstrate that spatial alignment significantly enhances the performance of EventBridge and ETNs, leading to more accurate and robust dense semantic predictions.
CONTROLS: We compare the impact of spatial alignment on EventBridge and ETNs, evaluating both methods with and without the spatial alignment module. We also investigate the effect of alignment errors on model performance, demonstrating that misaligned event-RGB fusion leads to significant degradations in model accuracy and robustness.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: Our proposed spatial alignment module improves the performance of dense semantic prediction models, but may require significant computational resources to perform temporal adjustments and re-projections of the event stream.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating the Importance of Spatial Alignment for Event-RGB Fusion
PROPOSAL: We REVISE this proposal to integrate the spatial alignment module directly into the 2D CNN used in EventBridge and ETNs, rather than treating it as a separate module. This approach allows the spatial alignment to be performed in a more effective and efficient manner, leveraging the learned spatial representations of the event stream within the 2D CNN. We demonstrate that integrating spatial alignment into the 2D CNN significantly enhances the performance of EventBridge and ETNs, leading to more accurate and robust dense semantic predictions.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of EventBridge and ETNs with and without the integrated spatial alignment module, evaluating the impact of alignment on model accuracy and robustness. We also investigate the effect of alignment errors on model performance, demonstrating that misaligned event-RGB fusion leads to significant degradations in model accuracy and robustness.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: Our revised approach improves the performance of EventBridge and ETNs, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to effectively integrate spatial alignment within the 2D CNN.

PREDICTION: Our attention mechanism significantly improves the performance of EventBridge in highly dynamic scenes, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to effectively focus on the most predictive event streams and RGB features.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dense-Sparse Fusion Network for High-Frame-Rate Semantic Perception
PROPOSAL: We develop a novel Dense-Sparse Fusion Network (DSFN) that effectively integrates RGB and event streams. Our method consists of two main components: a 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) that processes RGB features at a fine spatial resolution and high temporal resolution, and a dilated spatial-temporal graph CNN that aggregates event features at a coarse spatial resolution and microsecond-scale temporal resolution. The two sub-networks are jointly trained to predict dense semantic maps at arbitrary timestamps. We leverage self-attention mechanisms to explore both spatial and temporal dependencies across the fused features. The model is optimized using a combination of classification loss and a novel temporal uncertainty loss, which jointly minimizes classification errors and encourages the model to be confident in its predictions.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach with state-of-the-art RGB and event capturing variants, including Temporal Ensembling (TE), RGB-E occurrence count (REOC), and Video Semantic Segmentation (VSS).
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: DSFN is expected to demonstrate significant improvements over existing state-of-the-art approaches, achieving state-of-the-art performance on all autonomous driving navigation evaluation metrics (e.g. Mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), mean Average Precision (mAP)) when tested with various RGB and event streams. Its ability to handle complex dynamic scenes and wide prediction intervals might also yield competitive performance, albeit with a higher risk of degradation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sampled RGB-Event Factorization for Efficient High-Frame-Rate Perception
PROPOSAL: To mitigate the high computational cost associated with densely processing RGB and event streams, we propose a novel Sampled RGB-Event Factorization (SREF) approach. SREF employs dimensionality reduction techniques, such as PCA or autoencoders, to effectively capture the most informative features of the RGB and event streams without loss of semantic information. We Then, only a subset of the data features are fed into a fusion network, similar to DSFN, while the discarded features are explicitly incorporated into the network's spatial-temporal graph architecture. This two-step factorization process results in efficient, high-resolution prediction maps at arbitrary timestamps. Experiments are conducted to validate the efficiency of SREF in large-scale real-world systems.
CONTROLS: We compare SREF against DSFN, without dimensionality reduction, as well as against other sparse compression methods.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: SREF is expected to achieve state-of-the-art inference speed while maintaining the accuracy of DSFN, thus allowing it to be applied in scenarios with resource constraints and high computational demands. However, SREF performance may slightly degrade in highly dynamic scenarios due to the loss of spatial details.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anytime RGB-Event Fusion with Uncertainty Estimation
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel approach for anytime RGB-event fusion with uncertainty estimation, which is essential for reliable and causal high-frame-rate semantic perception. Our method employs a Bayesian neural network architecture to model the uncertainty of the predictions at each timestamp, enabling the estimation of confidence in the predicted semantic maps. We incorporate event data using a dilated spatial-temporal graph convolutional neural network (ST-GCN) that captures the complex dynamics of events and fuses with RGB features through Bayesian fusion. This enables the model to make confident predictions at any arbitrary timestamp.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against DSFN and SREF, focusing on the accuracy of uncertainty estimates at different prediction timestamps and use latency-latency product as the key evaluation metric.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: The proposed approach is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance in terms of uncertainty estimation and anytime perception, owing to its ability to model uncertainty and provide more confident predictions. However, the use of Bayesian neural networks may introduce additional computational cost and memory requirements.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Modal Fusion with EventPTR and RGB 3DConv
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach for multi-modal fusion of RGB and event data, leveraging the principles of both the Sampled RGB-Event Factorization (SREF) and the Temporal Attention Module (TAM) of DSFN. Our model incorporates the EventPTR (Event Propagation and Transformation Regression) approach to focus on the most relevant events and the 3D convolutional layer for RGB data, to capture contextual information. This enables the model to process both modalities efficiently and leverage their complementary strengths in high-frame-rate semantic perception.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against DSFN without TAM, SREF, and other state-of-the-art RGB-event fusion methods, focusing on the trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, and the degree of captured contextual information.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: The proposed approach is expected to strike a balance between DSFN's strong performance and SREF's efficiency, thus outperforming both while being more practical for real-world deployment. However, its performance may degrade in highly dynamic environments where both RGB and event modalities struggle to accurately capture scene information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Temporal Coherence for Efficient Anytime RGB-Event Fusion
PROPOSAL: To further enhance the efficiency and accuracy of anytime RGB-event fusion, we introduce a novel hierarchical temporal coherence approach. This method employs a hierarchical graph neural network (H-GNN) to capture coarse-to-fine temporal relationships between event sequences, while iteratively refining the RGB event fusion process using a temporal attention mechanism. By leveraging the hierarchical temporal coherence, we enable the model to propagates contextual information between event sequences, resulting in more accurate predictions at arbitrary timestamps.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against the revised DSFN with TAM, any of the previous models, and other state-of-the-art RGB-event fusion methods, focusing on the trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, and spatial contextual information captured.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: The proposed approach is expected to showcase strong performance in both static and dynamic scenes, thanks to the effective capture of hierarchical temporal relationships and efficient fusion of RGB and event modalities. However, the risk of overfitting to the hierarchical graph structure might arise, potentially increasing model size and computation time.

TITLE: Online RGB-Event Fusion for High-Frame-Rate Autonomous Driving
PROPOSAL: We propose an online RGB-event fusion approach for high-frame-rate semantic perception in autonomous driving. Our method leverages a lightweight neural network that processes RGB and event streams in real-time, using both static and dynamic information extracted from the input streams. By always predicting the most recent and accurate semantic label, our model ensures consistency with the autonomous system's state and decisions. This is crucial in a real-world setting, where stability and responsiveness are critical for safe and reliable operation.
CONTROLS: We compare our online approach against the previously developed hierarchical models, including the revised DSFN and hierarchical temporal coherence-based fusion, and conducting experiments on real-world datasets for autonomous driving.

PREDICTION: The proposed online approach is expected to achieve high accuracy and robustness, ensuring reliable operation in real-world environments, particularly when rapid scene changes occur. However, challenges related to efficiency, stability, and deliberation during online updates and estimation might impact its performance.

Experiments are conducted to validate the efficiency of SREF in large-scale real-world systems.
CONTROLS: We compare SREF against DSFN, without dimensionality reduction, as well as against other sparse compression methods.
COST: 16200
PREDICTION: SREF is expected to achieve state-of-the-art inference speed while maintaining the accuracy of DSFN, thus allowing it to be applied in scenarios with resource constraints and high computational demands. However, SREF performance may slightly degrade in highly dynamic scenarios due to the loss of spatial details.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Dense-Sparse Fusion Network for High-Frame-Rate Semantic Perception
PROPOSAL: We revise the Dense-Sparse Fusion Network (DSFN) to adaptively select relevant temporal information from the event stream based on the RGB frame's semantic context, thus further enhancing the fusion process between RGB and event features. In particular, we employ a Temporal Attention Module (TAM) to iteratively refine the selection of event information, weighted by the likelihood of the RGB frame's semantic entities appearing in the future event stream. By capturing the relevance of the event information to the current RGB frame, we enable DSFN to better handle highly dynamic scenes and utilize the event stream more effectively.
CONTROLS: We compare the revised DSFN against the original DSFN and other attention-based fusion methods, including channel-wise attention and graph-based attention, with varying weights applied to event and RGB features.
COST: 16200
PREDICTION: The revised DSFN is expected to exhibit improved performance, especially in scenarios with complex temporal dynamics, such as multiple moving objects or fast-changing lighting conditions. However, there is a risk that the TAM might introduce additional computation and slow down the model, potentially offsetting the overall performance improvement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anytime RGB-Event Fusion with Uncertainty Estimation
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel approach for anytime RGB-event fusion with uncertainty estimation, which is essential for reliable and causal high-frame-rate semantic perception. Our method employs a Bayesian neural network architecture to model the uncertainty of the predictions at each timestamp, enabling the estimation of confidence in the predicted semantic maps. We incorporate event data using a dilated spatial-temporal graph convolutional neural network (ST-GCN) that captures the complex dynamics of events and fuses with RGB features through Bayesian fusion. This enables the model to make confident predictions at any arbitrary timestamp.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against DSFN and SREF, focusing on the accuracy of uncertainty estimates at different prediction timestamps and use latency-latency product as the key evaluation metric.
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: The proposed approach is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance in terms of uncertainty estimation and anytime perception, owing to its ability to model uncertainty and provide more confident predictions. However, the use of Bayesian neural networks may introduce additional computational cost and memory requirements.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Modal Fusion with EventPTR and RGB 3DConv
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach for multi-modal fusion of RGB and event data, leveraging the principles of both the Sampled RGB-Event Factorization (SREF) and the Temporal Attention Module (TAM) of DSFN. Our model incorporates the EventPTR (Event Propagation and Transformation Regression) approach to focus on the most relevant events and the 3D convolutional layer for RGB data, to capture contextual information. This enables the model to process both modalities efficiently and leverage their complementary strengths in high-frame-rate semantic perception.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against DSFN without TAM, SREF, and other state-of-the-art RGB-event fusion methods, focusing on the trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, and the degree of captured contextual information.
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: The proposed approach is expected to strike a balance between DSFN's strong performance and SREF's efficiency, thus outperforming both while being more practical for real-world deployment. However, its performance may degrade in highly dynamic environments where both RGB and event modalities struggle to accurately capture scene information.

TITLE: Hierarchical Temporal Coherence for Efficient Anytime RGB-Event Fusion
PROPOSAL: To further enhance the efficiency and accuracy of anytime RGB-event fusion, we introduce a novel hierarchical temporal coherence approach. This method employs a hierarchical graph neural network (H-GNN) to capture coarse-to-fine temporal relationships between event sequences, while iteratively refining the RGB event fusion process using a temporal attention mechanism. By leveraging the hierarchical temporal coherence, we enable the model to propagates contextual information between event sequences, resulting in more accurate predictions at arbitrary timestamps.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against the revised DSFN with TAM, any of the previous models, and other state-of-the-art RGB-event fusion methods, focusing on the trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, and spatial contextual information captured.
COST: 32400
PREDICTION: The proposed approach is expected to showcase strong performance in both static and dynamic scenes, thanks to the effective capture of hierarchical temporal relationships and efficient fusion of RGB and event modalities. However, the risk of overfitting to the hierarchical graph structure might arise, potentially increasing model size and computation time.
