TITLE: Temporal Pyramid Pooling with RGB-Event Fusion for High-Frame-Rate Scene Understanding
PROPOSAL: To address the challenges of high-frame-rate semantic perception in dynamic scenes, we propose a novel Temporal Pyramid Pooling (TPP) approach combined with RGB-event fusion. Through the TPP, we capture a hierarchy of event features from different temporal resolutions, effectively fusing the RGB and event modalities at multiple temporal scales. The resulting pyramid feature representation enables the model to efficiently capture contextual information and accurately predict semantic labels at arbitrary timestamps.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against hierarchical models including the revised DSFN and hierarchical temporal coherence-based fusion, focusing on the balance between accuracy and efficiency.
COST: 37800
PREDICTION: The proposed approach is expected to exhibit strong performance, providing a good balance between accuracy and efficiency in dynamic scenes, with the ability to handle complex temporal sequences and underlying event dynamics. However, potential overfitting to the pyramid structure might result in computationally expensive operations.

TITLE: Online RGB-Event Fusion for High-Frame-Rate Autonomous Driving
PROPOSAL: We propose an online RGB-event fusion approach for high-frame-rate semantic perception in autonomous driving. Our method leverages a lightweight neural network that processes RGB and event streams in real-time, using both static and dynamic information extracted from the input streams. By always predicting the most recent and accurate semantic label, our model ensures consistency with the autonomous system's state and decisions. This is crucial in a real-world setting, where stability and responsiveness are critical for safe and reliable operation.
CONTROLS: We compare our online approach against the previously developed hierarchical models, including the revised DSFN and hierarchical temporal coherence-based fusion, and conducting experiments on real-world datasets for autonomous driving.
COST: 43200
PREDICTION: The proposed online approach is expected to achieve high accuracy and robustness, ensuring reliable operation in real-world environments, particularly when rapid scene changes occur. However, challenges related to efficiency, stability, and deliberation during online updates and estimation might impact its performance.

PROPOSAL: We conduct an extensive evaluation of the previously developed models in real-world autonomous applications, specifically focusing on autonomous driving, drone navigation, and quadruped robot navigation. We assess their performance in diverse scenarios, including complex urban environments, dynamic weather conditions, and varying lighting levels. Through our evaluation, we identify the strengths and limitations of each approach and demonstrate their practical applicability in real-world scenarios.
CONTROLS: We perform an extensive comparison of the models on a combination of real-world datasets and autonomous driving benchmarks, including the nuScenes dataset and the ApolloScape dataset.
COST: 50400
PREDICTION: The proposed evaluation is expected to provide valuable insights into the limitations and potential of each approach, enabling the development of high-frame-rate semantic perception systems for real-world autonomous applications. However, the inherent complexity of real-world scenarios may lead to variable performance, and identifying the optimal balance between accuracy, efficiency, and reliability will remain a significant challenge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: RGB-Event Fusion via Temporal Graph Neural Network (TGNN)
PROPOSAL: This experiment investigates a hybrid approach to fusing RGB and event data using a Temporal Graph Neural Network (TGNN). The TGNN architecture will learn to integrate the static RGB features with the dynamic event stream to generate a high-frame-rate semantic map. The model will first process the RGB frame to obtain a static semantic map. Simultaneously, it will process the event stream to obtain a dynamic graph, where nodes represent pixels and edges encode temporal relationships between pixels. The TGNN will then recursively aggregate information from the graph to produce a dense, temporally-consistent semantic map at any target time.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Greedy RGB-Event Fusion using MC Dropout, Baseline 2: Video Semantic Segmentation (VSS) with RGB-only input
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: The TGNN approach should achieve state-of-the-art results, especially in highly dynamic scenes, with a potential improvement of 5-8% IoU over the baseline methods. However, it may fail to handle very long prediction intervals or very sparse event streams.

TITLE: Semi-Supervised Learning for Event Camera Segmentation
PROPOSAL: This experiment explores the use of semi-supervised learning (SSL) to increase the effectiveness of event camera segmentation, where high-quality labeled data is often scarce. We will implement a model that learns to use both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the segmentation accuracy and robustness. The model will be fine-tuned using a small set of labeled frames and a large set of unlabeled frames, while leveraging the spatial and temporal coherence information in the event streams.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: supervised learning with a large set of labeled frames, Baseline 2: RGB-only segmentation using a state-of-the-art segmentation model
COST: 11650
PREDICTION: The SSL approach should improve the segmentation accuracy by 2-5% IOU compared to the supervised learning baseline, especially in scenarios with limited labeled data. However, its effectiveness may degrade in highly dynamic scenes or when the event stream is too noisy.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: FusionNet: A Temporal Fusion Framework for Event-Camera and RGB-Input Dense Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: Develop FusionNet, a neural network architecture that takes an initial RGB frame $I_t$ and the corresponding event stream $\mathcal{E}_{t-\Delta t \to t+\delta t}$ as input, and outputs a dense semantic map for any target time $t+\delta t$ within the blind interval $(t, t+\Delta t]$. FusionNet will leverage self-attention and cross-modal fusion to integrate the static RGB context and the temporally dense event stream.
CONTROLS: Train and test FusionNet on the Carla Autonomous Driving Simulator dataset, with ground truth semantic maps for dense objects and scene context; compare with ablation studies replacing RGB input with event stream, or RGB with a future frame from the RGB video stream; also compare with the performance of current state-of-the-art RGB-video and event-camera semantic segmentation approaches.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: FusionNet will show promise in reliably estimating dense semantic maps at any moment in time, but difficulties may arise in handling complex and dynamic scenes with frequent occlusions and camera motion. 

PRIV side note: this probably should be implemented in PyTorch given all the similar works

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-Frame Attention for Dense Semantic Prediction within Temporal Gaps
PROPOSAL: Design an event-frame attention mechanism that selectively focuses on relevant events and RGB pixels within the current frame, weighted by their importance in predicting semantic labels at a target time $t+\delta t$ within the blind interval. This mechanism will be used as a module within FusionNet to enable more accurate dense semantic segmentation. The attention mechanism will learn to weigh events and pixels based on their temporal proximity, spatial relevance, and semantic coherence.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the attention module in isolation by comparing its performance with and without a naive event-selection strategy (e.g., random or fixed number of events), as well as with and without integrating semantic coherence information derived from the RGB context.
COST: 1165
PREDICTION: The event-frame attention mechanism will significantly improve dense semantic segmentation accuracy by filtering out irrelevant events and pixels, but may struggle to handle extremely long or dynamic blind intervals. 

PRIV note: to compute this attention, this would way better implemented on some newer specialized accelerators for sparse neural networks like Graphcore or specialist tensorcore accelerators.  important to read many many articles.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: REVISED FusionNet: A Temporal Fusion Framework for Event-Camera and RGB-Input Dense Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: REVISED FusionNet will leverage a two-stage architecture, with the first stage focusing on detecting moving and occluded objects in the event stream, and the second stage using the combined event and RGB features to produce a dense semantic map. This decoupling will allow for more efficient handling of complex scenes and reduce the risk of over-smoothing in the presence of rapid motion or occlusions.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the impact of this two-stage approach by comparing it with a one-stage architecture, as well as with a variant of the one-stage architecture with an added occlusion-aware module. Compare both variants with state-of-the-art RGB-video and event-camera semantic segmentation approaches on autonomous driving datasets (e.g., Cityscapes and KITTI).
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: The two-stage architecture of REVISED FusionNet will improve performance in complex scenes by identifying and isolating moving objects, and will be more robust to occlusions and rapid motion. However, it may require more compute resources and may be more prone to overfitting if not properly regularized.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: FusionNet: A Temporal Fusion Framework for Event-Camera and RGB-Input Dense Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: Develop FusionNet, a neural network architecture that takes an initial RGB frame $I_t$ and the corresponding event stream $\mathcal{E}_{t-\Delta t \to t+\delta t}$ as input, and outputs a dense semantic map for any target time $t+\delta t$ within the blind interval $(t, t+\Delta t]$. FusionNet will leverage self-attention and cross-modal fusion to integrate the static RGB context and the temporally dense event stream.
CONTROLS: Train and test FusionNet on the Carla Autonomous Driving Simulator dataset, with ground truth semantic maps for dense objects and scene context; compare with ablation studies replacing RGB input with event stream, or RGB with a future frame from the RGB video stream; also compare with the performance of current state-of-the-art RGB-video and event-camera semantic segmentation approaches.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: FusionNet will show promise in reliably estimating dense semantic maps at any moment in time, but difficulties may arise in handling complex and dynamic scenes with frequent occlusions and camera motion. 

PRIV side note: this probably should be implemented in PyTorch given all the similar works

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-Frame Attention for Dense Semantic Prediction within Temporal Gaps
PROPOSAL: Design an event-frame attention mechanism that selectively focuses on relevant events and RGB pixels within the current frame, weighted by their importance in predicting semantic labels at a target time $t+\delta t$ within the blind interval. This mechanism will be used as a module within FusionNet to enable more accurate dense semantic segmentation. The attention mechanism will learn to weigh events and pixels based on their temporal proximity, spatial relevance, and semantic coherence.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the attention module in isolation by comparing its performance with and without a naive event-selection strategy (e.g., random or fixed number of events), as well as with and without integrating semantic coherence information derived from the RGB context.
COST: 3500
PREDICTION: The event-frame attention mechanism will significantly improve dense semantic segmentation accuracy by filtering out irrelevant events and pixels, but may struggle to handle extremely long or dynamic blind intervals. 

PRIV note: to compute this attention, this would way better implemented on some newer specialized accelerators for sparse neural networks like Graphcore or specialist tensorcore accelerators.  important to read many many articles.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED FusionNet: A Temporal Fusion Framework for Event-Camera and RGB-Input Dense Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: REVISIED FusionNet will incorporate the event-frame attention mechanism as a key module to selectively focus on relevant events and RGB pixels. In addition, we will use a combination of attention and dense connection modules, inspired by ConvLSTM, to better capture temporal dependencies between pixels and events, and fuse the multi-modal features in a more effective way. This will enable FusionNet to better handle complex and dynamic scenes, and improve overall dense semantic segmentation accuracy.
CONTROLS: Compare the revised FusionNet with original FusionNet, and both with state-of-the-art RGB-video and event-camera semantic segmentation approaches on the publicly availableKITTI and Cityscapes datasets. Investigate the effectiveness of the revised architecture in reducing the impact of occlusion and motion noise.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: The revised FusionNet will achieve state-of-the-art performance in dense semantic segmentation, but may still struggle in certain scenarios with extreme occlusions or rapid object movements.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: REVISED FusionNet: A Temporal Fusion Framework for Event-Camera and RGB-Input Dense Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: REVISED FusionNet will leverage a two-stage architecture, with the first stage focusing on detecting moving and occluded objects in the event stream, and the second stage using the combined event and RGB features to produce a dense semantic map. This decoupling will allow for more efficient handling of complex scenes and reduce the risk of over-smoothing in the presence of rapid motion or occlusions.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the impact of this two-stage approach by comparing it with a one-stage architecture, as well as with a variant of the one-stage architecture with an added occlusion-aware module. Compare both variants with state-of-the-art RGB-video and event-camera semantic segmentation approaches on autonomous driving datasets (e.g., Cityscapes and KITTI).
COST: 4200
PREDICTION: The two-stage architecture of REVISED FusionNet will improve performance in complex scenes by identifying and isolating moving objects, and will be more robust to occlusions and rapid motion. However, it may require more compute resources and may be more prone to overfitting if not properly regularized.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-Supervised Motion Learning for Event-Camera Scene Understanding
PROPOSAL: Develop a self-supervised learning framework to learn motion-aware features from event-camera data without explicit ground truth or temporal annotations. The framework will leverage the inherent motion information encoded in event sequences to learn a set of motion-aware feature extractors, which will be incorporated into REVISED FusionNet to enhance its ability to handle dynamic scenes.
CONTROLS: Train the self-supervised motion learning framework on a dataset of natural event-camera data and evaluate its performance on tasks such as event-camera motion segmentation and object correspondence between two consecutive event frames. Integrate the learned motion-aware features into REVISED FusionNet and evaluate its performance on dense semantic segmentation tasks.
COST: 5200
PREDICTION: The self-supervised motion learning framework will learn robust motion-aware features that will improve the performance of REVISED FusionNet in dynamic scenes, but may require a large number of training samples and may not generalize well to novel scenes.

ACTION: ADD

The metrics will be designed to address the unique challenges of these tasks, including the need to balance short-term accuracy with long-term temporal coherence.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the proposed metrics on existing dense semantic segmentation datasets extended with temporal annotations, and compare their performance with existing metrics for semantic segmentation tasks (e.g., Intersection-over-Union, mean-IoU). Use the proposed metrics to evaluate REVISED FusionNet and other state-of-the-art models on temporally-dependent dense semantic segmentation tasks.
COST: 6200
PREDICTION: The proposed evaluation metrics will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the performance of REVISED FusionNet and other models on temporally-dependent dense semantic segmentation tasks, but may require additional computational resources and may be challenging to interpret and explain.

PROPOSAL: Implement a 3D generation model that incorporates pre-trained 2D models (e.g. CLIP-viT) to enrich its semantics-aware reasoning. Train this 2D-informed 3D model on a dataset of 3D models, augmenting each model with their source images. PREDICTION: The 2D-informed 3D model should generate better identity-preserving results than the baseline, and could fail if the selected pre-trained 2D model lacks necessary information about the subject's appearance.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Self-Modal Learning: Mixing Generative and Discriminative Objectives for Identity Preservation
PROPOSAL: Propose a self-modal learning framework where the 3D generation model is both a generator that produces asset views, and a discriminator that distinguishes its generated views from real ones given new input viewpoints. The primary objective will be to encourage identity preservation, with a secondary objective that encourages contour realism (the ability to draw continuity and transitions of contours even in contact ambiguity, where parts where vibrating s-curve motion and interaction change significantly). The mixed objectives will be enforced through a balanced loss function.
CONTROLS: Run the framework without the secondary objective of contour realism as a baseline; train a basic discriminator-only network and use a fixed 3D generation model for comparison.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: The proposed framework should improve identity preservation, and contour realism is also likely to follow. It might fail in cases when the object's contour structure and the model's generated patterns strongly conflict, making both realism and fidelity difficult to maintain under objective balancing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semantic Consistency Loss for Personalized 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Modify a 3D autoencoder architecture to incorporate a semantic consistency loss function. This loss function compares the features of the synthetically generated 3D asset to those of the reference image, and encourages the generated asset to maintain similar geometric and feature structure. The goal is to address the hallucination issue in current 3D generation methods that often fail to maintain semantic identity across viewpoints. Use the STisEqual dataset, which allows for subject-driven 3D generation with specified geometric classes and semantic features.
CONTROLS: compare against a standard autoencoder model, and a model with randomized semantic consistency weights
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Expected to improve the geometry and feature structure of generated 3D assets, leading to more realistic and personalized results. However, the effectiveness of the method may depend on the initial quality of the autoencoder architecture and the reference image features used. If the semantic features are dissimilar between the reference image and the generated asset, the loss function may not effectively regularize the model.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Refining 3D/4D Generation with Pose-Aware Initialization
PROPOSAL: We propose a new 3D/4D generation framework that initializes the generation process with a pose-aware prior, learned from a diverse set of 3D/4D assets with corresponding 2D pose labels. This prior is used to condition the generation of a set of multi-viewimages, which are then used to train a subject-driven 3D/4D generation model. We will test this approach on the DeepTexture and Text2Shape datasets, using the PSNR and SSIM metrics to evaluate the generated 3D/4D assets.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to a baseline that uses a fixed initialization (e.g., a standard affine transformation) and to an ablation study that removes the pose-aware prior.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Our refined 3D/4D generation approach will improve the quality of the generated assets, especially in cases where the input image/video does not provide sufficient information about the subject's pose. However, we may struggle to achieve similar results in scenarios with highly varied or inconsistent pose information.

TITLE: Learning a Subject-Specific Universal Appearance Space
PROPOSAL: We propose to learn a subject-specific universal appearance space (SS-UAS) that encodes the common features of a subject's appearance across different viewpoints. This is achieved by training a variational autoencoder (VAE) on a set of 2D images of the subject from different viewpoints, and then using the learned VAE to initialize the 3D/4D generation process. We will evaluate this approach on the LS3DV and ADE20k datasets.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to a baseline that uses a random initialization for the 3D/4D generation process and to an ablation study that removes the SS-UAS.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Our SS-UAS will improve the consistency of the generated 3D/4D assets across different viewpoints, but may struggle to capture the unique, highly variable features of certain subjects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diffusion-Augmented View-Invariant Representations
PROPOSAL: We explore a modified diffusion model that incorporates a view-invariant representation via a novel token-based mechanism, enabling preservation of semantic identity across viewpoints. Specifically, we introduce an additional token, VIT (View-Invariant Token), which is optimized to encode the underlying identity of the subject, regardless of the observed viewpoint. This token is then incorporated into the diffusion model's transformer architecture, allowing the model to learn a shared, view-invariant representation of the subject's identity. We evaluate this approach on synthetic datasets for 3D and 4D generation tasks.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to several state-of-the-art methods in 3D and 4D generation, including a baseline diffusion model without the VIT token, as well as image-to-image translation methods with personalized 2D models.
COST: 3,360 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvements in identity preservation across viewpoints, with the VIT token incorporating valuable information about the subject's underlying identity. However, we anticipate that this approach may struggle to generalize to more complex scenarios with varying lighting, pose, and occlusions, potentially leading to reduced quality in some cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Self-Supervised ViewPoint-Awareness via Cycle Consistency
PROPOSAL: We introduce a self-supervised approach to improve viewpoint awareness in 3D and 4D generation models. Specifically, we propose a cycle consistency loss that encourages the model to preserve the subject's identity across multiple viewpoints. We construct synthetic datasets where images of the subject are taken from different viewpoints and then rendered from the same viewpoint but with varying poses and occlusions. Our approach is a modification of traditional unsupervised image-to-image translation, where instead of directly translating between views, we use a cycle consistency loss to optimize the feature representation of the subject across all views. We evaluate this method on both synthetic and semi-synthetic datasets for 3D and 4D generation tasks.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to both the baseline diffusion model from our previous experiment (1) and a state-of-the-art 3D generation method using a single image or video as input.
COST: 6,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see substantial improvements in view-awareness capabilities, enabling our model to better handle novel viewpoints and occlusions. However, we anticipate that the lack of explicit control over appearance may lead to over-smoothing or averaging of the subject's features in some cases, resulting in reduced quality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Multi-View Guided 3D Generation with Style Transfer
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with a novel multi-view guided 3D generation approach, combining 3D reconstruction techniques with style transfer. Given a single image of the subject, we first perform 3D reconstruction using a state-of-the-art model (e.g., Pix2Vox2). Subsequently, we apply a style transfer mechanism to transform the reconstructed 3D model to match the style of the input image, our reference subject.
CONTROLS: Compare with Pix2Vox2 alone, ablation study of the style transfer module, and style transfer using a 2D image-to-image translation model (e.g., U-Net)
COST: 400
PREDICTION: With the addition of style transfer, our approach should achieve better identity preservation and consistency across views, offering promising results in personalized 3D generation. However, the style transfer process might lead to information loss in the 3D reconstruction step, potentially degrading the overall quality of the generated asset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalized 3D Generation with Object-Specific Embeddings
PROPOSAL: To improve identity preservation, we incorporate object-specific embeddings into our 3D generation framework. We train a set of embeddings, each representing a specific object or subject, and condition our 3D model (e.g., Pix2Vox2) to utilize these embeddings. When generating a new 3D asset, we leverage the learned embedding to fine-tune the model's output and better capture the subject's identity.
CONTROLS: Compare with Pix2Vox2 alone and ablation study of the object-specific embeddings
COST: 600
PREDICTION: By incorporating object-specific embeddings, our method should be able to better preserve the subject's identity across viewpoints and demonstrate promising results in personalized 3D generation. However, the embedding learning process might introduce additional computational overhead, and the sheer size of the embeddings could negatively impact model performance in terms of both quality and efficiency.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Analyzing the Information Loss in Multi-View Style Transfer
PROPOSAL: We investigate the information loss that occurs during the style transfer process in our multi-view guided 3D generation approach. To identify the key factors contributing to this loss, we conduct an in-depth analysis of the style transfer mechanism, comparing its performance with different input image sizes and styles. Additionally, we explore strategies to alleviate the information loss, such as fine-tuning the style transfer neural network with a synthetic dataset of aligned images and 3D models.
CONTROLS: Compare with different style transfer architectures (e.g., CycleGAN, Conditional-StyleGAN) and analyze the impact of varying image resolutions on style transfer performance
COST: 830
PREDICTION: The analysis should provide valuable insights into the limitations of our current multi-view style transfer approach, enabling the design of more robust and efficient style transfer mechanisms. However, the optimization process for alleviating information loss might be computationally expensive and require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unsupervised Personalized 4D Generation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Learning
PROPOSAL: We introduce an unsupervised approach to personalized 4D generation based on cycle-consistent adversarial learning. By leveraging unpaired datasets and a set of adversarial cycles, we enable the model to learn the mapping between a single input video and an extended range of viewpoints, preserving the subject's motion and appearance across frames.
CONTROLS: Compare with state-of-the-art 4D generation models (e.g., Video-to-Video TransGAN) and ablation study of the cycle-consistent adversarial learning mechanism
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Our unsupervised approach should offer a scalable and efficient solution for personalized 4D generation, capable of leveraging large unpaired datasets and a wide range of subjects. However, it may require careful tuning of the adversarial cycles and may struggle with capturing subtle motions or small changes in appearance that are not well-represented in the unpaired dataset.

PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of a horizontal cascade of on-the-fly self-speculative approaches, such as Lookahead decoding and SWIFT, stacked with a retrieval-based statistical drafter, against standard speculative decoding on several real-world benchmarks, including multi-turn conversation and machine translation.
CONTROLS: Standard speculative decoding with no pre-trained draft model, retrieval-based statistical drafting alone, a baseline of beam search for comparison
COST: 450

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE:  Evaluating Cascade Schedules for On-the-Fly Self-Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: Experimentally compare the efficiency of different cascade schedules with self-speculative acceleration techniques applied to a retrieval-based drafter, utilizing the large Conversational AI (CAI) and Multi-Task DeCKaR (MTD) conversational and machine translation benchmarks. 
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard speculative decoding with a single retrieved drafter; ablations for comparing the performance of individual self-speculative techniques in cascade configurations, and a comparison with a family of separately trained draft models as in prior work.
COST: 672 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find that certain cascade schedules significantly outperform the baseline, yielding speedups that vary depending on the specific application and self-speculative technique used, but overall, achieving up to 30% improvement over standard speculative decoding under ideal conditions, though potentially failing if the compute resources for training the baseline draft models can be included.

TITLE:  Optimizing Cascade Hyperparameters via Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: Utilize a meta-learning approach to adaptively search for the optimal hyperparameters for cascade schedules and self-speculative techniques on diverse set of benchmark tasks, focusing on multi-domain few-shot learning on benchmarks such as QLearner and MathQA problem sets. COST: 1800 GPU-hours

ACTION: REVISE 
TITLE:  Optimizing Cascade Hyperparameters via Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL:  Incorporate the insights gained from the previous proposals, and optimize the meta-learning for cascading while considering the varying task complexity. Utilize a dynamical cascade approach that can adapt to the task complexity in real-time and proposes optimal self-speculative techniques to accelerate the cascade through Repler, Rescer and Lookleo activation methods.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard speculative decoding without self-speculative and dynamical techniques; comparison with the fixed approach and performance comparison with single-source unibloc method.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE:   Evaluating Cascade Robustness to Model Architecture and Input Variability
PROPOSAL:  Investigate the robustness of the suggested cascade approaches to different model architectures and input varieties, especially considering mid-level abstractions for the range over commonly accepted fusion input methods. This involves using web-scraped natural language datasets and static inference time metrics, such as raw corpus transformations and body-level coverage as metrics for sensitivity analysis.
CONTROLS: Baseline: testing the performance of a fixed cascade schedule on a single model architecture.
COST: 2200 GPU-hours

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE:   Improving Cascade Training with Acceleration-Aware Loss Functions
PROPOSAL:  Develop and test acceleration-aware loss functions that explicitly incorporate the computational cost and inference latency into the training objectives, allowing the cascade models to optimize for simultaneous efficacy and efficiency. Apply our modified loss functions on datasets sourced from varied scenarios.
CONTROLS: Baseline: training cascade models using traditional cross-entropy loss.
COST: 2400 GPU-hours

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE:   Towards Optimizing Resource Utilization for Real-World Deployments
PROPOSAL:  Investigate ways to further balance performance and compute efficiency for real-world cascade deployment scenarios by considering variable batch sizes, limited compute budgets, or distributed device resources, leveraging techniques such as trust-region optimization, input subsampling or distributed learning to accelerate execution.
CONTROLS: Baseline: testing existing cascade architectures on resource-constrained scenarios without modifications to resource utilization.
COST: 3000 GPU-hours

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Evaluating Training-Free Self-Speculative Decoding for Cascade Construction
PROPOSAL: We will experimentally evaluate if existing training-free self-speculative decoding methods, such as Lookahead decoding or SWIFT, can be used to construct an effective cascade of draft models above retrieval-based drafting methods for lossless, on-the-fly speculative decoding on several large real-world benchmarks, including multi-turn conversation, machine translation, summation, and question answering.
CONTROLS: Our baselines will be standard speculative decoding with a trained draft model, speculative decoding with a retrieval-based statistical drafter of negligible cost, as well as ablated versions of our proposed cascade with all draft models using the same self-speculative technique.
COST: 12000 
PREDICTION: We expect to find that using cascade construction with training-free self-speculative decoding methods can achieve improved speedup over standard speculative decoding with a trained draft model, and comparable to or even better than speculative decoding with a retrieval-based drafter alone, but this may not always hold for multi-turn conversation, which is more complex and has larger variations in expense for different responses and tasks, and here default to only moderate improvements.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Measuring the Robustness of Cascade Construction to Variations in Acceleration Techniques and Hardware
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate the robustness of our proposed cascade construction with training-free self-speculative decoding methods to variations in acceleration techniques, including different self-speculative methods and their combinations, as well as hardware configurations and usage scenarios, on several large real-world benchmarks.
CONTROLS: Our baselines will be standard speculative decoding with a trained draft model, as well as ablated versions of our proposed cascade construction with a fixed acceleration technique or hardware configuration.
COST: 36000 
PREDICTION: We expect to find that while cascade construction can provide good robustness to variations in acceleration techniques and hardware for tasks with relatively consistent input semantics and cognition demands, such as machine translation and question answering, it may struggle to generalize to tasks with pattern changes in input requests, linguistic artifact changes or different hardware, such as mathematical reasoning and conversation with extreme contextual shifts.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Evaluating Training-Free Self-Speculative Decoding for Cascade Construction
PROPOSAL: We will experimentally evaluate if existing training-free self-speculative decoding methods, such as Lookahead decoding or SWIFT, can be used to construct an effective cascade of draft models above retrieval-based drafting methods for lossless, on-the-fly speculative decoding on several large real-world benchmarks, including multi-turn conversation, machine translation, summation, and question answering.
CONTROLS: Our baselines will be standard speculative decoding with a trained draft model, speculative decoding with a retrieval-based statistical drafter of negligible cost, as well as ablated versions of our proposed cascade with all draft models using the same self-speculative technique.
COST: 36000 
PREDICTION: We expect to find that using cascade construction with training-free self-speculative decoding methods can achieve improved speedup over standard speculative decoding with a trained draft model, and comparable to or even better than speculative decoding with a retrieval-based drafter alone, but this may not always hold for multi-turn conversation, which is more complex and has larger variations in expense for different responses and tasks, and here default to only moderate improvements.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Cascade Schedules for Training-Free Self-Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: Experimentally compare and tune various cascade schedules (different numbers of levels, layer skips, and draft lengths) on 10 real-world benchmark tasks (including multi-turn conversation, machine translation, and summarization) using 4 existing training-free self-speculative techniques (Lookahead, SWIFT, LayerSkip, and Weighted Layer Skipping) below a retrieval-based statistical drafter.
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments using each self-speculative technique separately, as well as standard speculative decoding and a lightweight retrieval-based drafter.
COST: 830
PREDICTION: Cascades can achieve better acceleration than using each technique in isolation, but the best schedule will depend on the task and technique, and may require more GPU-hours to optimize than a simple ablation study. 

This experiment will set the stage for more in-depth analysis of the effects of cascade scheduling on the performance of speculative decoding, and provide a foundation for the second research question about adaptive draft model selection.

TITLE: Exploring Early-Exit Strategies for Draft Models in Cascade Schedules
PROPOSAL: Investigate how early-exit strategies (e.g., stop the draft model after a specified number of tokens or when confidence exceeds a threshold) interact with cascade schedules, focusing on reducing computational overhead while maintaining high acceptance rates. PREDICTION: Early-exit strategies can lead to substantial reductions in computational overhead, especially for tasks with short sequence lengths, but may compromise acceptance rates for longer sequences.

TITLE: Confidence-Calibrated Discriminative Reward Model via Joint Training with an Uncertainty Estimator
PROPOSAL: Develop a discriminative reward model (based on the recent Skywork-Reward framework) that incorporates an uncertainty estimator trained jointly in a Bayesian neural network (BNN) to produce a probability density function (PDF) of reward scores for each response. This can capture the inherent ambiguity in human preference judgments, allowing for uncertainty-aware ranking and calibration of reward scores. We'll apply this novel model to the bAbI gelişim dataset, a widely-used benchmark for chatbot response quality evaluation.

COST: 12,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the novel model to yield more accurate and calibrated reward scores than state-of-the-art discriminative models, especially under conditions with annotator disagreement. However, the increased model complexity and training costs might challenge its practical deployment, particularly when adapting to new domains or with limited quality annotations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Inter-domain Adaptability of Reward Models using Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: Explore meta-learning techniques (e.g., MAML, RePTile) to develop reward models that can efficiently adapt to new, unseen domains with limited learning data. We'll train a meta-reward model on a mix of diverse LLM domains (mathematical reasoning, chatbot safety, role-play dialogue) and fine-tune it on each target domain. This approach aims to ground the reward model in an absolute quality scale using limited quality annotations available in new domains, while preserving ranking accuracy.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the meta-reward model's adaptability using a temperature-based adaptation strategy and compare it with the standard approach of fine-tuning upon retraining a large quantity of data annotations in every target domain.
COST: 36,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Meta-learning might improve adaptation efficiency but might not fully capture domain-specific knowledge and implicitly calibrate to different domain samples, which could degrade model performance in less familiar domains or domains with drastic distribution shifts.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hybrid Reward Model for LLMs (HRM)
PROPOSAL: We design a hybrid reward model that combines the strengths of discriminative and generative reward paradigms. HRM consists of a modified version of Skywork-Reward's discriminator as the base, on top of which we attach an optional generative head (a simple transformer-based sequence-to-sequence model) responsible for producing 8-BIT-confidence scores for each response. Unlike its generative counterparts, HRM's generative head does not require rigid pairwise input formats, can be trained end-to-end with support from the base discriminator, and only leverages the small subset of responses that the discriminator flags as high-quality or low-quality. The confidence scores will quantify the model's uncertainty in ranking responses.
CONTROLS: Strong baseline comparisons to both Skywork-Reward and a full generative model like InternLM2-Reward, as well as an ablation study which trains HRM without the generative head.
COST: 14400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: HRM should outperform discriminative models in terms of ranking accuracy and out-of-distribution robustness and match or slightly outdo generative models in terms of efficiency and interpretability. If adversarially trained with a Mixup adversary, HRM may get seriously off-track, leading to loss of interpretability in the confidence scores.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generative Discriminative Hybrid Reward Model (GDHRM)
PROPOSAL: We design a new Generative Discriminative Hybrid Reward Model (GDHRM) that integrates a discriminative model (e.g., Skywork-Reward) within a probabilistic framework that outputs continuous confidence scores for the generative model's chain-of-thought critiques. GDHRM combines the ranking accuracy of discriminative models with the interpretability of generative models. It first leverages a discriminator like Skywork-Reward to estimate a prior probability distribution over response quality, and uses this prior to derive a posterior probability distribution over quality for a response given its critiques.
CONTROLS: Strong baseline comparisons to both Skywork-Reward and a full generative model like InternLM2-Reward, as well as a case study on several diverse LLM-based applications.
COST: 86400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: GDHRM should outperform existing generative and discriminative reward models on ranking accuracy, while offering increased interpretability through its probabilistic outputs. If the discriminator and generative model are too strongly optimized, the posterior distribution may not accurately reflect uncertainty in the model's responses.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Relative Quality Estimation using Active Learning (RQEA)
PROPOSAL: We design a novel active learning framework, RQEA, to efficiently estimate the relative quality of responses generated by LLMs, incorporating active selection of informative instances for supervision. By leveraging an initial discriminative base model's predictions and sampling a subset of instances for human evaluation, RQEA can iteratively refine the evaluation model to accurately rank responses according to their quality, adapting the sampling strategy based on the uncertainty and confidence of the base model's predictions.
CONTROLS: Testing on both synthetic and real-world datasets for ranking accuracy, with strong baseline comparisons to standard ranking methods and uncertain-based sampling strategies, on role-play dialogue evaluation.
COST: 192000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: RQEA should result in improved ranking accuracy through efficient active learning, particularly in scenarios with scarce human annotation resources; however, its performance may be undermined by inadequate initial base models or inconsistent human evaluation outputs.

TITLE: Scalable and Transferable Reward Model via Meta-Learning (SMRM)
PROPOSAL: We develop SMRM, a meta-learning approach that trains reward models to adapt to diverse LLM applications and domains by learning a set of generalized task-invariant features and updating rules. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hybrid Reward Model for LLMs (HRM)
PROPOSAL: We design a hybrid reward model that combines the strengths of discriminative and generative reward paradigms. HRM consists of a modified version of Skywork-Reward's discriminator as the base, on top of which we attach an optional generative head (a simple transformer-based sequence-to-sequence model) responsible for producing 8-BIT-confidence scores for each response. Unlike its generative counterparts, HRM's generative head does not require rigid pairwise input formats, can be trained end-to-end with support from the base discriminator, and only leverages the small subset of responses that the discriminator flags as high-quality or low-quality. The confidence scores will quantify the model's uncertainty in ranking responses.
CONTROLS: Strong baseline comparisons to both Skywork-Reward and a full generative model like InternLM2-Reward, as well as an ablation study which trains HRM without the generative head.
COST: 43200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: HRM should outperform discriminative models in terms of ranking accuracy and out-of-distribution robustness and match or slightly outdo generative models in terms of efficiency and interpretability. If adversarially trained with a Mixup adversary, HRM may get seriously off-track, leading to loss of interpretability in the confidence scores.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Hybrid Reward Model for LLMs (HRM)
PROPOSAL: Refining the proposal from earlier, we now include a new learning objective for the HRM's generative head, inspired by self-supervised sequence-to-sequence pretraining models, which encourages it to predict the ground-truth preference judgments for an additional small validation set of real-world data. This self-supervised setup allows us to leverage limited quality annotations more efficiently and trains the HRM to directly predict intrinsic quality.
CONTROLS: Same as before, with an additional analysis of how self-supervised pretraining affects the generative head's learning dynamics and overall model performance.
COST: 86400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Incorporating self-supervised pretraining should result in HRM models that better capture absolute quality and diverge less from discriminative models in ranking accuracy, but obtaining these benefits will likely come at the cost of more extensive computational resources, which may offset benefits seen on some smaller datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generative Discriminative Hybrid Reward Model (GDHRM)
PROPOSAL: We design a new Generative Discriminative Hybrid Reward Model (GDHRM) that integrates a discriminative model (e.g., Skywork-Reward) within a probabilistic framework that outputs continuous confidence scores for the generative model's chain-of-thought critiques. GDHRM combines the ranking accuracy of discriminative models with the interpretability of generative models. It first leverages a discriminator like Skywork-Reward to estimate a prior probability distribution over response quality, and uses this prior to derive a posterior probability distribution over quality for a response given its critiques.
CONTROLS: Strong baseline comparisons to both Skywork-Reward and a full generative model like InternLM2-Reward, as well as a case study on several diverse LLM-based applications.
COST: 259200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: GDHRM should outperform existing generative and discriminative reward models on ranking accuracy, while offering increased interpretability through its probabilistic outputs. If the discriminator and generative model are too strongly optimized, the posterior distribution may not accurately reflect uncertainty in the model's responses.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Generative Discriminative Hybrid Reward Model (GDHRM)
PROPOSAL: Building on the previous GDHRM design, we integrate a risk calibration factor, inspired by calibration metrics, as a regularization term in the generative model's training objective. This factor encourages the model to produce uncertainty estimates that are consistent with empirical risk for a diverse range of responses and application domains. This allows the model to better capture the uncertainty in its predictions and align with real-world requirements for robustness.
CONTROLS: Maintain same controls as before, with an additional analysis of the impact on ranking accuracy and robustness under various levels of risk calibration.
COST: 388800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Introducing the risk calibration factor should improve the robustness and reliability of GDHRM, allowing it to better capture uncertainty and variance across diverse LLM applications. However, overly aggressive calibration might lead to a reduction in ranking accuracy or too conservative predictions.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: 1. Hybrid Reward Model for LLMs (HRM)
PROPOSAL: We revise the HRM's self-supervised learning objective to leverage a new variant of the coherence score, specifically designed to better account for the varying degrees of controversial or ambiguous input prompts and the annotator disagreement that often accompanies them. This revised coherence score will allow HRM to improve its ability to accurately capture the intrinsic quality of responses, even in the presence of conflicting preference judgments.
CONTROLS: Maintain same controls as before, with an additional analysis of how the revised coherence score impacts model performance on diverse set of input prompts.
COST: 576000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Incorporating the revised coherence score should enhance the HRM's robustness to conflicted or hard-to-evaluate input prompts and better align with real-world requirements for evaluating response quality. However, accurately designing and training the revised coherence score remains a challenging task, which could impact model performance if not handled correctly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration of Discriminative Reward Models through Ensemble Methods
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the use of ensemble methods (bagging, boosting, or stacking) in discriminative reward models to reduce uncertainty and improve calibration. Specifically, train multiple ML-based value heads, and combine their outputs using different ensemble techniques. The base models will be trained on various datasets from the RLHF and chatbot response evaluation domains, with the Bradley-Terry objective optimized. In a real-world evaluation, use 5-shot average precision and the Bradley-Terry ranking error as metrics to compare the integrated ensemble models with baseline discriminative models.
CONTROLS: Baseline discriminative models trained with mere Bradley-Terry, same hyperparameters for all ensembled variants.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Improved calibration and reduced ranking error should be observed compared to baseline models, as excepted due to effective ensemble-based uncertainty reduction. However, individual results might vary significantly based on choice of base models, learning schedules and hyperparameters for the ensembled models, defecting diminishing returns in over-ensembled instance.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Ensembling Discriminative Models for Consistent Reward Signals
PROPOSAL: We propose an ensembling method that combines multiple instances of a state-of-the-art discriminative reward model to produce a consensus score, which represents a probabilistic ranking over potential responses. This is achieved by training multiple models on different subsets of the data or with different weight architectures. The final score for a given response is obtained by aggregating the individual scores from these models. We also explore various ensembling techniques, such as Bayesian model averaging, stacking, and bagging, to further improve the quality of the reward signal.

However, this approach might introduce some extra computational overhead, especially when dealing with very large datasets.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Learning Absolute Quality Judgments using a Rank-Based Calibration Framework
PROPOSAL: We propose a rank-based calibration framework to ground the reward model in an absolute quality scale, using a limited number of quality annotations. We train a ranker model to predict the pairwise rankings between responses, and then use a calibration function to convert these rankings into absolute quality scores. We further incorporate a subset of quality annotations to fine-tune the calibration function, allowing it to learn the absolute quality scale. We investigate different calibration functions, such as Platt scaling and isotonic regression, to optimize the performance of the reward model.
CONTROLS: Baselines include state-of-the-art discriminative reward models like Skywork-Reward and ArmoRM, as well as a naive approach that uses raw rankings to determine absolute quality. We also experiment with ablating different calibration functions to evaluate their contribution.
COST: 260000
PREDICTION: The proposed rank-based calibration framework should enable the reward model to learn absolute quality judgments using limited quality annotations, and achieve state-of-the-art performance in absolute quality evaluation metrics. However, this approach might be sensitive to the quality of the few-shot quality annotations, and its performance could degrade if the ranker model is not well-calibrated.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Generative Reward Model with Flexibility in Response Evaluation
PROPOSAL: We propose an uncertainty-aware generative reward model that leverages the native generative capabilities of LLMs to produce probabilistic critiques and scores for multiple responses. The model is trained using a combination of reinforcement learning and uncertainty-aware objectives, such as entropy regularization and moment matching, to encourage the model to produce more informative and reliable critiques. We also introduce a flexibility mechanism that allows the model to evaluate responses in a flexible manner, such as ranking multiple responses or providing absolute quality scores.
CONTROLS: Baselines include state-of-the-art generative reward models like HelpSteer2-Preference and ArmoRM, as well as a simple generative model that produces deterministic critiques. We also experiment with ablating different uncertainty-aware objectives to evaluate their contribution.
COST: 432000
PREDICTION: The proposed uncertainty-aware generative reward model should improve the accuracy and interpretability of the reward signal by accounting for the uncertainty in human preference judgments, and achieve state-of-the-art performance in both ranking and absolute quality evaluation metrics. However, this approach might introduce some extra computational overhead due to the complexity of the uncertainty-aware objectives.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Beyond ReDeEP: Quantifying External Context and Internal Knowledge Utilization with Graph Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: We will design a graph neural network (GNN) to quantify external context utilization E(a | q, d) and internal knowledge utilization I(a | q, d) without relying on heuristics such as specific attention heads or layers. The GNN will represent the generated response a as a node, and the context tokens and the internal knowledge states as separate nodes. The edges between these nodes will capture the attention weights and the semantic relationships between the context tokens, and the internal knowledge states, respectively. We will use a message passing algorithm to propagate the information through the graph and generate two vector representations of the response, one capturing the external context utilization and the other capturing the internal knowledge utilization. We will then use these vectors to compute the divergence between them, which will serve as the hallucination score.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to ReDeEP and other recent approaches that rely on mechanistic-interpretability heuristics. We will also conduct an ablation study to show that the specific architecture of the GNN is crucial for achieving good performance.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: We expect our approach to outperform recent approaches that rely on heuristics, but may struggle with models that have internal knowledge that is very similar to the external context, which could lead to underdetection.

TITLE: Efficient Entropy-based Hallucination Detection with Pre-trained Language Models
PROPOSAL: We will design a method that uses pre-trained language models to compute the entropy of the generated response given the external context, and compare it to the entropy of the generated response without the context. The difference between these two entropies will serve as the hallucination score. We will use a pre-trained language model to compute the probability distributions over the tokens in the response, and then compute the Shannon entropy of these distributions. We will also use an evaluation dataset to fine-tune the language model to better capture the hallucination phenomenon.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Beyond ReDeEP: Quantifying External Context and Internal Knowledge Utilization with Graph Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: We will design a graph neural network (GNN) to quantify external context utilization E(a | q, d) and internal knowledge utilization I(a | q, d) without relying on heuristics such as specific attention heads or layers. The GNN will represent the generated response a as a node, and the context tokens and the internal knowledge states as separate nodes. The edges between these nodes will capture the attention weights and the semantic relationships between the context tokens, and the internal knowledge states, respectively. We will use a message passing algorithm to propagate the information through the graph and generate two vector representations of the response, one capturing the external context utilization and the other capturing the internal knowledge utilization. We will then use these vectors to compute the divergence between them, which will serve as the hallucination score.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to ReDeEP and other recent approaches that rely on mechanistic-interpretability heuristics. We will also conduct an ablation study to show that the specific architecture of the GNN is crucial for achieving good performance.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: We expect our approach to outperform recent approaches that rely on heuristics, but may struggle with models that have internal knowledge that is very similar to the external context, which could lead to underdetection.

The difference between these two entropies will serve as the hallucination score. We will also use an evaluation dataset to fine-tune the language model to better capture the hallucination phenomenon.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to recent approaches that rely on heuristics, and to a baseline that uses the entropy of the generated response without any context.

PREDICTION: We expect our approach to perform well on datasets where the external context is relevant and sufficient, but may struggle with models that have internal knowledge that is very similar to the external context.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Grounded Generation: Measuring External Context Utilization with Retrieval-Aware Pre-Trained Transformers
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of a new retrieval-aware pre-trained transformer, which is trained to predict the relevance of external context to the generated response, and to focus on utilizing the external context when generating responses. This model is designed to learn an embedding space where the relevant external context is close to the generated response in the embedding space, and an attention mechanism that selects relevant external context. We will measure the performance of this model on LAMBADA and NewsQA datasets, using metrics such as perplexity and BLEU. We will compare it to a strong baseline of Retriever-Augmented Generative Adversarial Networks (RAGAN) on news summarization and data-to-text generation tasks.
CONTROLS: RAGAN
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Grounded Generation model shows significant improvement in utilizing external context and reducing hallucinations, with a 15% increase in BLEU score and a 20% decrease in perplexity compared to the RAGAN baseline. It may fail to generalize well to out-of-domain datasets.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Grounded Generation: Measuring External Context Utilization with Retrieval-Aware Pre-Trained Transformers
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of a new retrieval-aware pre-trained transformer, which is trained to predict the relevance of external context to the generated response, and to focus on utilizing the external context when generating responses. This model is designed to learn an embedding space where the relevant external context is close to the generated response in the embedding space, and an attention mechanism that selects relevant external context. We will measure the performance of this model on LAMBADA and NewsQA datasets, using metrics such as perplexity and BLEU. We will compare it to a strong baseline of Retriever-Augmented Generative Adversarial Networks (RAGAN) on news summarization and data-to-text generation tasks.
CONTROLS: RAGAN
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Grounded Generation model shows significant improvement in utilizing external context and reducing hallucinations, with a 15% increase in BLEU score and a 20% decrease in perplexity compared to the RAGAN baseline. It may fail to generalize well to out-of-domain datasets.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Grounded Generation: Measuring External Context Utilization with Retrieval-Aware Pre-Trained Transformers
PROPOSAL: REVISED APPROACH: To address the potential domain shift issue of the previous approach, we will train a unsupervised domain adaptation module that allows the model to adapt to new domains while maintaining its ability to utilize external context. We will incorporate adversarial training to regularize the model and improve its ability to handle out-of-domain data. We will also introduce a head-to-head comparison with a state-of-the-art hallucination detection method, ReDeEP, on a larger and more diverse set of datasets, including NaturalHistory-C, TriviaQA and ON-HOLD.
CONTROLS: ReDeEP
COST: 3150
PREDICTION: The revised Grounded Generation model shows significant improvement in handling out-of-domain data, with a 25% increase in BLEU score and a 30% decrease in perplexity compared to the original model. However, it may still require extensive fine-tuning to handle very different domains.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Attention-Based Hallucination Scoring using Neural Embeddings
PROPOSAL: Introduce a new hallucination scoring method that uses attention-based neural embeddings to quantify the degree of hallucination in responses. We will use the licensed Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) and use metrics like ROUGE, F1, and accuracy along with a hallucination classification metric. This approach aims to directly capture the essence of hallucination by analyzing the attention distributions and the semantic meaning of responses. We will compare this method to the ReDeEP and Grounded Generation models, and also examine its potential combination with existing hallucination detection techniques.
CONTROLS: Grounded Generation, ReDeEP
COST: 5550
PREDICTION: Attention-Based Hallucination Scoring shows promising results in capturing hallucination, with a 5% increase in ROUGE and a 10% decrease in F1 score, but it may struggle with noisy attention patterns.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Attention-Based Hallucination Scoring using Neural Embeddings
PROPOSAL: REVISED APPROACH: To address the noise issues in attention patterns, we will introduce a noise-aware regularizer that encourages the model to focus on the most relevant and coherent aspects of the context when generating responses. We will also explore using attention as a weighted mask for the generated response to filter out hallucinations, and use the masked response as an input to the hallucination detection model. We will compare the performance of the revised Attention-Based Hallucination Scoring method with the standard approach on the SQuAD dataset, and also evaluate its utility in conjunction with the Grounded Generation model.
CONTROLS: Grounded Generation
COST: 4050
PREDICTION: The revised Attention-Based Hallucination Scoring method shows significant improvement in accuracy, with a 20% increase in F1 score and a 15% decrease in ROUGE score, but it may still struggle with highly abstractive text.

TITLE: External Context Bottleneck Regularized Language Model
PROPOSAL: Introduce a new regularization method for language models that encourages the model to focus on the external context provided when generating responses. This is achieved by adding a bottleneck layer thatcompresses the external context into a lower-dimensional space, and using this compressed representation as a constraint on the model's generation process. We will evaluate the performance of this model on a variety of datasets, including NewsQA and NaturalHistory-C, and compare its performance with the Grounded Generation and Attention-Based Hallucination Scoring methods.
CONTROLS: Grounded Generation, Attention-Based Hallucination Scoring
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: The External Context Bottleneck Regularized Language Model shows promising results in reducing hallucinations, with a 10% increase in F1 score and a 20% decrease in ROUGE score, but it may struggle with highly dependent information across multiple context documents.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning to Use Context and Model Knowledge Signals
PROPOSAL: We will train a newISIBLE-Metric multimodal learning framework on a suite of benchmarks in the retrieval-augmented question answering task (RAQA). This framework will learn to predict the visibility of the two signals - E and I - i.e. how much of the internal knowledge vs. external context is used to generate a response. The visibility score of both signals can then be used to detect hallucinations in RAQA systems.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: A simple ablation study comparing performance of our framework on the task of predicting overall response utilization, to simply predicting whether a response is factual, will examine if our framework learns to utilize the difference between internal and external knowledge.
- Baseline LMs: State-of-the-art models, such as the multi-document summarization models Longformer and BigBird on the multi-task learning benchmark CNN/Daily Mail.
- RAG benchmarks: We will compare our scores to ReDeEP, the retrieval-Augmented generation model proposed for hallucination diagnostics that utilized E and I in RAQA and utilized original scoring methods.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: We aim to show state-of-the-art hallucination detection capability with our Searches-based Metric using practical benchmark tests, with sensitivity evaluation using standard metrics such as accuracy and precision, and testing on news summarization and a range of datasets to unfold the robustness of our scores for visibility i.e. it captures internal model knowledge and external retrieved data usage or otherwise where it may fail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Utilization-Sensitive Language Model Controls
PROPOSAL: Inspired by the observation that the model should rely more on the external context when sufficient and relevant information is available, we design utilization-sensitive controls (USCs) for LLM training. Specifically, we modify the cross-entropy loss used in LLM training by appending an auxiliary loss term that encourages the model to use the external context while generating responses. We will investigate the impact of using USC on hallucination rates and response quality in both RAG and RAQA tasks.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: Train LLMs without USC.
- Hyperparameter tuning: Comprehensive search for the optimal weight of the auxiliary loss.
- Augmented Retrieval: Comparison with the case where the base LLM is fine-tuned with augmented documents for RAG, while giving more weight to those augmentations that more clearly agree with the given query or data contained within.
COST: 14000
PREDICTION: By tweaking LLM training objectives, USCs will effectively bring down the hallucination rates while potentially reducing response quality, since sometimes using less of the original LLM in producing answers can make it lower the generalization to new tasks but utilizing the  background LLM knowledge leads the discovery.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context-Aware Value Alignment for Detecting Hallucinations
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel approach that directly optimizes the value alignment between the model's internal knowledge and the external context in a way that encourages the model to rely on the external context more heavily than internal knowledge when sufficient and relevant information is available. This is achieved through contextualized embeddings of the input and output sequences, and an additional value alignment loss that penalizes the model for deviating from the value alignment.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: Utilization-sensitive language model controls without value alignment.
- Comparison to existing hallucination detection methods: We compare the performance of our approach to existing methods on detecting hallucinations, such as ReDeEP.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: By focusing on value alignment, we expect our approach to be more effective in detecting hallucinations, especially in cases where the model's internal knowledge and external context strongly conflict, but perform worse where there is missing or contradictory info in the context.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Task Learning for Hallucination Detection and Response Quality
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-task learning framework that trains the model to detect hallucinations and improve response quality simultaneously. The framework consists of two components: a hallucination detection module and a response quality prediction module. The hallucination detection module is trained to predict whether a response is hallucinated or not, while the response quality prediction module is trained to predict the quality of a response. We use a shared encoder for both modules and a dual output loss function to optimize both tasks simultaneously.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: Single-task learning for hallucination detection.
- Comparison to existing hallucination detection methods: We compare the performance of our approach to existing methods on detecting hallucinations, such as ReDeEP.
- Evaluation on response quality: We evaluate the performance of our approach on response quality prediction and compare it to existing methods.
COST: 28000
PREDICTION: By training the model to detect hallucinations and improve response quality simultaneously, we expect our approach to be more effective in detecting hallucinations and improving response quality, but it may require careful balancing of the two tasks to avoid overfitting.

TITLE: Learning to Use Context and Model Knowledge Signals
PROPOSAL: We will train a newISIBLE-Metric multimodal learning framework on a suite of benchmarks in the retrieval-augmented question answering task (RAQA). This framework will learn to predict the visibility of the two signals - E and I - i.e. how much of the internal knowledge vs. external context is used to generate a response. The visibility score of both signals can then be used to detect hallucinations in RAQA systems.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: A simple ablation study comparing performance of our framework on the task of predicting overall response utilization, to simply predicting whether a response is factual, will examine if our framework learns to utilize the difference between internal and external knowledge.
- Baseline LMs: State-of-the-art models, such as the multi-document summarization models Longformer and BigBird on the multi-task learning benchmark CNN/Daily Mail.
- RAG benchmarks: We will compare our scores to ReDeEP, the retrieval-Augmented generation model proposed for hallucination diagnostics that utilized E and I in RAQA and utilized original scoring methods.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: We aim to show state-of-the-art hallucination detection capability with our Searches-based Metric using practical benchmark tests, with sensitivity evaluation using standard metrics such as accuracy and precision, and testing on news summarization and a range of datasets to unfold the robustness of our scores for visibility i.e. it captures internal model knowledge and external retrieved data usage or otherwise where it may fail.

TITLE: Utilization-Sensitive Language Model Controls
PROPOSAL: Inspired by the observation that the model should rely more on the external context when sufficient and relevant information is available, we design utilization-sensitive controls (USCs) for LLM training. Specifically, we modify the cross-entropy loss used in LLM training by appending an auxiliary loss term that encourages the model to use the external context while generating responses. We will investigate the impact of using USC on hallucination rates and response quality in both RAG and RAQA tasks.

TITLE: Context-Aware Value Alignment for Detecting Hallucinations
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel approach that directly optimizes the value alignment between the model's internal knowledge and the external context in a way that encourages the model to rely on the external context more heavily than internal knowledge when sufficient and relevant information is available. This is achieved through contextualized embeddings of the input and output sequences, and an additional value alignment loss that penalizes the model for deviating from the value alignment.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: Utilization-sensitive language model controls without value alignment.
- Comparison to existing hallucination detection methods: We compare the performance of our approach to existing methods on detecting hallucinations, such as ReDeEP.
COST: 54000
PREDICTION: By focusing on value alignment, we expect our approach to be more effective in detecting hallucinations, especially in cases where the model's internal knowledge and external context strongly conflict, but perform worse where there is missing or contradictory info in the context.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Attentionomaly Analysis for Hallucination Detection
PROPOSAL: We propose an attentionomaly analysis framework to identify hallucinations in RAG systems. The framework uses attention maps to visualize and quantify the differences between the model's attention patterns on relevant and irrelevant information in the external context. By analyzing these differences, we can identify areas where the model is relying too heavily on internal knowledge, indicating potential hallucinations.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline: Random attention patterns.
- Evaluation on synthetic data: We evaluate the effectiveness of our framework on synthetic data generated with and without hallucinations.

PREDICTION: By analyzing attention patterns, we expect our framework to be able to identify hallucinations with high accuracy, but it may struggle with cases where the attention patterns are highly variable or noisy.

PROPOSAL: We enhance our previous approach of Context-Aware Value Alignment for Detecting Hallucinations by incorporating a regularization term that encourages the model to rely on the external context and reduce over-reliance on internal knowledge. This is achieved through a L1 regularization term on the internal knowledge embeddings and a L2 regularization term on the external context embeddings. By adding these regularization terms, we expect to improve the model's ability to detect hallucinations and reduce over-reliance on internal knowledge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Exploiting Cross-Channel Dependencies with a Scaled Channel Attention Mechanism
PROPOSAL: We propose a variant of the popular transformer architecture that incorporates a scaled channel attention mechanism to capture cross-variable interactions in multivariate time-series forecasting tasks. The proposed mechanism extends the channel-independent encoder by adding a new scaled attention block, which adaptively scales individual attention weights to emphasize cross-channel correlations, alleviating the computational burden and inconsistent accuracy gains associated with existing channel-dependent encoders. This new module will be combined with a channel-wise normalization layer to achieve balanced channel attention. Specifically, we design a sparse self-attention mechanism with soft-masking to further enhance the effect of channel attention across different learnable maps and simplify the computational complexity.
CONTROLS: Compare with the baseline channel-independent encoder (e.g., Encoder-ELM), channel-dependent encoder (e.g., MADE) and segmentation-based transformer (Trans-Fused).
COST: 1440
PREDICTION: The proposed approach is expected to achieve competitive or superior forecasting accuracy compared to existing channel-independent and channel-dependent encoders on our evaluated real-world datasets, while offering a more computationally efficient solution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Efficient Decoding of Temporal Dependencies with a Neural Reconstructor
PROPOSAL: To improve the effectiveness of forecasting models, we explore an alternative to the simple linear projection for decoding, where we introduce a neural reconstructor to directly predict future values from encoded representations. The neural reconstructor consists of a series of stacked long short-term memory (LSTM) cells with gated resonance, designed to learn hierarchical representations of temporal patterns and systematically capture complex temporal dynamics. We propose to learn the reconstructor in a two-stage process: first, we pretrain the reconstructor using a masked reconstruction loss to learn domain-specific temporal patterns; second, we fine-tune the reconstructor with a supervised forecasting objective to achieve accurate future predictions.
CONTROLS: Compare with the baseline linear projection decoding, with and without the proposed two-stage training strategy.
COST: 2160
PREDICTION: By leveraging the self-supervised learning capabilities of the reconstructor to capture complex temporal dynamics, we expect the forecasting model to exhibit improved forecasting accuracy and robustness on the evaluated datasets.
