ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Multitask Learning for Time-Series Forecasting with Attention Enhanced Transformers
PROPOSAL: Inspired by the success of multitask learning in single-channel time-series forecasting, we propose a novel multitask learning approach that leverages attention enhanced transformers to capture multimodal temporal dependencies and interactions in multivariate time-series forecasting. We extend the encoder and decoder components of transformers with attention modules that focus on both channel and temporal dependencies. This approach is trained with multiple loss functions, one for each task, to adapt the model to learn from multiple, possibly related, forecasting objectives. To evaluate the proposed approach, we employ a variety of multitask setups on real-world time-series datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare with the baseline transformers, single-task transformers, and models with shared knowledge across tasks (e.g., AutoEncoders).
COST: 6480
PREDICTION: By learning multiple tasks concurrently and explicitly modeling cross-task dependencies, this approach is expected to outperform baseline models on our evaluated real-world datasets and contribute to improved forecasting accuracy in real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Pretraining-Based Training Strategies for Time-Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: To bridge the gap between pretraining-finetuning and inductive learning, we explore alternative pretraining objectives and training strategies specifically tailored for time-series forecasting tasks. Unlike previous fine-tuning approaches, we design three pretraining objectives that adapt domain-specific knowledge to our inductive forecasting model. (i) Temporal Masking-Reconstruction: We adapt a masking-reconstruction loss to learn temporal patterns. (ii) Channel Masking-Reconstruction, (iii) Temporal Channel Convergence, which captures correlation among channels and premises temporal pattern extraction. We compare these strategies on our various time-series forecasting tasks to analyze their robustness, adaptability and universality.
CONTROLS: Compare with the baseline fine-tuning approach, and pretraining-based models (MAE, MaskedLM).
COST: 10560
PREDICTION: The developed pretraining-based approaches will provide improved adaptation capabilities for inductive models on time-series forecasting tasks across multiple domains, outperforming baseline pretraining-fine-tuning strategies and serving as an intermediate milestone between the purely pretraining and purely fine-tuning methodologies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Metric-Agnostic Evaluation for Time-Series Forecasting Models
PROPOSAL: Existing metrics for evaluating time-series forecasting models are often problem-specific and task-dependent, making it challenging to compare and rank models across different forecasting tasks. To address this issue, we propose a metric-agnostic evaluation framework for time-series forecasting models. We introduce a Novel evaluation approach, INSANITY, based on Information gap, calibration gap, Shapley critique, necessity, Allocation Unbalance and serving Nonlinearity, using Composite instead of basic methods that warrants model robustness.
CONTROLS: Compare with the baseline evaluation metrics (e.g., MSE, MAE), suitable benchmarks to relate INSANITY to the best such available solution.
COST: 81500
PREDICTION: The metric-agnostic evaluation approach will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the performance and robustness of time-series forecasting models, enabling more reliable comparison across different tasks and models. This can be expected to provide superior value for testament frameworks that purport to evaluate & rank models in a principled way.

PROPOSAL: Design and experimentally evaluate a novel hybrid encoder architecture that combines the strengths of channel-independent and channel-dependent encoders. Specifically, we propose a two-stage encoder that first uses a channel-independent encoder to capture low-frequency trends and then uses a channel-dependent encoder to model cross-channel interactions. This approach aims to leverage the robustness and simplicity of channel-independent encoders while incorporating the ability to capture complex cross-channel dependencies.

We will compare the regular masking strategy (i.e., randomly masking a sequence of timesteps) to other variants such as: (1) masking based on higher-frequency trends, (2) masking based on channel-specific patterns, and (3) combination of the above strategies.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline model trained with the regular masking strategy and evaluate the effect of different masking strategies on the generalization performance of the model.

PREDICTION: We expect that masking strategies that are tailored to the patterns and trends present in time-series data will lead to performance improvements over the regular masking strategy, with the combined strategy potentially yielding the best results due to its ability to capitalize on both higher-frequency trends and channel-specific patterns.

TITLE: Graph Convolutional Network for Time-Series Forecasting with Temporal and Cross-Variable Interactions
PROPOSAL: Develop a graph convolutional network (GCN) architecture to model temporal and cross-variable interactions in multivariate time-series forecasting tasks. We will represent the time series data as a graph, where nodes are time-steps and edges are connections between time-steps based on their temporal proximity. We will then use GCN layers to aggregate information from neighboring nodes to make predictions.
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art time-series forecasting models that do not incorporate graph structures, such as transformer-based models, and evaluate the effectiveness of the GCN architecture on various datasets with different levels of temporal and cross-variable dependencies.
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: We expect that the GCN-based model will outperform traditional models on tasks with complex temporal and cross-variable patterns, such as weather forecasting and traffic flow prediction. However, the optimal graph structure and hyperparameters may require extensive tuning, and the scalability of the GCN model to large datasets remains to be explored.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Channel Masking for Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the effectiveness of an adversarial channel masking framework to learn and exploit cross-variable interactions without incurring excessive computational cost. Specifically, we introduce a sports-like environment where different variates in the input data act as contestants competing with each other in an adversarial game. By adopting the gradient reversal layer, our framework allows one variate to know its rival's performance while preventing its winning impacts on the rival's final rank or performance. Our aim is to establish whether this approach facilitates manifest improvements in multivariate time-series forecasting over channel-independent baselines.
CONTROLS: We consider the M4 multi-step time-series forecasting dataset, a widely-used benchmark for various time-series forecasting tasks, and a standard Transformer encoder with channel-independent masking as a baseline. We also use RCAN (Range-based Cascade Attention Network) to compare the different outcomes of channel dependent architectural frameworks that remained proclaimed to be outperformed by powerful multistage dilated casacades based transformers along our proposal designs.
COST:  50
PREDICTION: Our proposed framework enables significantly better forecasting performance than the baseline, which we believe is due to the strengthened learning of cross-channel interactions and flexible channel masking that corrupts their correlations and produces efficiency features. Nonetheless, the algorithm could potentially underperform when the information captured between different variates is limited, especially without accessibility to other computation presets.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bridging Encoder-Decoder Architectures with Masked Hierarchical Attention
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of aligning the training objective with the model architecture in multivariate time-series forecasting, we propose a novel hierarchical attention mechanism that enables the sequential learning of short-term and long-term temporal dependencies. By masking different hierarchies of resolutions and projecting the grouped statistics back to the input space for computation, our model is capable of paying attention to the most relevant contextual information without degrading the quality of captured dynamics. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach in achieving more accurate results than existing state-of-the-art encoder-decoder models that adopt simple pretraining strategies by dissolving them with high attention bias multiplicators around various maskings.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to the pretraining-based Baseline, using masked signal hereby referred to as mBERT-type training against a directly frozen masking-stronger multi-stage adapter topology containing a multi-state finetuning loop that obsesses to streaming separates.
COST:  180
PREDICTION: Our proposed model outperforms the pretraining-based baseline and achieves state-of-the-art results in multivariate time-series forecasting. However, the attention weights could not necessarily generalize to unseen data distribution scenarios that manifest with fundamentally varying temporal correlations, leading to potential degradation of performance.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Bridging Encoder-Decoder Architectures with Masked Hierarchical Attention
PROPOSAL: Revision: To further improve the hierarchical attention mechanism, we add a gated module to control the flow of information between different hierarchical levels. TITLE: Asynchronous Training for Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Most existing approaches to multivariate time-series forecasting rely on synchronous data processing, where all input variables are processed in parallel. We propose an asynchronous training approach that leverages the strengths of asynchronous processing to improve forecasting accuracy and reduce computational overhead. Our method uses a subset of input variables to predict future values of other variables, allowing for efficient and parallelizable training. By experimenting with different communication patterns and learning rates, we can improve model generalization and reduce overfitting. We also investigate the use of momentum-based updates to accelerate convergence.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to existing state-of-the-art methods on various real-world multivariate time-series forecasting datasets, including traffic flow forecasting, with a focus on point forecast accuracy and probabilistic forecast calibration.

PROPOSAL: We propose to compare various pretraining strategies for time-series forecasting models, specifically examining the impact of different masking schemes, data augmentation, and reconstruction objectives on model performance. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring the Robustness of Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting Models to Distribution Shifts
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the robustness of multivariate time-series forecasting models to distribution shifts, which can occur when the underlying data distribution changes over time. Distribution shifts are a common challenge in real-world forecasting applications, and can lead to significant degradation in model performance. For this experiment, we will use the M4 dataset, which provides a large and diverse collection of time-series datasets with controlled distribution shifts.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: No robustness training, Baseline 2: Traditional regularization techniques (e.g., dropout, L1/L2 regularization)
COST: 10744
PREDICTION: We expect that using robustness training methods (e.g., robust loss functions, adversarial training) will improve the out-of-distribution generalization of multivariate time-series forecasting models, and reduce the impact of distribution shifts on model performance. However, we also anticipate that the optimal approach will depend on the specific characteristics of the distribution shift and the forecasting model being used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Pretraining Strategies for Time-Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose to compare various pretraining strategies for time-series forecasting models, specifically examining the impact of different masking schemes, data augmentation, and reconstruction objectives on model performance. For this experiment, we will utilize the ConvTASNet (Li et al., 2020) model and train it on the Area Traffic Flow (ATF) dataset (Duan et al., 2016), a real-world benchmark for traffic flow forecasting.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: ConvTASNet pretraining with random masking, Baseline 2: ConvTASNet pretraining with exponential moving average (EMA) masking, Baseline 3: ConvTASNet without pretraining
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: We expect to observe improved forecasting accuracy with pretraining, with EMA masking outperforming random masking, and random masking outperforming no pretraining. However, the extent of improvement may vary across different masking schemes, and we anticipate that no pretraining might lead to the best results in some cases where the pretraining objective is mismatched with the target task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Channel-Dependent Modeling with Graph Attention Networks
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the use of Graph Attention Networks (GATs) as a channel-dependent encoder for multivariate time-series forecasting. The GAT will learn to selectively attend to relevant channels and capture their interactions, potentially improving forecasting accuracy without increasing computational cost. For this experiment, we will utilize the M5 dataset (Taylor and Letham, 2020) for multivariate electricity load forecasting, which includes time-series data of 12 different channels.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Convolutional layer for channel-dependent modeling, Baseline 2: Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) for channel-dependent modeling
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: We expect GAT to outperform GCN in terms of forecasting accuracy, as it can selectively and adaptively attend to relevant channels. However, we also predict a potential risk of overfitting with GAT, which could be mitigated by increasing the training data or incorporating regularization techniques.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Designing a Hierarchical Architecture for Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a hierarchical time-series forecasting architecture that consists of multiple encoders and decoders, each processing a different scale or level of temporal resolution. This architecture can learn to capture local temporal patterns at each scale, as well as higher-level temporal dependencies that span multiple scales. For this experiment, we will utilize the NASDAQ stock prices dataset, which provides multivariate time-series data with multiple financial indicators and different time scales.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Single-scale encoder-decoder architecture, Baseline 2: Multi-scale convolutional neural network (CNN)
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: We expect the hierarchical architecture to improve forecasting accuracy by capturing complex temporal patterns at multiple scales, and to outperform the single-scale architecture. Our primary concern is the potential for increased computational cost and complexity due to the hierarchical design, which could be mitigated by pruning or compressing the model once it has been trained.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Enhancing Prediction with Domain Knowledge through Ontology-driven Data Transformation
PROPOSAL: We revise our previous proposal on Designing a Hierarchical Architecture for Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting, by incorporating domain knowledge and ontological information about the time-series data into the hierarchical architecture. We will transform the raw time-series data into a more abstract representation that is consistent with the domain ontology, and then feed the transformed data into the hierarchical architecture. This approach can help the model capture complex relationships between different variables and improve forecasting accuracy in the target domain. For this experiment, we will utilize the weather forecasting dataset from the National Weather Service (NWS), which provides a rich source of domain knowledge and ontological information.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Hierarchical architecture without domain knowledge, Baseline 2: Traditional forecasting methods (e.g. ARIMA, SARIMA) with domain knowledge
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: We expect the ontology-driven data transformation to significantly improve forecasting accuracy, especially for long-term predictions. Our primary concern is the potential for information loss during the transformation process, which could affect the model's ability to capture local temporal patterns.

For this updated experiment, we will utilize the NASDAQ stock prices dataset, which provides multivariate time-series data with multiple financial indicators and different time scales.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Single-scale encoder-decoder architecture, Baseline 2: Multi-scale convolutional neural network (CNN), Baseline 3: Hierarchical architecture without TAF

PREDICTION: We expect the TAF-enhanced hierarchical architecture to improve forecasting accuracy by adaptively focusing on the most relevant features at each scale and scale level, and to outperform the single-scale architecture and the multi-scale CNN. Our primary concern is the potential risk of overfitting due to the increased complexity of the hierarchical architecture with TAF.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Channel-Interactions via Asymmetric Transformers
PROPOSAL: Develop an asymmetric Transformer-based architecture for multivariate time-series forecasting, where channel-independent and channel-dependent components are combined to exploit cross-channel interactions. Specifically, we'll use a large encoder that captures variate-level patterns using a standard Transformer layer, and a smaller decoder that focuses on capturing cross-variable interactions using a custom-made Transformer block with attention weights between channels. To train the model, we'll use a combination of masking-and-reconstruction and mean squared error loss functions.
CONTROLS: Compare with the state-of-the-art channel-independent and channel-dependent Transformers on the dataset, as well as a baseline model that incorporates a simple linear projection for decoding.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: This model should achieve state-of-the-art performance by capturing both high-level and low-level channel interactions, achieving average improvement of 5-7% over existing methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Alternative Decoding Path for Cross-Channel Interactions
PROPOSAL: Design a novel decoding head to generate cross-channel predictions, based on the interaction patterns learned by both variants of the asymmetric Transformer and the adaptive temporal alignment encoding. Through an Inter-Layer-Attention based decoding (IAD) appropriate to a Transformer encoder, we add self-interactions on its internal representations to transfer learned knowledge about channel interactions. Our model focuses on decoding methods that are less likely to disrupt information that was encoded separately for each input dimension, also via masking- and prediction-based objectives to eventually handle decoding consistency within encoded cross-channel representation relationships.
CONTROLS: Model against strong baseline methods with sophisticated encoding-decoding mechanisms and we also assess our IAD against simple projection/standard linear projection rules such as those typically used in time-series decoding frameworks.
COST: 2100
PREDICTION: Our IAD model can lead to an average forecast improvement of 12-14% against the multivariable benchmarks on real data, benefitting especially time-series forecasting tasks in electricity consumption, speed predictions, and solar power forecasting.

TITLE: Decentralized Hyperparameter Learning for Time-Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel decentralized approach to hyperparameter learning in time-series forecasting models to reduce computational overhead and avoid overfitting. A swarm of agents, each responsible for adjusting the model's hyperparameters, collaborates to find the optimal set of parameters for the entire forecasting system. This decentralized strategy can improve the adaptability and robustness of the forecasting model to changing environmental conditions.
CONTROLS: Compare decentralized hyperparameter learning with traditional grid search and random search methods, as well as decentralized hyperparameter learning with a central controller for model hyperparameter tuning.
COST: 3500
PREDICTION: Decentralized hyperparameter learning can significantly reduce training time and achieve comparable or even better forecasting performance in comparison with traditional methods, especially in large-scale or dynamic systems like those encountered in electricity transformer temperature forecasting or solar power generation forecasting.

PROPOSAL: Design a novel forecasting framework based on Monte Carlo Q-Networks (MCQN) to effectively model and quantify uncertainty in time-series forecasting tasks. PROPOSAL: Propose an efficiency-oriented time-series forecasting framework using series decomposition and Riemann sum neural networks (RSNN). By decomposing time-series data into multiple sub-series, RSNN learns a more compact and interpretable representation of the data, enabling efficient forecasting and uncertainty quantification. This approach can be particularly effective in scenarios with highly variable or irregularly sampled data, such as traffic flow forecasting or electricity consumption forecasting.

PROPOSAL: Design a scalable federated learning framework for time-series forecasting in edge computing scenarios, where decentralized data storage and computation are critical. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Channel-Interactions via Asymmetric Transformers
PROPOSAL: Develop an asymmetric Transformer-based architecture for multivariate time-series forecasting, where channel-independent and channel-dependent components are combined to exploit cross-channel interactions. Specifically, we'll use a large encoder that captures variate-level patterns using a standard Transformer layer, and a smaller decoder that focuses on capturing cross-variable interactions using a custom-made Transformer block with attention weights between channels. To train the model, we'll use a combination of masking-and-reconstruction and mean squared error loss functions.
CONTROLS: Compare with the state-of-the-art channel-independent and channel-dependent Transformers on the dataset, as well as a baseline model that incorporates a simple linear projection for decoding.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: This model should achieve state-of-the-art performance by capturing both high-level and low-level channel interactions, achieving average improvement of 5-7% over existing methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhancing Encoding thru Temporal Alignment
PROPOSAL: Introduce temporal alignment techniques into the channel-independent encoder architecture to improve its ability to capture temporal patterns in the data. Specifically, we'll apply soft-histogram-based temporal alignment and a fully-synchronous version of it to the input time-series at all variates, followed by a standard Transformer encoder. This will enable a better understanding of time-evolving signals and enhance the quality of encoded representations.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance with and without temporal alignment techniques applied to different variants of the baseline channel-independent Transformers; a simple variant without temporal alignment; and a standard model without temporal alignments.
COST: 2450
PREDICTION:  Temporal alignment is expected to improve forecasting performance on datasets where signals overlap substantially in time, particularly revealing 10-12% improvement in metrics in comparison to original settings.)

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Enhancing Encoding thru Temporal Alignment
PROPOSAL (REVISION): Modify the temporal alignment (TA) step in the encoder to be adaptive per-channel. This involves learning a channel-specific learned synchronization technique, contrasting a post-hoc histogram alignment. This adaptive TA learns to handle dynamics where signals have different temporal frequencies and/or varying time scales. We will compare its effectiveness against the hard-coded histogram-based approach and other existing variate-aware learning methods in different forecasting domains.
CONTROLS: The performance comparison will examine various case studies using real-world datasets to demonstrate that learning-based temporal alignment performs consistently better across both strong and weak signal channels than state-of-the-art synchronization strategies. (Contrast a histogram-based alignment vs. the adaptive TA for predicting top- performing few variate data of weather forecasting.) 
COST: 4300
PREDICTION: The adaptive temporal alignment could significantly increase encoding quality and yield an overall increase in forecasting performance of up to 15-17% in comparison to the static histogram alignment strategy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Alternative Decoding Path for Cross-Channel Interactions
PROPOSAL: Design a novel decoding head to generate cross-channel predictions, based on the interaction patterns learned by both variants of the asymmetric Transformer and the adaptive temporal alignment encoding. Through an Inter-Layer-Attention based decoding (IAD) appropriate to a Transformer encoder, we add self-interactions on its internal representations to transfer learned knowledge about channel interactions. Our model focuses on decoding methods that are less likely to disrupt information that was encoded separately for each input dimension, also via masking- and prediction-based objectives to eventually handle decoding consistency within encoded cross-channel representation relationships.
CONTROLS: Model against strong baseline methods with sophisticated encoding-decoding mechanisms and we also assess our IAD against simple projection/standard linear projection rules such as those typically used in time-series decoding frameworks.
COST: 6300
PREDICTION: Our IAD model can lead to an average forecast improvement of 12-14% against the multivariable benchmarks on real data, benefitting especially time-series forecasting tasks in electricity consumption, speed predictions, and solar power forecasting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decentralized Hyperparameter Learning for Time-Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel decentralized approach to hyperparameter learning in time-series forecasting models to reduce computational overhead and avoid overfitting. A swarm of agents, each responsible for adjusting the model's hyperparameters, collaborates to find the optimal set of parameters for the entire forecasting system. This decentralized strategy can improve the adaptability and robustness of the forecasting model to changing environmental conditions.
CONTROLS: Compare decentralized hyperparameter learning with traditional grid search and random search methods, as well as decentralized hyperparameter learning with a central controller for model hyperparameter tuning.
COST: 10500
PREDICTION: Decentralized hyperparameter learning can significantly reduce training time and achieve comparable or even better forecasting performance in comparison with traditional methods, especially in large-scale or dynamic systems like those encountered in electricity transformer temperature forecasting or solar power generation forecasting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Monte Carlo Q-Networks for Exploring Forecasting Uncertainty
PROPOSAL: Design a novel forecasting framework based on Monte Carlo Q-Networks (MCQN) to effectively model and quantify uncertainty in time-series forecasting tasks. MCQN integrates deep reinforcement learning and Monte Carlo tree search to efficiently explore the uncertainty space and make more informed predictions. This approach can provide better risk assessment and decision-making capabilities in uncertain or volatile conditions.
CONTROLS: Compare MCQN-based forecasting with traditional Bayesian neural networks and ensembling methods, as well as ablation studies on the MCQN architecture.
COST: 12500
PREDICTION: MCQN can achieve significant improvements in forecasting performance and uncertainty estimation compared to state-of-the-art methods, especially in high-noise or high-uncertainty domains such as traffic flow forecasting or weather forecasting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficiency-Oriented Time-Series Forecasting via Series Decomposition and Riemann Sum Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: Propose an efficiency-oriented time-series forecasting framework using series decomposition and Riemann sum neural networks (RSNN). By decomposing time-series data into multiple sub-series, RSNN learns a more compact and interpretable representation of the data, enabling efficient forecasting and uncertainty quantification. This approach can be particularly effective in scenarios with highly variable or irregularly sampled data, such as traffic flow forecasting or electricity consumption forecasting.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of RSNN-based forecasting against state-of-the-art methods, including variational autoencoders and temporal convolutional networks, as well as ablation studies on the effectiveness of series decomposition and Riemann sum-based learning.
COST: 14500
PREDICTION: RSNN-based forecasting can achieve improvements in both efficiency and forecasting accuracy, especially in scenarios with high data variability or irregular sampling rates, and outperform existing methods in some cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable Federated Learning for Time-Series Forecasting in Edge Computing Scenarios
PROPOSAL: Design a scalable federated learning framework for time-series forecasting in edge computing scenarios, where decentralized data storage and computation are critical. The framework, called EdgeTS, enables efficient collaboration between edge devices and a central server to leverage collective knowledge and update global models. EdgeTS incorporates techniques for distributed data aggregation, model synchronization, and adaptive sampling to achieve high-quality forecasting performance while maintaining data privacy and reducing communication overhead.
CONTROLS: Compare EdgeTS-based forecasting with traditional centralized learning and decentralized methods, such as federated learning with single-device updates, and evaluate the impact of network topology, device mobility, and model size on the overall performance of the framework.
COST: 17500
PREDICTION: EdgeTS can significantly improve the scalability and efficiency of time-series forecasting in edge computing scenarios, achieving comparable or even better performance than traditional centralized methods while ensuring data privacy and reducing communication overhead.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Characterizing View Information through Conditional Mutual Information
PROPOSAL: We propose to measure the amount of information contributed by each view through the lens of conditional mutual information (CMI), specifically by computing the CMI between a view and the original instance conditional on the entire training set (or a subset thereof). We'll consider the VARENV (VARIational scene ENVIronment) dataset from the visual scene understanding domain, and evaluate our approach using the standard metrics of negative log likelihood (NLL) for predicting a corresponding view, and mutual information score (MIS) between the original instance and each view.
CONTROLS: This experiment will be controlled by comparing to a baseline method that uses a fixed, predefined order of views, and an ablation study will also be performed with the CMI estimator evaluating the uniformity across views only.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: We expect a moderate improvement in mutual information scores between the original instance and each view, with some instances showing a higher reduction in the CMI compared to others, potentially indicating limitations of the approach in capturing complex instance dependencies. The experiment might fail due to difficulties in estimating CMI from samples.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Adaptive View Expansion through Open-Set Information Bottleneck
PROPOSAL: Building upon the insight from proposal 1, we'll explore a novel method to adaptively expand the representational capacity of each instance through an open-set information bottleneck (OSIB) objective, which explicitly trades off view informativeness against instance accuracy. OSIB will be optimized through a minimax formulation that seeks to minimize the information lost about instances, while maximizing the information gained about novel, unseen views.
CONTROLS: To demonstrate the efficacy of our adaptive method, we compare against SimCLR, MoCo, and a static augmentation baseline, while also exploring an ablation study that replaces OSIB with the standard noise contrastive estimation (NCE) objective.
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: We expect our OSIB objective to significantly outperform existing methods, particularly in settings where instance representations need to adapt rapidly to novel patterns. However, the minimax optimization might introduce instabilities or mode collapse, which could impact the robustness of our method.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Instance-Level Information in Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We investigate the role of instance-level information in contrastive learning models through an information-theoretic lens. Specifically, we will decompose the mutual information between views into two components: instance-level information and class-level information. This will enable us to analyze how each contributes to the overall performance of contrastive learning models and to identify potential opportunities for improvement.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to a variety of baseline methods that ignore instance-level information, as well as to methods that use hand-crafted features to capture instance-level information.
COST: 480000
PREDICTION: We expect to find that instance-level information plays a crucial role in the performance of contrastive learning models, and that our approach can significantly improve performance by capturing this information accurately. However, the high computational cost of estimating instance-level information may limit the feasibility of this approach in practice.

TITLE: Investigating Information Gain through Contrastive Learning with Active Augmentations
PROPOSAL: We will extend a variant of SimCLR with an active augmentation pipeline that adaptively selects new augmentations based on the information gained about each instance. Specifically, we will use a simple iterative process: augment an instance, compute the mutual information between the original instance and its augmented views, and use this information to guide the selection of the next augmentation. We will apply this process in a small-batch setting, with a batch size of 32.

PREDICTION: We expect to see a moderate increase in representation quality, with some instances exhibiting larger gains due to the adaptiveness of the augmentation process. However, we anticipate potential instability and decreased generalization for the worst-case instances.

TITLE: Analyzing View Diversity through b-Mutual Information
PROPOSAL: We will study the effects of view diversity in contrastive learning by introducing a new information-theoretic quantity: b-mutual information (bMI). bMI measures the mutual information between two sets of instances viewed as separate random variables, and can be used to quantify the diversity of views. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Contrastive Learning in Hardware-Constrained Settings with Low-Shot Learning
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the efficacy of contrastive learning in low-shot learning settings where neither the batch size nor the number of augmentations per instance can be increased. To overcome the limitations of hardware, we will leverage a set of precomputed augmentations generated offline, and instead limit model capacity through knowledge distillation. We will train a teacher model using the original full-batch dataset, and then train a student model in a low-shot setting with the precomputed augmentations.
CONTROLS: We will compare the student model to a baseline model trained under the original batch size constraints, as well as a state-of-the-art low-shot learning method without contrastive learning.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: We expect the knowledge distillation framework to mitigate the effects of low-shot learning, allowing the model to reach acceptable performance levels. However, we anticipate potential instabilities and overfitting risks due to the limited capacity of the student model.

TITLE: Contrastive Learning with Adaptive View Transformation (ALT)
PROPOSAL: Implement a novel contrastive learning algorithm, ALT, which dynamically adjusts view transformations based on the instance's information gain. Inspired by attention mechanisms, ALT introduces a learnable transformation matrix that controls the adaptability of each view. The model seeks to maximize mutual information between different views and their correspondent augmented versions. We evaluate ALT against state-of-the-art methods like SimCLR and MoCo on benchmark datasets such as ImageNet and CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100.

COST: 336

TITLE: Instance-Specific Mutual Information Analysis (ISMIA)
PROPOSAL: Develop a method to estimate instance-specific mutual information (ISMIA) as a measure of the information gain between different views of the same instance. This involves creating a custom estimator using the associability framework from causality and kernel-based methods for non-linear dependencies. We apply ISMIA to analyze the mutual information dynamics of existing contrastive learning methods, such as SimCLR and MoCo, and to inform the design of ALT.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Contrastive Learning with Adaptive View Transformation (ALT)
PROPOSAL: Implement a novel contrastive learning algorithm, ALT, which dynamically adjusts view transformations based on the instance's information gain. Inspired by attention mechanisms, ALT introduces a learnable transformation matrix that controls the adaptability of each view. The model seeks to maximize mutual information between different views and their correspondent augmented versions. We evaluate ALT against state-of-the-art methods like SimCLR and MoCo on benchmark datasets such as ImageNet and CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100.
CONTROLS: SimCLR and MoCo with static augmentations, SimCLR with dynamic augmentations (e.g., RandAugment)
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: ALT is expected to outperform SimCLR and MoCo on ImageNet and CIFAR-100, achieving better representational adaptability and generalization, but may fail in extreme regimes where the adaptive transformation strategy is overly aggressive, losing semantic coherence.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Instance-Specific Mutual Information Analysis (ISMIA)
PROPOSAL: Develop a method to estimate instance-specific mutual information (ISMIA) as a measure of the information gain between different views of the same instance. This involves creating a custom estimator using the associability framework from causality and kernel-based methods for non-linear dependencies. We apply ISMIA to analyze the mutual information dynamics of existing contrastive learning methods, such as SimCLR and MoCo, and to inform the design of ALT.
CONTROLS: State-of-the-art mutual information estimators (e.g., CR Div, MIG), baseline analysis of existing contrastive methods
COST: 2500
PREDICTION: ISMIA will uncover insights into the comparative information gain of different contrastive frameworks and shed light on the dynamic trade-offs between in- and out-of-sample generalization, but may struggle with instances with complex and heterogeneous structures due to the assumptions of the associability framework.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diagnosing Contrastive Learning Divergence
PROPOSAL: Investigate the sensitivity of SimCLR to the distribution of augmented views by computing the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the marginal distributions of each view and the marginal distribution of the input data with the original unperturbed view. This will quantify how far each augmented view is from the unperturbed data distribution, giving insights into the representational capacity and information density of the views.
CONTROLS: Compare with a baseline of random augmentations and ablate parameters of the hard-negative miner.
COST: 10.744
PREDICTION: We expect to see high divergence values for less informative augmentations and a moderate degree of divergence for those that maintain similarity with the original view, but with clusters of much higher divergence values when contrasted with random augmentations; augmentations whose importance goes unmeasured in this work.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hyperparameter Tuning for Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the interplay between hyperparameters and contrastive learning dynamics by performing a comprehensive hyperparameter search over SimCLR's parameters, focusing on temperature, batch size, and momentum. We will utilize a combinations of classical optimization algorithms, evolutionary strategies, and Bayesian optimization to efficiently search for a well-performing hyperparameter configuration.
CONTROLS: Evaluate hyperparameter search results on multiple image classification datasets and compare with existing state-of-the-art results for SimCLR.
COST: 93.312
PREDICTION: Depending on the dataset and evaluation metric, we expect to identify key hyperparameters that yield optimal performance and explore trade-offs between hyperparameters to better understand their respective roles in contrastive learning. However, the best hyperparameters might be overfit to a specific dataset and not generalize well to others.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Contrastive Augmentation Learning (ACAL)
PROPOSAL: Introduce ACAL, a novel framework for adaptively generating augmentations for contrastive learning that balances representation diversity and semantic coherence. ACAL learns to update instance-wise augmentation policies using an on-the-fly information bottleneck principle, ensuring that the model captures diverse yet semantically relevant representations for each instance. Evaluate ACAL on various real-world benchmarks (e.g., ImageNet, CIFAR-10) and compare with state-of-the-art augmentation methods (e.g., SimCLR).
CONTROLS: Compare performance with SimCLR, MoCo, and their variants, as well as ablations to quantify the effect of each design component on ACAL's performance. Evaluate robustness to various regularization techniques (e.g., weight decay, dropout).
COST: 830
PREDICTION: ACAL should achieve state-of-the-art performance on contrastive learning benchmarks, with improved adaptability to instance-wise semantic variability. It may struggle to capture rare, anomalous instances due to its reliance on on-the-fly adaptation.

TITLE: Information-theoretic View Diversification
PROPOSAL: Develop an information-theoretic methodology to automatically determine the optimal number of views (augmentations) for a given instance in a dataset. This methodology uses bounds on the mutual information between views and the latent representation to determine the minimum number of views required to capture the relevant variations in each instance, while avoiding redundant or semantically inconsistent views.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing view selection heuristics (e.g., random sampling, uniform sampling), and evaluate on real-world datasets (e.g., ImageNet, CIFAR-10).
COST: 400
PREDICTION: This approach should provide a principled method for View Diversification, resulting in more efficient use of computational resources and improved performance on contrastive learning benchmarks. It may fail for instances with complex, non-linear semantic relationships between views, requiring many views to fully capture their variability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sparse Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Introduce a sparse contrastive learning framework that seeks to learn a sparse representation of the data by promoting sparsity in the prediction space. This is achieved through a novel loss function that balances the mutual information between views and the prediction probability of the positive class, with an additive term enforcing sparsity in the predictions.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing sparse representation learning methods, as well as sparsity-free contrastive learning baselines. Evaluate on datasets where sparsity naturally emerges (e.g., MNIST, FashionMNIST).
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: This sparse contrastive learning framework should lead to improved representation learning and generalization, particularly in scenarios where explicit sparsity is beneficial (e.g., natural images, sparse datasets). However, it might be difficult to control for the level of sparsity, which could lead to suboptimal performance if not carefully tuned.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Complementarity of Test-Time and Training-Time Adaptation
PROPOSAL: Explore the potential synergy between test-time adaptation (TTA) and training-time fine-tuning (TTF) of VLMs, asking whether TTA can be used to enhance the performance of TTF and vice versa. Specifically, investigate the performance gains from combining episode-based TTA with various TTF strategies (e.g., few-shot learning, generative learning).
CONTROLS: Include ablation studies evaluating TTF strategies alone and in combination with TTA, as well as a no-adaptation baseline.
COST: 1,200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This experiment will reveal that TTA can indeed enhance the performance of TTF, especially when used to augment few-shot learning or generative fine-tuning, but the complementary benefits will depend on the specific VLM architecture and task at hand.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Episodic TTAs on CLIP
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of three popular episodic TTA methods (PAM, Tadam, and SGD+) on the CLIP-ViT-B/32 model using the Conceptual Captions v2 (CC2) validation set. Report accuracy, MAP, and AUC scores for a subset of classes, as well as ROUGE-L scores to evaluate the models' ability to preserve high-level semantics. Conduct a small ablation study on the embedding dimensionality of the fine-tuning process to assess its impact on adaptation quality.

COST: 1020 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: SGD+ is expected to achieve the highest accuracy improvements, with stronger semantic preservation than other methods, around 5-10% relative gains. However, Tadam may diverge more easily on certain items if the adaptation space is poorly conditioned, potentially undermining its robustness.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Unified Framework for Test-Time Adaptation Across Episodic and Online Settings
PROPOSAL: Propose a unified framework that combines the strengths of episodic and online TTA methods, allowing for seamless adaptation to both individual and batched test data. Our framework incorporates a set of dynamic switches to control the flow of adaptation information, allowing the model to adapt to the input data in real-time. We will evaluate the proposed framework on a range of vision-language tasks, including image classification and semantic segmentation, to demonstrate its effectiveness and versatility.
CONTROLS: CLIP-vision RND model without adaptation, episodic and online TTA methods with proposed unified framework
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: The unified framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on both episodic and online tasks, demonstrating its potential for real-world deployment. However, its success may be limited by the computational overhead of dynamic switches, particularly for large models and datasets.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Binarization and Motion Modeling with vid-DiffAugment
PROPOSAL: 
We develop vid-DiffAugment, a novel pre-training method for discrete video tokenizers and autoregressive models. vid-DiffAugment jointly optimizes for token binarization through various techniques such as imposing a 1 bit compressor penalty, through other formulations of expected L0 bit constraints, as well as learning to model displacement from previous frames through a vision-based Euclidean LCD motion layer (to estimate displacement without discernible intensity classification signals using 8 bit depth image)
. Controls include pre-training without vid-DiffAugment as well as with separately trained binarizers and motion models. We demonstrate significant reductions in training cost without much degradation in reconstruction quality. Evaluation on certain video extrapolation challenges will also serve as preliminary tests of the temporal consistency of the motion models as we jointly binarize and learn these spatial and appearance displacements within a single pass. 
COST: 150000
PREDICTION: We expect vid-DiffAugment to significantly shorten training times while preserving movieprop quality and mitigate temporal inconsistency while jointly binarizing and inferring motion on longer short clips like 10 second video clips.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Spatiotemporal Modeling with a Shared Bitfield
PROPOSAL:
We introduce a novel discrete autoregressive model for video generation, which unifies the modeling of spatial and temporal dimensions through a shared bitfield. The model consists of a spatial encoder, a temporal encoder, and a shared bitfield decoder. The spatial encoder processes each frame independently, while the temporal encoder captures the temporal dynamics by attending to the previous frames. The shared bitfield decoder generates a binary representation of the video data, which is used to compute the likelihood of the next token. Our model allows for efficient modeling of both spatial and temporal dimensions and can be optimized using the same training objective.

Controls: 
--trained without shared bitfield
-our approach with separately trained spatial and temporal encoder-decoders as baseline
- Real-world video datasets such as UCF-101 and HMDB-51 for evaluation.

COST: 900,000
PREDICTION: We expect the shared bitfield model to improve the visual quality of the generated videos while reducing the computational cost compared to state-of-the-art methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Long-Term Memory Module for Video Generation
PROPOSAL:
We propose an efficient long-term memory module for video generation, which specifically addresses the issue of maintaining temporal consistency for long-term video generation. Our module consists of a novel hierarchical attention mechanism that selectively attends to the most relevant frames in the long-term memory, allowing our model to efficiently capture temporal dynamics and maintain consistency over time. We also introduce a novel sparse updating mechanism that selectively updates the long-term memory, reducing the computational overhead of updating the entire memory.

Controls: 
- Baseline model with only short-term memory
- Model with the proposed long-term memory module but without sparse updating
- Real-world video datasets such as UCF-101 and HMDB-51 for evaluation
COST: 300,000 
PREDICTION: We expect our efficient long-term memory module to improve the temporal consistency and reduce the computational overhead for long-term video generation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Discrete Video Tokenization with Coarse-to-Fine Coding
PROPOSAL:
We propose a hierarchical discrete video tokenization method with a coarse-to-fine coding scheme. In the coarse coding stage, we use a smaller number of discrete tokens to represent the overall appearance and motion of the video, while in the fine coding stage, we use a larger number of tokens to represent the detailed textures and edges of the video. Our method uses a hierarchical decoder to progressively refine the video representation and achieve high fidelity. We also introduce a novel loss function that encourages the model to learn a sparse and efficient video representation.

Controls: 
- Baseline model with traditional discrete video tokenization
- Model with hierarchical discrete video tokenization but without the coarse-to-fine coding scheme
- Model with a different hierarchical decoding strategy
COST: 1,800,000
PREDICTION: We expect our hierarchical discrete video tokenization method to achieve higher fidelity and efficiency for video generation, while also providing a more interpretable video representation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Agent Framework for Interactive Video Generation
PROPOSAL:
We propose a multi-agent framework for interactive video generation, where each agent is responsible for generating a different aspect of the video (e.g., background, characters, objects). The agents communicate with each other to ensure coherent and realistic video generation. We use reinforcement learning to train the agents to optimize a unified objective function that balances video quality, coherence, and interactivity. Our framework allows for real-time interactive video generation, enabling users to provide feedback and guide the generation process.

Controls: 
- Baseline model with a single agent generating the entire video
- Model with multiple agents but without reinforcement learning
- Model with a different type of interactivity
COST: 3,500,000
PREDICTION: We expect our multi-agent framework to achieve state-of-the-art performance in interactive video generation, while providing a high degree of control and customization for users.

PROPOSAL: Develop a novel discrete video tokenizer by jointly learning from both image and video data. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Consistency via Masked Autoregressive Video Prediction
PROPOSAL: Introduce a masked autoregressive video prediction (MAVP) component to the discrete autoregressive model to capture temporal consistency. In each time step, a fraction of the previous frame's tokens are masked and predicted along with the tokens for the current frame. The model is trained to simultaneously predict the masked tokens while conditioning on the remaining visible tokens. This forces the model to attend to the previously generated content and maintain temporal coherence.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Compare with the model without the MA-VP component, where all tokens are predicted autoregressively.
Baselines 2-3: Evaluate the effect of different masking ratios (e.g., 20% to 50% of tokens masked) and investigate the trade-off between computational cost and consistency.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Observations from experiments suggest that the introduction of the MAVP component improves temporal consistency, reducing the visual artifacts and jitters in videos compared to the baseline, potentially upping those at top-tier diffusion models by 5-10%. Findings might get increasingly unstable for extreme masking ratios (both very high masking, failing coherence, and low masking, failing for competitive speed and enable potential convergence issues).

PROPOSAL: We modify the previously proposed discrete autoregressive model by incorporating a Conditional Masked Transformer module conditioned on the text input. The module predicts a sequence of binary masks, which are then used to condition the autoregressive video synthesis process. This design allows the model to better capture the relationships between text and video, leading to improved video synthesis quality and more faithful text-to-video generation.

PROPOSAL: We will investigate the impact of jointly modeling spatial and temporal scales on discrete video generation. CONTROLS: Our baseline is a state-of-the-art diffusion model specifically designed for video generation tasks, presented by Digital Creations as "DiffS Hadamard".

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of Implication Inference in Open-Domain QA
PROPOSAL: Design a robustness evaluation protocol to assess how well LLMs maintain their implication inference capability in open-domain question answering when faced with unforeseen (out-of-distribution) contexts, entities, or types of implications. Conduct experiments using a realistic and dynamic open-domain QA benchmark, where the test-time context, entities, or implication types differ from those seen during training. Measure robustness using metrics such as inference accuracy, calibration, and break-point thresholds, evaluated on two main settings: (i) transferred inference (e.g., generalizing from related entities) and (ii) zero-shot inference (e.g., applying unobserved implication types).
CONTROLS: Compare the robustness of a state-of-the-art LLM with that of a baseline model with a dedicated implication inference module trained solely on the in-distribution implication data.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: We expect that, even if the model exhibits robust implication inference for a specific group of implications and questions, it might struggle with harder, unseen questions or implications, especially when compositionality and abstraction kick in. However, direct comparison of these robustness evaluations between LLMs and the baseline might show surprising differences depending on their pre-training data and computational complexities.

PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel multitask learning approach to improve implication inference capabilities of LLMs. Propose a dynamic, span-based explicit memory component that actively selects, retrieves, and combines relevant information from the input context to improve the model's generalization and robustness. Incorporate this memory component with an auxiliary learning objective, which, using a binary classification framework, encourages the model to reason about which information in the input is relevant or irrelevant to the implication inference task. Conduct experiments on a range of open-domain QA benchmarks and compare against state-of-the-art models.
CONTROLS: Ablate the different components of the proposed framework, including the explicit memory component and the binary classification objective, to understand their relative contributions to implication inference performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Implication Inference for Compositional Reasoning: A Hierarchy of Explanation Layers
PROPOSAL: Propose a hierarchical explanation framework to facilitate compositional reasoning in implication inference tasks. This framework incorporates multiple explanation layers, each specifically designed to model a particular level of compositional reasoning: (i) atomic reasoning (deductions based on single facts), (ii) intermediate reasoning (deductions based on combinations of facts), and (iii) global reasoning (high-level, context-aware deductions). Each explanation layer will retain explanations from lower layers, enabling the model to track and propagate the reasoning process at multiple scales.
CONTROLS: Compare this hierarchical framework against traditional, flat explanation frameworks and monitor its relative benefits in terms of compositional reasoning, implicational accuracy, and robustness.
COST: 11000
PREDICTION: We expect that this hierarchical explanation framework will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the implication inference process, facilitating the identification of compositional reasoning patterns and potentially leading to improvements in implicational accuracy and robustness. Nonetheless, this framework may require careful initialization and regularization of the model parameters to prevent over-complexity.

TITLE: Investigating the Conditions for Gradient-Based Implication Inference
PROPOSAL: This proposal aims to derive a theoretical understanding of when and how gradient-based training leads a transformer to infer implications for subjects whose implications were never observed. We will provide a formal analysis of the conditions on the training data, model architecture, and optimization algorithms that enable implication inference. Specifically, we will prove that a transformer with a specific structure and sufficient capacity will be able to infer implications if the training data contains sufficient "anchoring" triples (facts that appear in both the training and the testing) and the optimization algorithm is designed to maximize the overlap between the learned representations of related facts.
CONTROLS: We will compare our theoretical results against several ablations, including transformers with different structures, optimization algorithms, and training datasets. We will also compare our results against the state-of-the-art transformer-based models for implication inference.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: Our theoretical results should provide a clear understanding of the conditions under which a transformer can infer implications, but the practical applicability of these results remains to be seen, and further experiments may be needed to confirm our findings.

TITLE: Analyzing Consequences of Knowledge Injection on Out-of-Context Implications
PROPOSAL: Investigate the relationship between fine-tuning for factual knowledge injection and the model's ability to form out-of-context implications using synthetic data. Specifically, we'll experiment with four synthetic datasets: KILT, comprising (s, r, o) triples with synonyms for relations, and an extended version (KILT+) that includes unseen relation types. We'll assess a transformer-XL model, finetuned on each dataset to achieve a satisfactory precision on out-of-context implications. We'll compare results on both datasets, evaluating the precision of unseen implications (.PI) and compare it with an ablated version that was not fine-tuned for the related relation types.
CONTROLS: Ablations: model architecture (e.g., BART, T5), true relation types known while testing (no negative examples for relation pairs).
COST: 576_gpu-hours
PREDICTION: We expect fine-tuning on KILT+ (synthetic with unseen relation types) to outperform fine-tuning on KILT (synthetic with known synonyms) to some extent, but both should outperform the ablated version that was not fine-tuned for related relation pairs. Where it may fail: if fine-tuning doesn't capture enough contextual data leading to hallucination in test time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Gradient Dynamics for Implication Inference
PROPOSAL: Investigate the properties of gradient-based training that enable transformer models to infer implications for subjects whose implications were never observed during training. Specifically, examine how the gradient flow through the model's attention mechanism affects the learning of implication rules, and analyze the role of activation functions, layer norms, and residual connections. Utilize synthetic data and a custom dataset where implication rules are explicitly defined, allowing for controlled experiments and analysis.
CONTROLS: Compare to a baseline where implication rules are learned solely through fact recall, and investigate the effect of varying hyperparameters on implication inference.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the gradient dynamics enable the model to learn implication rules that generalize to unseen subjects, but also introduce noise that can contribute to hallucinations. If the model's ability to generalize implication rules is not robust to hyperparameter choices, this could explain why hallucinations arise even when generalization is observed.

PREDICTION: We expect that introducing regularization will reduce hallucinations, but also decrease the model's ability to generalize implication rules, potentially revealing a fundamental tradeoff between these two desirable properties.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Learning-Based Depth Estimation with Focal Stack Prior
PROPOSAL: Train a U-Net encoder-decoder architecture on KITTI 2015 depth estimation benchmark with focal stack inputs. To incorporate focal stack prior, introduce a learnable semantic similarity module that takes concatenated focus maps across the stack as input, predicting a weight map to emphasize region-specific focus cues. The main goal is to verify whether learning-based DFF benefits from the focal stack prior in mitigating texture-induced artifacts and enhancing overall performance.
CONTROLS: State-of-the-art monocular stereo, and classical stereo methods (SBD, MC-CNN).
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: We expect to outperform current state-of-the-art methods on certain patterns with repeating surface structures while potentially faltering in the presence of strong image gradients from slopes and sharp edges, where texture can become misleading.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Improved Focal Stack Prior for Depth Estimation with Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: Modify proposal 1 to implement multi-task learning for the U-Net, jointly predicting depth maps and all-in-focus images from the focal stack. The all-in-focus image prediction is trained as a regression task using L1 loss, and the learned equivariant representation across the stack is expected to aid focal stack prior. To better handle ambiguous focus responses, introduce a spatial attention mechanism that selectively focuses on the most relevant regions for depth estimation.
CONTROLS: Poly-SDN, PSMNet with focal stack, monocular stereo.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: This setup should improve the joint estimation of depth maps and all-in-focus images and potentially outperform proposal 1 by capitalizing on the learned equivariant representation. However, it might lead to over-smoothing in regions where texture is dominant, making it challenging to distinguish true depth edges.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Robust Depth Estimation from Focal Stack via Focal-aware Attention and Smoothing
PROPOSAL: Modify the Improved Focal Stack Prior (proposed in 1) by incorporating focal-aware attention in the decoder and uncertainty-based smoothing for depth confidence estimation. Focal-aware attention will selectively focus on regions with highest focus confidence, while uncertainty-based smoothing will down-weight ambiguous or uncertain depth predictions, enhancing overall robustness. We aim to improve depth estimation in complex and challenging scenarios.
CONTROLS: Baseline will be the Improved Focal Stack Prior (1), we will also include a variant without focal-aware attention (Test 1), without uncertainty-based smoothing (Test 2), and with only focal-aware attention (Test 3) to study the effects of these two components.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: With the addition of focal-aware attention and uncertainty-based smoothing, the model should achieve better overall performance and robustness, especially in scenarios with low-texture regions, reflective surfaces, and abrupt depth changes. However, it might lead to overly conservative depth predictions in regions with high confidence.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Physics-based Focal Stack Analysis for Uncertainty Estimation
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework to analyze the relationship between focal stack inputs and depth uncertainty. By modeling the physical processes of focusing, we aim to derive a probabilistic representation of the uncertainty associated with each depth prediction. This will be achieved by formulating a Bayesian framework that takes into account the noise model of the camera, the characteristics of the focal stack, and the geometry of the scene. This analysis will be used to guide the development of new uncertainty-aware depth estimation methods.
CONTROLS: Analysis of existing uncertainty estimation methods (e.g., aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty) in the context of focal stack depth estimation.
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: This theoretical framework should provide valuable insights into the relationship between focal stack inputs and depth uncertainty, allowing for more accurate and robust uncertainty estimation. However, it may be challenging to formalize the physical processes of focusing and accurately model the uncertainty associated with each depth prediction.

TITLE: Investigating Learning-Based Depth Estimation with Focal Stack Prior
PROPOSAL: Train a U-Net encoder-decoder architecture on KITTI 2015 depth estimation benchmark with focal stack inputs. To incorporate focal stack prior, introduce a learnable semantic similarity module that takes concatenated focus maps across the stack as input, predicting a weight map to emphasize region-specific focus cues. The main goal is to verify whether learning-based DFF benefits from the focal stack prior in mitigating texture-induced artifacts and enhancing overall performance.
CONTROLS: State-of-the-art monocular stereo, and classical stereo methods (SBD, MC-CNN).
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: We expect to outperform current state-of-the-art methods on certain patterns with repeating surface structures while potentially faltering in the presence of strong image gradients from slopes and sharp edges, where texture can become misleading.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Improved Focal Stack Prior for Depth Estimation with Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: Modify proposal 1 to implement multi-task learning for the U-Net, jointly predicting depth maps and all-in-focus images from the focal stack. The all-in-focus image prediction is trained as a regression task using L1 loss, and the learned equivariant representation across the stack is expected to aid focal stack prior. To better handle ambiguous focus responses, introduce a spatial attention mechanism that selectively focuses on the most relevant regions for depth estimation.
CONTROLS: Poly-SDN, PSMNet with focal stack, monocular stereo.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: This setup should improve the joint estimation of depth maps and all-in-focus images and potentially outperform proposal 1 by capitalizing on the learned equivariant representation. However, it might lead to over-smoothing in regions where texture is dominant, making it challenging to distinguish true depth edges.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Robust Depth Estimation from Focal Stack via Focal-aware Attention and Smoothing
PROPOSAL: Modify the Improved Focal Stack Prior (proposed in 1) by incorporating focal-aware attention in the decoder and uncertainty-based smoothing for depth confidence estimation. Focal-aware attention will selectively focus on regions with highest focus confidence, while uncertainty-based smoothing will down-weight ambiguous or uncertain depth predictions, enhancing overall robustness. We aim to improve depth estimation in complex and challenging scenarios.
CONTROLS: Baseline will be the Improved Focal Stack Prior (1), we will also include a variant without focal-aware attention (Test 1), without uncertainty-based smoothing (Test 2), and with only focal-aware attention (Test 3) to study the effects of these two components.
COST: 16200
PREDICTION: With the addition of focal-aware attention and uncertainty-based smoothing, the model should achieve better overall performance and robustness, especially in scenarios with low-texture regions, reflective surfaces, and abrupt depth changes. However, it might lead to overly conservative depth predictions in regions with high confidence.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Physics-based Focal Stack Analysis for Uncertainty Estimation
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework to analyze the relationship between focal stack inputs and depth uncertainty. By modeling the physical processes of focusing, we aim to derive a probabilistic representation of the uncertainty associated with each depth prediction. This will be achieved by formulating a Bayesian framework that takes into account the noise model of the camera, the characteristics of the focal stack, and the geometry of the scene. This analysis will be used to guide the development of new uncertainty-aware depth estimation methods.
CONTROLS: Analysis of existing uncertainty estimation methods (e.g., aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty) in the context of focal stack depth estimation.
COST: 8100
PREDICTION: This theoretical framework should provide valuable insights into the relationship between focal stack inputs and depth uncertainty, allowing for more accurate and robust uncertainty estimation. However, it may be challenging to formalize the physical processes of focusing and accurately model the uncertainty associated with each depth prediction.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Warp-based Depth Representation: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Focal Stack Warping for Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: Modify the existing proposal (2) to include a comprehensive evaluation of the warp-based depth representation on various scenarios, including scenes with repetitive textures, fine details, and occlusions. We will also investigate the effect of different warping techniques (e.g., linear, non-linear, and multi-scale warping) on the quality of the depth representation. Additionally, we will compare the warp-based depth representation with other state-of-the-art depth estimation methods to assess its effectiveness in different scenarios.
CONTROLS: Comparison will be performed with state-of-the-art methods, including both focal stack depth estimation and non-focal stack depth estimation methods.
COST: 24300
PREDICTION: The warp-based depth representation is expected to perform well in scenes with repetitive textures and fine details, but its effectiveness may be limited in scenarios with occlusions or high levels of distortion. The choice of warping technique will also significantly impact the quality of the depth representation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Monocular-to-Focal-Stack Adaptation for Improved Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: Explore the feasibility of adapting monocular depth estimation models to the focal stack setting, rather than treating the focal stack as a completely new source of information. We will fine-tune a pre-trained monocular depth estimation model on a small subset of focal stack images and evaluate its performance on a variety of scenarios, including scenes with complex texture and occlusions. This adaptation approach can potentially improve the accuracy of depth estimation and mitigate the need for extensive retraining from scratch.
CONTROLS: Comparison will be performed with state-of-the-art focal stack depth estimation methods, as well as the original pre-trained monocular depth estimation model.
COST: 40500
PREDICTION: The adaptation approach may lead to improved performance on certain scenarios, but it might not generalize well to novel scenarios or complex scenes. Additionally, the effectiveness of this approach will depend on the quality of the pre-trained monocular depth estimation model and the size of the focal stack adaptation dataset.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Learning Transferable Knowledge for Focal Stack Depth Estimation via Monocular-to-Focal-Stack Adaptation
PROPOSAL: Modify the existing proposal (4) to incorporate a learning-based approach for adapting monocular depth estimation models to the focal stack setting. We will train a transfer learning model that takes the pre-trained monocular depth estimation model as a feature extractor and fine-tunes its output to better suit the focal stack setting. This will be achieved by adding a novel focal stack branch to the transfer learning model, which will learn to generate focal stack-specific features from the pre-trained features.
CONTROLS: Comparison will be performed with state-of-the-art focal stack depth estimation methods, as well as the original pre-trained monocular depth estimation model and the adaptation approach without the learning-based adaptation (Test 1).
COST: 60750
PREDICTION: The learning-based adaptation approach may lead to improved performance on focal stack depth estimation tasks, especially when combined with the focal stack branch, but it may also introduce additional complexity and overfitting issues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Focal Stack Depth Estimation with Temporal Consistency
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of temporal consistency regularization to improve focal stack depth estimation. We will incorporate a temporal consistency loss into the training process, which will encourage the model to produce depth maps that are consistent across frames of the focal stack. This will be achieved by measuring the similarity between the predicted depth maps at different time steps and adding a loss term to the overall loss function.
CONTROLS: Comparison will be performed with state-of-the-art focal stack depth estimation methods, as well as the model without temporal consistency regularization.
COST: 91020
PREDICTION: The temporal consistency regularization may help to improve the accuracy and robustness of focal stack depth estimation, especially in scenarios with slow-moving objects or scenes with complex texture. However, it may also introduce additional complexity and computational overhead.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Uncertainty Estimation for Focal Stack Depth Estimation via Joint Optimization of Physics-based and Learning-based Models
PROPOSAL: Combine the physics-based focal stack analysis (proposed in 3) with the machine learning-based approach for uncertainty estimation. We will train a joint model that takes the physics-based uncertainty estimates as auxiliary information and optimizes the uncertainty estimation using a multi-task learning setup. This will enable the model to leverage the strengths of both physics-based and learning-based approaches, leading to more accurate and robust uncertainty estimation for focal stack depth estimation.
CONTROLS: Comparison will be performed with state-of-the-art uncertainty estimation methods, as well as the model without joint optimization (Test 1).
COST: 121470
PREDICTION: The joint optimization approach may lead to improved uncertainty estimation performance, especially in scenarios with complex texture or occlusions. However, it may also introduce additional complexity and require significant computational resources.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of Frequency-Domain Features on Focal-Stack Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: Train and compare the performance of two state-of-the-art DFF models: one utilizing frequency-domain contrast and sharpness operators, and the other utilizing phase congruency and local pattern local binary patterns (LP-LBP) derived from the frequency-domain representation of focal-stack images. Evaluate models on the widely-used (but relatively small) NYU-Depth-V2 dataset, which includes diverse scenes with depth discontinuities, and the more recent, large-scale IDD dataset, released under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license.
CONTROLS: Compare against classical DFF techniques that incorporate traditional heuristic focus measures, such as Laplacian-based operators.
COST: 1,700
PREDICTION: The frequency-domain features will significantly improve upon classical DFF models, especially on fine-textured regions and at depth discontinuities, but the exact boundaries and costs of such performance gains are difficult to forecast given the proposed experiment's limited focus on the frequency-domain and the simplified setup (as trained and tested only on NYU-Depth-V2 and IDD, for example, but also the usage of singular DFF backbones).
