ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Vision-Language Detector Adaptation via Adaptive Weight Transfer
PROPOSAL: Inspired by the success of vision-language foundation models, we propose a novel adaptive weight transfer mechanism to adapt the pre-trained weights of a vision-language detector during test time. Instead of fine-tuning the entire model, we adaptively transfer the weights from the source model to the target model based on the similarity of their feature distributions. Specifically, we use a self-supervised learning approach to update the weight transfer policy by minimizing the discrepancy between the feature distributions of the two models. This allows the model to adapt to new domains without significant performance degradation.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate our adaptive weight transfer method in conjunction with CAPP (proposal 1) and compare its performance with baseline one-shot fine-tuning and weighted self-training methods, which either transfer all pre-trained weights or use a fixed weighted average of the source and target models.
COST: 14400
PREDICTION: Our adaptive weight transfer method is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance in terms of test-time adaptation and preserve the pre-trained generalization of the vision-language detector. However, it might be challenging to select an optimal transfer policy, which could impact adaptation performance in certain scenarios.

PROPOSAL: We revise the proposed framework CAPP (Confidence-Aware Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-trained detecTorS) by incorporating attention-weighted confidence scores to re-weight pseudo-labels based on their relevance to the specific region of interest. TITLE: Transferable Classifier Adaptation for Cross-Domain and Cross-Category Test-Time Adaptation
PROPOSAL: We propose a transferable classifier adaptation (TCA) framework that leverages a pre-trained discriminative model to adapt to new domains and categories. TCA consists of a domain-invariant feature extractor and a task-agnostic classifier, allowing it to transfer knowledge across domains and categories. We also introduce a novel adversarial training strategy to improve the transferability of the feature extractor and the classifier.
CONTROLS: We compare TCA with CAPP (revised) and evaluate the performance of both methods on cross-domain and cross-category test-time adaptation tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Detectors with Confidence-Aware Pseudo-Labeling
PROPOSAL: We propose a test-time adaptation (TTA) framework called CAPP (Confidence-Aware Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-trained detecTorS) that leverages pre-trained vision-language detectors to adapt to arbitrary cross-domain and cross-category target data without any access to source data or statistics. In CAPP, a confidence threshold is applied to the pseudo-labels generated during self-training, but instead of discarding uncertain samples, a refinement mechanism is introduced to generate additional pseudo-labels based on a set of confident features. We sample these features from the pre-trained feature space, incorporating both region-of-interest (ROI) and global features. The refined pseudo-labels are then re-introduced into the self-training loop, improving the adaptation outcome.
CONTROLS: We compare CAPP with the baseline self-training-based methods, which either discard uncertain samples or do not generate additional pseudo-labels. We will also investigate the effect of different confidence threshold values on the performance of CAPP.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: CAPP is expected to outperform baseline methods in terms of test-time adaptation performance and to remain robust even when high-quality pseudo-labels are scarce, noisy, or missing altogether for some test samples. However, CAPP might struggle with balancing confidence threshold values, which could lead to either over-refining or under-refining pseudo-labels.

TITLE: Robust Vision-Language Detector Adaptation via Adaptive Weight Transfer
PROPOSAL: Inspired by the success of vision-language foundation models, we propose a novel adaptive weight transfer mechanism to adapt the pre-trained weights of a vision-language detector during test time. Instead of fine-tuning the entire model, we adaptively transfer the weights from the source model to the target model based on the similarity of their feature distributions. Specifically, we use a self-supervised learning approach to update the weight transfer policy by minimizing the discrepancy between the feature distributions of the two models. This allows the model to adapt to new domains without significant performance degradation.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate our adaptive weight transfer method in conjunction with CAPP (proposal 1) and compare its performance with baseline one-shot fine-tuning and weighted self-training methods, which either transfer all pre-trained weights or use a fixed weighted average of the source and target models.
COST: 43200
PREDICTION: Our adaptive weight transfer method is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance in terms of test-time adaptation and preserve the pre-trained generalization of the vision-language detector. However, it might be challenging to select an optimal transfer policy, which could impact adaptation performance in certain scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Adversarial Test-time Adaptation for Vision-Language Detectors
PROPOSAL: Investigate the application of adversarial training to vision-language detectors for test-time adaptation, specifically designing a discriminator to distinguish between aligned and unaligned feature distributions between the pre-trained model and the target domain, and a generator to produce pseudo-labels that fool the discriminator, allowing for online adaptation under arbitrary cross-domain and cross-category scenarios.
CONTROLS: Compare with traditional self-training based methods, and ablate the role of the discriminator and generator components.
COST: 1340 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach could synergistically leverage the strengths of both vision-language detectors and adversarial training, leading to improved detection performance on target data, while avoiding the overfitting issues associated with traditional self-training methods; however, the method's efficacy in cases with noisy target data remains a concern.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Adaptive Weight Pruning for Efficient Test-time Adaptation
PROPOSAL: Explore pruning the pre-trained weights of the vision-language detector during test-time adaptation, conditioning the pruning on the evolving feature distributions in the target domain, to select only the most relevant parameters while preserving the generalization capability of the pre-trained model.
CONTROLS: Compare with applying pruning uniformly across all domains, and evaluate the effect of different pruning schedules on adaptation performance.
COST: 2056 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach could efficiently adapt the pre-trained model to new domains by eliminating less relevant parameters, mitigating overfitting issues, and reducing computational costs; however, determining the optimal pruning schedule and selection criterion remains a significant challenge.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Self-Supervised Test-Time Domain Alignment
PROPOSAL: Develop a self-supervised learning-based approach to align the feature distributions between the pre-trained vision-language detector and the target domain during test-time adaptation, by minimizing a domain confusion loss function that generates plausible examples through data augmentation and variation.
CONTROLS: Compare with traditional unsupervised domain adaptation methods, and ablate the role of different data augmentation strategies on adaptation performance.

PREDICTION: This approach could adapt the pre-trained model to target domains without requiring any labeled data or source statistics, while promoting robustness against noisy samples and missing pseudo-labels; however, fine-tuning task-specific weights might still be necessary, necessitating a trade-off between domain alignment and pre-trained knowledge preservation.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Cascade Pseudo-Labeling for Reliable Test-Time Adaptation
PROPOSAL: Propose a cascade pseudo-labeling framework that generates high-quality pseudo-labels for test images through a sequence of refinement steps, each employing a progressively more stringent confidence threshold and exploiting contextual information from neighboring images.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing pseudo-labeling methods, and evaluate the effect of different refinement strategies on adaptation performance.
COST: 4129 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach could alleviate the issues of incomplete pseudo-labels and noisy samples during test-time adaptation, ensuring more reliable adaptation and improved detection performance; however, determining the optimal cascade configuration and refinement step parameters may be cumbersome.

PREDICTION: This updated approach could more accurately adapt the pre-trained model to new domains by dynamically identifying and adjusting the most relevant parameters, reducing overfitting issues, and preserving the pre-trained model's generalization capability; however, the computational overhead of neural attention and fine-tuning might hinder real-time adaptation in certain scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Vision-Language Detector Adaptation via Localized Weight Tuning
PROPOSAL: Modify the pre-trained vision-language detector (GLIP) to update only the weights of a localized neighborhood of the network, rather than fine-tuning all parameters. This neighborhood is determined by a domain-adaptation indicator that analyzes the feature maps of the target test data in real-time. The localized weight tuning is implemented through a two-stage process: (1) an initial adaptation phase that aligns the source and target feature distributions by adjusting the weights of a small, pre-defined neighborhood; (2) a self-training phase that iteratively updates the model's decision boundary based on pseudo-labels generated from the localized neighborhood.
CONTROLS: Compare to full-parameter fine-tuning and weight pruning techniques, and ablate the localized adaptation approach by fixing the pre-defined neighborhood size and excluding certain types of weight updates.
COST: 12,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should achieve a better trade-off between adaptation performance and generalization capability, while maintaining computational efficiency and reducing the risk of overfitting. However, it may fail if the pre-defined neighborhood size is chosen suboptimally or if the domain-adaptation indicator is not sufficiently effective in identifying the relevant features for adaptation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Confidence Thresholding for Vision-Language Detector Adaptation
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel confidence thresholding mechanism to adapt the threshold based on the estimation of label quality for each test image. This adaptation is achieved through a real-time retraining process that uses the generated pseudo-labels with high confidence as training data and a SSL (Self-Supervised Learning) mechanism that encourages the detector to regularize its prediction for low-confidence papers. By learning to adapt the threshold in an online manner, the TTA model can achieve robust pseudo-label generation even when the accuracy of target data pseudolabels is low.
CONTROLS: Compare to fixed thresholding methods, such as offline learning of the optimal threshold or naive adjustments.
COST: 13,678 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should lead to improved pseudo-label quality and adaptability, and reduce the risk of overfitting or using low-accurate pseudo-labels. However, potential bottlenecks may arise during the real-time retraining process, causing slow adaptation rates or falling back to shabby configurations.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Adaptive Confidence Thresholding for Vision-Language Detector Adaptation
REVISED PROPOSAL: Refine the previous proposal by incorporating an ensemble approach, where multiple pseudo-labeling mechanisms are utilized simultaneously, each using a different confidence threshold. The ensemble-pseudolabels of each mechanism is weighted by an uncertainty-aware weighting strategy to produce a final posterior distribution for pseudo-labels. For efficient runtime, the weighting is determined by a surrogate learner tasked with predicting a pseudo-label quality that corresponds to real-valued uncertainty, that is a task that substantially scales down expert solutions when adutating intelligibility across inputs.
CONTROLS: Compare to a single, fixed-confidence approach, a greedy approach using optimal recall, and removing or using one particular uncertainty-aware weighting strategy as part of the ablation study.

PREDICTION: This ensemble-based method should improve the robustness and accuracy of pseudo-label generation by considering multiple perspectives and learning to prioritize between them. However, it adds complexity and latency, potentially causing inferior detection performance if the surrogate learner or weighting strategy suffer from slow learning or improper weighting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-Agnostic Channel Pruning
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel channel pruning mechanism that selectively prunes domain-sensitive channels of the pre-trained GLIP model, while preserving the domain-agnostic channels. This mechanism first identifies domain-sensitive channels using a novel domain-aware index, and then utilizes an iterative pruning strategy to progressively eliminate the selected channels. By pruning domain-sensitive channels, the model's adaptation process becomes more stable and less prone to overfitting.
CONTROLS: Compare to traditional channel pruning methods, and ablate the effectiveness of the proposed domain-aware index and pruning strategy.

PREDICTION: This domain-agnostic channel pruning method should enable more stable and robust adaptation performance, with reduced risk of overfitting to the target domain. However, the pruning process may lead to decreased overall performance if too many channels are removed or misidentified.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-Time Objectness Masking
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel test-time objectness masking technique that leverages the uncertainty-aware pseudo-labels and the masked pseudo-labels generated by the ensemble-based adaptive confidence thresholding approach. The method first identifies uncertain pixels in the input image using the ensemble's uncertainty estimates and then raises the confidence threshold for masking these pixels. By selectively masking the uncertain pixels, the model focuses on more confident predictions, reducing the impact of noisy or uncertain annotations on the adaptation process.
CONTROLS: Compare to traditional confidence masking approaches and evaluate the effect of the uncertainty-aware masking strategy on adaptation performance.
COST: 24,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This test-time objectness masking method should enable more robust and accurate pseudo-label generation by focusing on confident predictions and reducing the influence of noisy annotations. However, it may lead to overlooking valid object instances if the uncertainty-aware masking strategy is too aggressive.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Vision-Language Detector Adaptation via Localized Weight Tuning
PROPOSAL: Modify the pre-trained vision-language detector (GLIP) to update only the weights of a localized neighborhood of the network, rather than fine-tuning all parameters. This neighborhood is determined by a domain-adaptation indicator that analyzes the feature maps of the target test data in real-time. The localized weight tuning is implemented through a two-stage process: (1) an initial adaptation phase that aligns the source and target feature distributions by adjusting the weights of a small, pre-defined neighborhood; (2) a self-training phase that iteratively updates the model's decision boundary based on pseudo-labels generated from the localized neighborhood.
CONTROLS: Compare to full-parameter fine-tuning and weight pruning techniques, and ablate the localized adaptation approach by fixing the pre-defined neighborhood size and excluding certain types of weight updates.
COST: 36,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should achieve a better trade-off between adaptation performance and generalization capability, while maintaining computational efficiency and reducing the risk of overfitting. However, it may fail if the pre-defined neighborhood size is chosen suboptimally or if the domain-adaptation indicator is not sufficiently effective in identifying the relevant features for adaptation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Confidence Thresholding for Vision-Language Detector Adaptation
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel confidence thresholding mechanism to adapt the threshold based on the estimation of label quality for each test image. This adaptation is achieved through a real-time retraining process that uses the generated pseudo-labels with high confidence as training data and a SSL (Self-Supervised Learning) mechanism that encourages the detector to regularize its prediction for low-confidence papers. By learning to adapt the threshold in an online manner, the TTA model can achieve robust pseudo-label generation even when the accuracy of target data pseudolabels is low.
CONTROLS: Compare to fixed thresholding methods, such as offline learning of the optimal threshold or naive adjustments.
COST: 40,800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should lead to improved pseudo-label quality and adaptability, and reduce the risk of overfitting or using low-accurate pseudo-labels. However, potential bottlenecks may arise during the real-time retraining process, causing slow adaptation rates or falling back to shabby configurations.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Adaptive Confidence Thresholding for Vision-Language Detector Adaptation
REVISED PROPOSAL: Refine the previous proposal by incorporating an ensemble approach, where multiple pseudo-labeling mechanisms are utilized simultaneously, each using a different confidence threshold. The ensemble-pseudolabels of each mechanism is weighted by an uncertainty-aware weighting strategy to produce a final posterior distribution for pseudo-labels. For efficient runtime, the weighting is determined by a surrogate learner tasked with predicting a pseudo-label quality that corresponds to real-valued uncertainty, that is a task that substantially scales down expert solutions when adutating intelligibility across inputs.
CONTROLS: Compare to a single, fixed-confidence approach, a greedy approach using optimal recall, and removing or using one particular uncertainty-aware weighting strategy as part of the ablation study
COST: 58,400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This ensemble-based method should improve the robustness and accuracy of pseudo-label generation by considering multiple perspectives and learning to prioritize between them. However, it adds complexity and latency, potentially causing inferior detection performance if the surrogate learner or weighting strategy suffer from slow learning or improper weighting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-Agnostic Channel Pruning
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel channel pruning mechanism that selectively prunes domain-sensitive channels of the pre-trained GLIP model, while preserving the domain-agnostic channels. This mechanism first identifies domain-sensitive channels using a novel domain-aware index, and then utilizes an iterative pruning strategy to progressively eliminate the selected channels. By pruning domain-sensitive channels, the model's adaptation process becomes more stable and less prone to overfitting.
CONTROLS: Compare to traditional channel pruning methods, and ablate the effectiveness of the proposed domain-aware index and pruning strategy.
COST: 48,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This domain-agnostic channel pruning method should enable more stable and robust adaptation performance, with reduced risk of overfitting to the target domain. However, the pruning process may lead to decreased overall performance if too many channels are removed or misidentified.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Vision-Language Detector Adaptation via Localized Weight Tuning
REVISED PROPOSAL: Incorporate the domain-aggressive pruning mechanism from the previous proposal into the original localized weight tuning framework, so that the feature maps after pruning progressively adjust the pre-defined neighborhood size, strategically tweaking the models reasoning. Perform adaptive channel pruning at every iteration of self-training phase to fine-tune the network and prevent static local minima, or adapt to possible over-specialization originating from domain-specific rerooting found at localized tuning steps.
CONTROLS: (Same controls from original 1, and domain-aggressive pruning control, to present effects of this additional step)
COST: 102,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This revised localized weight tuning method should address the limitations of the original approach by offering more flexible adaptation and promoting better generalization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-Time Objectness Masking
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel test-time objectness masking technique that leverages the uncertainty-aware pseudo-labels and the masked pseudo-labels generated by the ensemble-based adaptive confidence thresholding approach. The method first identifies uncertain pixels in the input image using the ensemble's uncertainty estimates and then raises the confidence threshold for masking these pixels. By selectively masking the uncertain pixels, the model focuses on more confident predictions, reducing the impact of noisy or uncertain annotations on the adaptation process.
CONTROLS: Compare to traditional confidence masking approaches and evaluate the effect of the uncertainty-aware masking strategy on adaptation performance.
COST: 72,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This test-time objectness masking method should enable more robust and accurate pseudo-label generation by focusing on confident predictions and reducing the influence of noisy annotations. However, it may lead to overlooking valid object instances if the uncertainty-aware masking strategy is too aggressive.

This is achieved by jointly learning the pseudo-label weights and uncertainty estimates through a novel end-to-end optimization framework.
CONTROLS: Compare to the previous adaptive confidence thresholding and ablate the effectiveness of the end-to-end optimization framework.
COST: 120,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This revised adaptive confidence thresholding method should further improve the robustness and accuracy of pseudo-label generation by more effectively incorporating uncertainty estimates into the weighting process. However, it may add complexity to the optimization process and increase the risk of overfitting.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Predicting Neural Scaling Laws for Combinatorial Search
PROPOSAL: We will use genetic programming to simulate the evolution of models with a fixed capacity trained on Euclidean traveling salesman problem (TSP) instances with varying numbers of locations. We will produce scaling laws for model performance by measuring the average tour length against the model size, number of generations (effective iteration count), and population size. This experiment will focus on the impact of growing solution spaces on model performance.
CONTROLS: Compare against random search, greedy heuristics, and different variations of genetic programming, such as mutation rates and crossovers.
COST: 100
PREDICTION: We expect an inverse polynomial decrease in average tour length with respect to population size and an exponential improvement with number of generations. However, fixed capacity limitations may hinder further improvements, manifesting as a ceiling effect, and the convergence rate may deteriorate as the solution space grows.

TITLE: Investigating Representation Space Complexity
PROPOSAL: We will generate TSP instances with a fixed number of locations but varying representation space complexities by introducing different types of obstacles (e.g., clusters, grid intersections) and barriers. We will simulate the evolution of models with a fixed capacity trained on these TSP instances and measure their performance in terms of average tour length, convergence rate, and solution quality. By varying the representation space complexity, we will observe how the scaling laws for model performance change in response to growing dimensionality.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline of uniformly distributed locations and against models trained on different neural network architectures (e.g., graph neural networks) that are more or less affected by the obstacles and barriers.

TITLE: Predicting Neural Scaling Laws for Combinatorial Search
PROPOSAL: We will use genetic programming to simulate the evolution of models with a fixed capacity trained on Euclidean traveling salesman problem (TSP) instances with varying numbers of locations. We will produce scaling laws for model performance by measuring the average tour length against the model size, number of generations (effective iteration count), and population size. This experiment will focus on the impact of growing solution spaces on model performance.
CONTROLS: Compare against random search, greedy heuristics, and different variations of genetic programming, such as mutation rates and crossovers.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: We expect an inverse polynomial decrease in average tour length with respect to population size and an exponential improvement with number of generations. However, fixed capacity limitations may hinder further improvements, manifesting as a ceiling effect, and the convergence rate may deteriorate as the solution space grows.

TITLE: Assessing Scaling Laws in Euclidean TSP through Synthetic Datasets

We train our model using a physics-inspired neural network that optimizes the trajectory/ tour length, and measure performance using the scaled TSP instance complexity as a proxy for problem difficulty. We explore the relationship between model capacity, compute budget, and performance on this synthetic benchmark to see if we observe predictable scaling trends.

We also include a simple analyses of the learnable space and examination of the solution phase, i.e., results as a function of parameters in terms of representation space's complexity.

PREDICTION: We expect to observe smooth scaling trends between model capacity, compute budget, and performance, and further research will be needed to understand the underlying mechanisms driving these trends. This task has limited ability to assess the robustness of performance trends across different tasks within a fixed dimensional problem, however.

TITLE: Investigating Neuromorphic Scaling Laws in Route Optimization
PROPOSAL: We use a variant of the Reichardt model as our neural encoder, and generate synthetic Euclidean TSP instances with scalable problem complexity by varying the number of points and their distribution. We train our model using a physics-inspired neural network that optimizes the trajectory/ tour length, and measure performance using the scaled TSP instance complexity as a proxy for problem difficulty. We explore the relationship between model capacity, compute budget, and performance on this synthetic benchmark to see if we observe predictable scaling trends.
CONTROLS: We compare to a standard deep neural network with a Euclidean distance predictor, and ablate by removing the physics-inspired objective from our model. We also include a simple analyses of the learnable space and examination of the solution phase, i.e., results as a function of parameters in terms of representation space's complexity.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: We expect to observe smooth scaling trends between model capacity, compute budget, and performance, and further research will be needed to understand the underlying mechanisms driving these trends. This task has limited ability to assess the robustness of performance trends across different tasks within a fixed dimensional problem, however.

ACTION: ADD

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: 
Investigating the Role of Solution Space Size on the Scaling Laws of Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: 
To begin understanding how the size of the solution space affects neural scaling laws, we will use a simulated version of the Euclidean Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) in which we can systematically vary the solution space size by modifying the number of nodes in the graph. We will use a fixed, medium-sized neural network (e.g., a generative neural network trained with simulated TSP data) and experimentally investigate how its performance degrades as the solution space grows. We will measure performance in terms of the average distance of the generated routes to the optimal route, and analyze how the degradation depends on the capacity of the model and the size of the solution space.
CONTROLS: 
* Baseline: A fixed-size solution space, with the number of nodes held constant.
* Ablation: A range of different neural network architectures, ranging from small to large, to see if differences in model capacity affect the trend.
* Baseline model: pre-trained generative neural network model on simulated TSP data with large solution space.
COST: 3360
PREDICTION: 
As the solution space size increases, the performance degradation should become steeper, due to the increased complexity of the problem, and this should be more pronounced with smaller model capacities. However, it could fail if the neural network is not sufficiently powerful to generalize to the increased solution space size, or if the specific implementation of the machine learning algorithm oscillates badly.

CONTROLS:

* Ablation: Trained on a range of dimensionality values, e.g. from 2 features (node positions) to 10 features (node positions plus connectivity information).

PREDICTION: 
The degradation in performance should become worse as the dimensionality of the representation space increases, due to overfitting and the curse of dimensionality, but differences between training algorithms and model architectures could modify this trend. However, it could fail if even with higher dimensionality the problem is effectively similar to when it has low dimensionality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multilingual Rater on a Multitask backbone
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the efficiency of using a multitask model as a backbone for training a multilingual rater. Specifically, we propose to train a RoBERTa model on a mixture of language translation, text classification, and question answering tasks over a diverse set of languages. The multitask model will serve as a shared feature extractor for our multilingual rater, which will be trained to predict a fine-grained quality score of a given text. We will evaluate this approach using the web-scale corpora as pretraining data and a set of held-out languages as testing domains.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to FineWeb2-HQ, the state-of-the-art model-based data-quality rater, and standard heuristics (e.g., perplexity-based filtering).
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Our multitask backbone-based rater should perform competitively with FineWeb2-HQ on the held-out languages, with potential improvements for languages with scarce annotated datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Validation of Multilingual Quality Judgment
PROPOSAL: We will develop an adversarial validation framework to evaluate the quality of multilingual quality judgments. Specifically, we will use a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to generate negatively correlated paired samples from the pretraining corpus. These pairs consist of a high-quality text and a lower-quality variant of the same text in the same language. We will then train our multilingual rater and FineWeb2-HQ on the paired samples and evaluate their performance on distinguishing between the high-quality and lower-quality text. This framework will help us assess the robustness of quality judgments and identify potential biases.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our multilingual rater and FineWeb2-HQ with and without the adversarial validation framework.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The adversarial validation framework should significantly improve the performance of both our multilingual rater and FineWeb2-HQ on the paired samples, with potential implications for domain robustness.

PROPOSAL: We will enhance the existing adversarial validation framework (Turn 2) to account for linguistic variations and cultural nuances by incorporating a multi-lingual discriminator network. We will integrate this discriminator with the GAN to generate more linguistically and culturally rich negative samples that better mimic the complexities of real web data.
CONTROLS: We will compare the enhanced adversarial validation framework to the original framework (Turn 2).

TITLE: Unsupervised Multilingual Rater Learning from Noisily Labeled Data
PROPOSAL: We propose an unsupervised method for learning a multilingual data quality rater that leverages noisy labels in the form of weak expert judgments (e.g., human judgments with high variance) available for a few languages. Our method, 'WeakOracle ensemble', aggregates noisy judgments from multiple languages using a clustering-based approach, robustifying the collective judgment by sidelining outliers and extreme aggregates. This allows us to leverage noisy judgments in resource-poor settings without requiring large amounts of accurate labels for a particular language. For the experiments, we'll use a noisy label set generated by ensemble disagreement in expert judgments as our negative dataset, and a subset of OH2.5 and Reddit ELI5 as our high-quality dataset for few-shot learning. The goal is to evaluate if the aggregation strategy effectively learns robust and transferable data quality assessments across languages.

TITLE: Uncertainty-Weighted Data Selection with Multitask Learning
PROPOSAL: To mitigate the risk of model-specific biases from over-reliance on a particular LLM and improve the generalizability of the multilingual rater, we propose an uncertainty-weighted data selection approach with multitask learning. Specifically, we'll train a rater on multiple classes of tasks, such as fluency evaluation and factuality assessment, with a meta-learning objective that encourages the model to make reliable judgments across tasks and languages. To reduce the risk of overfitting to a particular task or language, we'll use task- and language- uncertainty as a weight to guide data selection during training and at deployment. For experiments, we'll evaluate the performance of our approach on both the selected datasets and the whole datasets.
CONTROLS: to assess the impact of uncertainty-weighted selection on task adaptation and generalizability, we'll compare our approach with a baseline that selects data based on traditional heuristics, and also compare with the approach that simply uses task-dependent weights based on task-specific accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dual-Task Learning for Efficient Adaption to New Languages
PROPOSAL: We will develop DTLexi, a method that trains a single Multimodal Quality Filter (MQF) on a pair of "pivot" languages (e.g., English and Spanish), using a dataset that includes documents from both languages, and then adapts the model to new target languages by learning to predict an auxiliary "lexicon alignment" signal that captures semantic and linguistic relationships between the pivot and target languages.
CONTROLS: For comparison, we will train MQF on both pivot languages and the target languages separately, as well as a baseline using only self-supervised monolingual training data.
COST: 360 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: DTLexi will outperform the separate training approach for MQF on the pivot languages, and show potential for adaptation to new languages, demonstrating its feasibility and effectiveness in supporting low-resourced and multilingual scenarios. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leveraging Domain Knowledge for Quality Control
PROPOSAL: We propose to integrate domain-specific expertise into the MQF framework to enhance quality control. This will be achieved by using a prompt-based approach to elicit ratings from experts in various domains (e.g., medicine, law, finance), incorporating domain-specific knowledge graphs (KG) into the MQF architecture to provide richer context and relationships for quality judgment, and developing a novel contextual evaluation metric, CKG-Score, that combines expert ratings and KG information.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of MQF with and without domain-specific knowledge graph and the standard FastText classifier, which uses only general domain knowledge.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: MQF with domain knowledge and CKG-Score will exhibit significant improvement over MQF without domain knowledge and FastText in terms of quality assessment accuracy and adaptability to expert evaluations, thereby providing more robust and reliable quality assessments, especially in low-resource and high-stakes settings. However, training and maintaining such a system could require extensive domain-specific expertise, which may be difficult to scale.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multilingual Rater Training with Contrastive Adaptive Pretraining
PROPOSAL: Train a multilingual quality rater using a contrastive adaptive pretraining (CAP) framework, leveraging a multilingual task corpus and a set of domain-specific datasets as positive and negative supervision, respectively. The goal is to adapt the rater to a diverse set of candidate documents through self-supervised learning.
CONTROLS: Compare with FineWeb2-HQ and a randomly initialized model, with Ablation studies on different pretraining objectives (contrastive vs. masked language modeling) and document sampling strategies (uniform vs. language-aware).
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Improvements over FineWeb2-HQ in terms of rater adaptation efficiency, robustness to domain shifts, and inference time, while maintaining competitive quality assessment performance; However, adjustments for document length might lead to biased evaluation outcomes.

TITLE: Unsupervised Zero-Shot Generalization for Multilingual Quality Assessment
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of a multilingual encoder-decoder architecture, pre-trained with a cross-lingual dictionary learning objective, for zero-shot quality assessment across languages. This model learns to map documents to quality scores without explicit supervision, promoting language-agnostic quality evaluation.
CONTROLS: Compare with a multilingual rater trained on a similar dataset, as well as a set of language-specific raters for each language in the test set.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning for Low-Resource Language Rater Adaptation
PROPOSAL: Develop a meta-learning framework for adapting multilingual raters to low-resource languages with limited training data. This approach involves pre-training the rater on a set of surrogate languages and fine-tuning on the target language, with the goal of efficient transfer and robust quality assessment in unseen languages.
CONTROLS: Compare with domain-specific adaptation approaches, as well as transfer learning methods using intermediate languages as proxies for the target language.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The meta-learning framework adapts efficiently across a range of languages with varying levels of training data, outperforming conventional fine-tuning methods; However, adaptation may degrade for extremely low-resource languages, requiring additional regularization or generalized forms of inductive bias.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Human Evals of Voxel FML Versus PointDistribution Fields for Real-World 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: 
Use real-world 3D benchmarks (e.g., Stanford 3D Scanning Repository, ShapeNetCore) and conduct a human-evaluation study to compare the shape and view-dependent appearance quality of outputs from two recent 3D generative models: a grid-based FlexModularLatent (FML) model that captures view-dependent appearance and a point- distribution field (PDF) model that only captures geometry. The evaluation will use noise-robust metrics like DIC-CRFR (Drafting-Invariant Chamfer RECommender Flat-Right Rectified) objective and a human judgement score for visual fidelity. 
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Scores from a recent PDF-only 3D reconstruction model.
- Baseline 2: Scores from a recent FML variant that uses synthetic data and not real-world images as input.
- Ablation: FML model outputs without color-info; FML model outputs without incorporating view-dependent normals.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: 
We anticipate FML outputs to significantly outperform PDF model outputs in terms of view-dependent appearance quality due to its ability to include captures of color, normals, and other factors impinging on surface depiction such as material specular.

TITLE: Optimizing Viewpoint Diverse Active Sampling for Efficient Training of Grid FMLs on Real-World Data
PROPOSAL: 
Propose an optimization strategy to improve the efficiency of training grid-based FMLs (FlexModularLatents) on real-world 3D reconstruction data by methodically reducing the number of ground-truth views sampled for each object while preserving their viewpoint diversity. The strategy incorporates autoGM,MCTS (guided Monte Carlo Tree Search) to search for near-optimal sets and combines these active samples using pseudo-inverse L2 minimization to minimize the view-dependent information that would be missed.

- Ablation: Two variants of the optimization strategy relying on experimentally known active sampling criteria (similar to recent JSegM Retrieval methods) and  greedy random sampling.

PREDICTION: 
Removing redundant views without adequate POV change will decrease memory efficiency but a properly conducted reward model using pseudo-inverse L(2) least-squares regression should keep preservation high with contention limitation and causal optimization finished well within interactive time if question MPC overhead constraints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Transfer Learning for Grid FMLs on New Datasets
PROPOSAL: 
In this proposal, we explore the use of transfer learning for grid-based FMLs (FlexModular Latents) on new, unseen 3D reconstruction datasets. We aim to investigate how pre-training FMLs on a large, diverse dataset (e.g., ShapeNet or LF-M.INSTANCE) can improve their performance on a new, smaller dataset with different characteristics. Our goal is to identify the types of pre-training tasks and architectures that lead to the best transfer learning results, as well as to evaluate the impact of transfer learning on FML performance in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and robustness.
CONTROLS: 
- Baselines: Current FML training procedures without pre-training
- Ablations: Pre-training FMLs on a smaller dataset vs. a larger dataset; pre-training with different types of tasks (e.g., geometric reconstruction, appearance completion)
COST: 500
PREDICTION: 
We anticipate that pre-training FMLs on a large dataset will improve their performance on a new dataset, particularly for tasks that require accurate geometric reconstruction and view-dependent appearance modeling. However, the effectiveness of transfer learning may vary depending on the specific dataset and task, and further analysis is needed to identify the optimal pre-training strategies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Transfer Learning for Grid FMLs on New Datasets
PROPOSAL: 
In this proposal, we explore the use of transfer learning for grid-based FMLs (FlexModular Latents) on new, unseen 3D reconstruction datasets. We aim to investigate how pre-training FMLs on a large, diverse dataset (e.g., ShapeNet or LF-M.INSTANCE) can improve their performance on a new, smaller dataset with different characteristics. Our goal is to identify the types of pre-training tasks and architectures that lead to the best transfer learning results, as well as to evaluate the impact of transfer learning on FML performance in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and robustness.
CONTROLS: 
- Baselines: Current FML training procedures without pre-training
- Ablations: Pre-training FMLs on a smaller dataset vs. a larger dataset; pre-training with different types of tasks (e.g., geometric reconstruction, appearance completion)
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: 
We anticipate that pre-training FMLs on a large dataset will improve their performance on a new dataset, particularly for tasks that require accurate geometric reconstruction and view-dependent appearance modeling. However, the effectiveness of transfer learning may vary depending on the specific dataset and task, and further analysis is needed to identify the optimal pre-training strategies.

TITLE: Evaluating Signed Distance Functions for Geometry and View-Dependent Appearance
PROPOSAL: We'll experimentally investigate whether learned signed distance functions (SDFs) can capture both 3D geometry and view-dependent appearance by comparing their performance on chairs from the ShapeNet dataset with that of geometry-only SDFs. We will fine-tune a pre-trained occupancy network as our baseline SDF model, and compare its performance to that of our view-dependent appearance-aware SDF model which we'll train jointly on images sampled along rays and occupancy density estimates.
CONTROLS: Baseline SDF model without view-dependent appearance awareness and without view-dependent direction; ablated SDF model where our view-dependent appearance component is disabled
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our results could show that geometry-only models are matched in terms of geometric accuracy, while offering better quality view-dependent appearance - or, surprisingly, poor results due to over-complicating standard SDF learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Importance of Material Properties and Multi-View Input in 3D Object Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Given recent multi-view models' ability to reconstruct objects from a set of views, we consider controlled experiments evaluating the effect of including material properties and multi-view features when training. Specifically, we compare reconstruction quality on a dataset (e.g. ShapeNet) of objects with varying material properties (e.g., metal, wood, glass) under different input conditions: (1) multi-view RGB images w/ material properties as inputs, (2) single RGB image as input with no material properties, (3) model without material properties trained on multi-view images only. We expect the results will indicate clear improvements of jointly modeling material properties and features from multiple views, and those will have particularly positive effects on capturing appearance and rendering realistic reflections and highlights.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline model trained only on RGB images without material properties, (2) model trained with material properties but without additional multi-view features.
COST: 25000
PREDICTION: Our evaluation demonstrates improved geometric and appearance fidelity through incorporating material properties and features from multiple views, however, potential limitations arise from evident trade-offs in terms of difficulty in obtaining data with accurate material annotations, as it could cause inconsistent model training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conditional Generation of 3D Objects from Single Images using View-Dependent Appearance Models
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims at testing the potential of the proposed view-dependent appearance models for generating 3D objects from a single image, where the input image indicates a specific view of the object. To achieve this, we propose a conditional generative model that combines our earlier work on multi-view perspective fields with a foundation vision model-conditioned on the input image's layout and viewpoint. This will allow us to refine object posing and appearance, given an input image, while still accurately capturing the underlying 3D geometry. TITLE: Evaluating Generalization of View-Dependent 3D Appearance Models to Novel Environments
PROPOSAL: To assess the generalizability of our view-dependent 3D appearance models, we will evaluate their performance on objects from new environments and lighting conditions. We expect that this step will provide valuable insights into the adaptability and robustness of our view-dependent appearance models and contribute to the development of more reliable and practical 3D reconstruction methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Perspective Fields for View-Dependent Illumination and Reflections
PROPOSAL: To extend our previous work on multi-view perspective fields, we propose to incorporate view-dependent illumination and reflections into our model. We will use a variant of the perspective field architecture that includes a separate branch for modeling illumination and reflections, conditioned on the input images and the object's 3D geometry. This will enable our model to capture subtle changes in appearance due to lighting conditions and material properties. We expect this extension to improve the overall fidelity of our 3D appearance models and better capture realistic renderings of objects in different environments.
CONTROLS: (1) baseline: standard view-invariant geometry model with no illumination/reflection handling, (2) ablation study to determine contributions of individual components.
COST: 67200
PREDICTION: By incorporating view-dependent illumination and reflections, we expect to see significant improvements in the realism of our 3D appearance models, but challenges may arise in terms of accurately modeling complex lighting effects and material properties.

However, potential challenges may arise in optimizing the nesting schedule and ensuring consistent quality across different scene compositions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Multiview 3D Reassembly via Image-to-3D Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Develop an image-to-3D diffusion model capable of learning a probabilistic reconstruction of a 3D object from multiple input images taken from different viewpoints. The model will learn to diffuse the input images through learned noising, aligning them with a prior distribution of possible 3D object configurations. This will enable a probabilistic object reassembly from input images, given by a collection of multi-view images in RGB color.
CONTROLS: Direct Comparison: baseline methods for multiview 3D reconstruction like Active Appearance Models and StyleGAN; evaluation of the reconstruction quality, consistency, and accuracy of generated 3D models.
CONTROLS: ablation study on the impact of different diffusion processes and architectures on performance and ease of training.
COST: 1668.75
PREDICTION: The real-world multiview 3D reassembly via image-to-3D diffusion model will demonstrate the capacity to generate accurate, detailed, and robust 3D reconstructions from partial and possibly noisy input images.

TITLE: Flexible 3D Volumetric Representation with Neural-Encoded Sign Distance Functions
PROPOSAL: Modify the previous proposal by replacing neural-encoded sign distance functions with a more practical implementation, specifically using a neural normal encoder to capture geometry and appearance information in a shared latent space. This approach enables more efficient training and inference, as it avoids the need for high-precision distance field computations. The model will be trained on the PartNet dataset, which consists of 43,495 objects with rich annotations, including 3D meshes, images, and semantic labels.

CONTROLS: ablation study on the impact of using occupied grids vs. grid-based occupancy probabilities as inputs to the neural normal encoder.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: View-DependentLatent Learning with Neural Occupancy Fields
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel latent 3D representation that learns to jointly capture an object's geometry and appearance using a neural occupancy field. The neural occupancy field is defined as a set of learned occupancy values at a grid of points, which allow us to render images of the object from different viewpoints and lighting conditions. To extend this to capturing view-dependent effects, we use a neural material properties network that outputs the diffuse albedo, metallic, and roughness values at each point. The occupancy and material properties networks are trained together to minimize the difference between rendered images and input images.
CONTROLS: Grid-based latent, conventional 3D representation ( Occupancy or Signed Distance Field ), Prior Occupancy Networks
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Expected result: state-of-the-art performance on real-world benchmarks with strong view-dependent effects and good geometric accuracy. Potential failure: high memory requirement for training due to large neural occupancy field, could be mitigated with more efficient architecture.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Roto-Oriented Latent Representation Learning for Dynamic Scenes
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel latent representation that learns to capture 3D geometry and appearance in dynamic scenes by using a roto-oriented latent representation. This representation embeds rotational symmetry in the latent space, allowing for efficient learning of object structure and appearance across a wide range of viewpoints and lighting conditions. We introduce a new dataset of videos of objects undergoing dynamic transformations, and train a model to predict the latent representation from a sequence of images.
CONTROLS: Geometry-only latent, conventional 3D reconstruction methods (Iterative Closest Point, NHD ), Dynamic occupancy grid
COST: 1265.6
PREDICTION: Expected result: state-of-the-art performance on dynamic scene reconstruction with strong rotational symmetry and good appearance capture. Potential failure: might miss out on subtle changes in appearance due to dynamic transformation.

TITLE: neurOSF: Neural Signed Distance Field with Material Encoding
PROPOSAL: We propose a variation of the signed distance field representation that incorporates material properties through a neural encoding. This is achieved by training a neural network to predict material properties such as albedo, metallic, and roughness directly from the signed distance field. We use a NOR map to encode material information and add it to the SF representation to capture both geometry and view-dependent appearance.
CONTROLS: Material encoding Signed Distance Field, Geometry-only latent, conventional 3D representation ( Occupancy or Signed Distance Field )
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Expected result: significant improvement in material encoding compared to prior work and good performance on geometry-only benchmarks. Potential failure: might struggle with learning complex materials and appearances.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: neurOSF: Neural Signed Distance Field with Material Encoding
PROPOSAL: We propose a variation of the signed distance field representation that incorporates material properties through a neural encoding. This is achieved by training a neural network to predict material properties such as albedo, metallic, and roughness directly from the signed distance field. We use a NOR map to encode material information and add it to the SF representation to capture both geometry and view-dependent appearance.

This is motivated by the observation that high-frequency details in the occupancy field correspond to low-resolution textures in the image. The occupancy network is trained to predict a multi-resolution occupancy field, which is then used to render images at different scales.

This allows the model to capture more accurate view-dependent effects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding the Conditional Flow of Vector Quantization in Image Autoregressive Models
PROPOSAL: Experimentally investigate the flow of information through vector quantization (VQ) in image AR models by visualizing and analyzing the movement of points in the codebook embedding space during flow matching. This will help understand the challenges in learning the mapping from noise to data tokens.
CONTROLS: Compare to flow matching in DD1, and analyze the impact of VQ on the conditional flow.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: We expect to see a complex, non-linear flow that may explain the difficulties in learning the mapping, and possible issues with information loss or alteration. However, the precise nature of this flow and its effects remains unclear, and further investigation is needed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direct Flow Mapping
PROPOSAL: Investigate a new method called Direct Flow Mapping, which learns the mapping from noise to data tokens directly from the teacher AR model's output distribution without relying on flow matching or a predefined token order. This is achieved by using a neural network that takes the noise token and a conditioning vector of the previous tokens to output the corresponding data token, directly optimizing the log-likelihood of the sequence.
CONTROLS: Compare to DD1 and set prediction, and evaluate the impact of conditioning vector size and noise token dimensionality on performance.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: We expect Direct Flow Mapping to achieve competitive performance with DD1, possibly with less computational overhead, but it may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to avoid performance degradation.

ACTION: REVISE 1. Understanding the Conditional Flow of Vector Quantization in Image Autoregressive Models
TITLE: Conditional Flow Analysis with VQ-VAE
PROPOSAL: Adapt the analysis of the conditional flow to VQ-VAE (Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder) architecture, which uses a similar VQ mechanism but with a different latent space structure and objective. This will help to better understand how the VQ process impacts the conditional probability distribution and the generator's performance.
CONTROLS: Compare the movement of points in the VQ codebook embedding space and the magnitude of the probability mass assigned to each token to the VQ-VAE model, and analyze the impact of VQ on the conditional probability distribution of the VQ-VAE model.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: We expect to see similar results to the original analysis, but with some differences due to the different architecture and objective of the VQ-VAE model.

(new) ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leakage and Information Loss in One-Step Generators
PROPOSAL: Investigate the phenomenon of leakage and information loss in one-step generators, where the generator fails to reproduce the input information due to the sequential nature of the autoregressive model and the discrete VQ mechanism. This will help to better understand the limitations of the one-step generators and develop strategies to mitigate them.
CONTROLS: Measure the leakage and information loss using metrics that quantify the difference between the input and output information, and analyze the impact of different architectures, VQ mechanisms, and generator training procedures on leakage and information loss.
COST: 63000
PREDICTION: We expect to see significant leakage and information loss in one-step generators due to the sequential nature of the autoregressive model and the discrete VQ mechanism, and some improvement with the use of intermediate tokens or other techniques to mitigate these effects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Emulating Sequential Conditional Likelihood
PROPOSAL: Develop a one-step generator that models the conditional likelihood of a fixed-length token sequence as a single bijection, parameterized by a neural network, from a learned random noise vector to the token sequence, with the goal of emulating the sequential conditional likelihood of the teacher AR model. To this end, use a neural network to transform the noise vector into a sequence of intermediate representations, then with shared weights and a shared random noise vector, recalculate each intermediate representation in order to generate the final token sequence directly, so that each position's output is conditioned on the conditionals provided by the teacher AR model.
CONTROLS: Train a baseline one-step generator to map the noise vector to the token sequence directly without conditional information, and compare with the proposed method using the teacher AR model's sequential conditional likelihood as a proxy for evaluation.
COST: 408000
PREDICTION: The proposed one-step generator with conditional information should show improved overall generation quality and coverage of the sample space compared to the baseline method, and there may be some trade-off between the quality of generated sequences and the number of trainable parameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Regularization for One-Step Generation
PROPOSAL: To regularize the one-step generator and improve its ability to generate samples that match the distribution of the teacher AR model, incorporate an adversarial loss into the learning objective of the generator, where an additional discriminator network is trained to distinguish between real token sequences (drawn from the teacher AR model) and fake token sequences generated by the one-step generator, and the adversarial loss term is optimized in conjunction with the standard maximum likelihood loss of the generator.
CONTROLS: Train the baseline method without adversarial regularization (proposal 1 with its own baseline), and compare with the method that incorporates the adversarial loss term.
COST: 80000
PREDICTION: The proposed method with adversarial regularization should demonstrate significant improvement over the baseline one-step generator, and the discriminator network should become increasingly skilled at distinguishing between real and fake token sequences as training progresses. However, over-regularization or choosing a discriminator with too much capacity may impair the generator's ability to capture complex patterns in the data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Whether the Conditional Independence of AR Model Tokens Affects One-Step Sampling
PROPOSAL: We analyze the conditional independence properties of autoregressive (AR) model tokens by deriving a closed-form expression for the joint distribution of two tokens, p(q_i, q_j | q_<i)) using the teacher AR model. Specifically, we assume the token sequence is generated as yi ~ p(y_i | y_<i), with y_i being a feature vector in the codebook space. We use the chain rule to factorize the joint probability p(y_i, y_j) = p(y_j | y_i) * p(y_i).
CONTROLS: Baseline includes an experiment with a teacher AR model that fails to enforce conditional independence, such as GRAF (General Autoregressive Flow).
COST: 2880
PREDICTION: If conditional independence holds true, it might imply an inherent limit on the achievable compression of one-step sampling, i.e., that the number of necessary sampling steps for high-quality generation is related to the number of tokens in the sequence. Experimental validation with a VQ-VAE (Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder) and open-source implementations of AR models on various real-world datasets, including large object categories images.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does Practical Initialization Boost the One-Step Generator's Performance?
PROPOSAL: We investigate incorporating practical initialization techniques for the one-step generator, borrowing from those used in Natural Language Processing and primarily inspired by those used for Transformers, to see if it leads to improved quality in the generated sequence. This includes attention initialization by pre-training an auxiliary model that predicts the density of the next token, and we use gradient perpendicularity to give prior similarity in token replacements.
CONTROLS: We compare the baseline results with and without these initialization techniques, as well as evaluate their effect on the generator's robustness to overfitting and computational complexity.
COST: 7800.95
PREDICTION: Our practical initialization approach should improve performance on certain image quality metrics and resulting in reduction of computation time on larger datasets. One shortcoming is the possible performance drop in terms of complicated cases that require more adaptable learning process.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Does Practical Initialization Boost the One-Step Generator's Performance?
PROPOSAL: We augment the practical initialization techniques for the one-step generator to account for real-world imperfections and asymmetries in real image datasets. For example, instead of using a uniform distribution for prior initialization, we analyze if initializing with a more structured prior, such as a prior learned from natural image statistics, can significantly boost the generator's performance. Also, to surpass the model's sensitivity in local information and high-level semantic details, we introduce regional fingerprint to purely attribute steadfast initialization on delineating trained vocabs relative to noise vocabs that facilitate getting generating spaces reach real recovery.
CONTROLS: Similar to previous version, we compare baseline results with and without these initialization techniques, and evaluate their effect on the generator's robustness to overfitting, training speed and local error minimization.
COST: 15552
PREDICTION: With these updates, we anticipate that our generator can outperform the state-of-the-art models and achieve higher image quality metrics, assuming some unforeseen phenomena do not trap the improved initialization methods into suboptimal convergence. Failure might revolve around issues of degradation in conditioning to stratified noise regimes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning a Conditional Affine Transformation to Match Teacher AR Outputs
PROPOSAL: Train a one-step generator using a feedforward neural network that learns a conditional affine transformation to match the output of each position of the teacher AR model, p(q_i | q_<i). The generator maps a noise vector drawn from a prior distribution to the sequence of conditionals, conditioned on all previous conditionals. This is similar to flow matching used in DD1, but instead of relying on matching in the embedding space, we directly learn the transformation in the output probability space.
CONTROLS: Train and evaluate on the same datasets as DD1, using the same AR model as teacher.
COST: 420 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the generator to achieve similar performance to DD1 in terms of output quality, but with faster training, since it directly learns the transformation and does not require inference in the codebook space. However, it may struggle with capturing complex dependencies between conditionals, which is a challenge for this approach.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Euler Method for SDE-Based Generators
PROPOSAL: We propose to use a stochastic differential equation (SDE) as a basis for the generator, similar to the recent stochastic diffusion model. However, instead of discretizing the SDE using a standard Euler method with a small step size, we propose an efficient Euler method that can speed up the computation while maintaining the accuracy of the SDE-based generator. This method involves using a first-order Taylor expansion of the SDE around the current state, and then taking a larger step size to reach the next state. By doing so, we can achieve faster computation while maintaining the same level of stability and accuracy.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the efficient Euler method with the standard Euler method and other SDE-based generators, and evaluate the trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency.
COST: 1,331.09 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the efficient Euler method to achieve significant speedup while maintaining the accuracy of the SDE-based generator, but may see a slight reduction in performance due to the larger step size. However, the benefits of faster computation and smaller memory usage may outweigh the slight degradation in performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Structured Routing via Route-Guided Routing Loss
PROPOSAL: We design a new routing loss function, route-guided routing loss, which encourages the global batch diversity of the routing distribution to match the desired functional specialization pattern of the experts. This pattern is specified using an additional mask vector that rewards routing to experts who are most relevant to the current input tokens. In the experiment, we compare the route-guided routing loss with the standard routing loss and the extra-load balancing loss computed globally.
CONTROLS: (1) the standard routing loss and the extra-load balancing loss computed globally, (2) the route-guided routing loss without the mask vector for comparison on what extent the loss guides the specialized routing.
COST: 288000
PREDICTION: We expect to see that experts in the route-guided routing loss model show a better separation of their data distributions, i.e., reduce the overlap between experts, and more closely align with the desired function specialization pattern, comparing with the standard routing loss alone or the extra-load balancing loss. However, when the mask vector is not well designed, it might fail to guide the model in the desired direction, introducing more noise than signal, affecting model performance negatively.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Integrating Orthogonality Regularization with Route-Guided Routing Loss
PROPOSAL: We combine the route-guided routing loss with an orthogonality regularization term on the router's weight matrix, encouraging the linear combinations of experts to have well-separated subspaces, and hence facilitating more effective routing. This orthogonality regularization extends the benefits of the route-guided routing loss, making the experts more specialized and improve collaboration among them.
CONTROLS: (1) the routing model with route-guided routing loss alone, (2) the model with standard routing loss and orthogonality regularization only, (3) the combination of standard routing loss with orthogonality regularization and the route-guided routing loss.
COST: 430800
PREDICTION: We expect this combination of route-guided routing loss and orthogonality regularization to lead to even more efficient expert specialization, improved generalization performance, and robustness to routing noise, while maintaining the routing efficiency brought by MoE. However, directly applying orthogonality regularization could also add computational overhead to the model, affecting its scalability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert Curriculum Learning for Specialized Routing
PROPOSAL: We propose an expert curriculum learning approach, where the model is first trained on a subset of the data to encourage the formation of a primary set of well-specialized experts. Then, on top of the existing MoE training, we incorporate an extra learning phase with an enlarged dataset and mask targets that encourage experts to select from a subword vocabulary, forcing routing to focus on the exact subword tokens and leading to finer-grained functionalities among experts.
CONTROLS: (1) models trained with route-guided routing loss and orthogonality regularization for comparison, (2) the standard MoE model with global load balancing constraint only.
COST: 600000
PREDICTION: This experiment aims to verify that expert curriculum learning helps MoE better discover specialized routing patterns and improve overall generalization performance. However, this two-stage training procedure may increase training time and can lead to potential step-loss in downstream performance if the routing guidance they apply leads to an overfitting result for this expanded routing space in the second learning step.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ladder-Free Decoupled Routing for Scalable Pre-training and Transfer
PROPOSAL: We propose a ladder-free decoupled routing (DFR) method that decouples the routing matrix from the expert weights, allowing for more flexible and scalable pre-training and transfer learning. By treating the routing matrix as a hyperparameter, we introduce an additional criterion to avoid weight differences between routes, resulting in improved routing efficiency and fine-grained expert specialization. This method retains the routing benefits of the original MoE while reducing the constraints imposed by the ladder.
CONTROLS: (1) original MoE model with ladder-based routing, (2) ladder-free models, (3) models with pairwise-weight rerouting analysis for validation of search selection etc more areas loss unrecover pouñ rend.
COST: 830000
PREDICTION: Ladder-free decoupled routing eliminates the computational overhead and unnecessary constraints of the ladder, resulting in more efficient routing and improved generalization. However, the main challenge will be ensuring that the additional decoupling criterion does not over-restrict or under-restrict routing assignments when dealing with flexible pre-trained models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-GPU Training and Hierarchical Routing for Scaling-Up MoE
PROPOSAL: We explore the extension of our proposed methods to multi-GPU training and hierarchical routing configurations to achieve even larger MoE models. By decentralizing the routing computation and optimizing the inter-router communication, we demonstrate that our approaches can be effectively scaled up to utilize large numbers of GPUs, enabling the training of significantly larger and more complex MoE models than ever before.
CONTROLS: (1) standard multi-GPU training and routing model without our extensions, (2) evaluation of various inter-router communication strategies, (3) exploration of additional hierarchical routing topologies.
COST: 1296000
PREDICTION: Successful large-scale MoE model training with our methods should achieve state-of-the-art performance in various language modeling and downstream tasks while maintaining the efficiency benefits of the MoE architecture. However, optimizing these large models on a distributed computing environment and preventing packet loss among large data transfers will introduce significant computational and theoretical challenges that may necessitate future research.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned Routing Objective for Mixture-of-Experts
PROPOSAL: We propose an experiment where we replace the standard load-balancing loss for MoE models with a learned routing objective. This latent objective is learned end-to-end from the language modeling loss and the routing policy, such that the MoE model can infer a soft routing alignment with respect to the input data distribution. Specifically, we use a hypernetwork to predict the load-balancing loss on-the-fly for every mini-batch. This is implemented on top of the fair Moisture-of-Experts model.
CONTROLS: We compare against three baselines: 1) the vanilla Moisture-of-Experts model, 2) a model with a uniform routing policy to essentially ablate the routing mechanism, and 3) a model that uses a pre-defined routing alignment, which we use as a proxy to compare with our learned routing objective. 
COST: 13310.9
PREDICTION: We expect our learned routing objective to guide MoE models towards more structured routing diversity and effective specialization among experts, leading to better performance in both language modeling and downstream tasks. However, this may fail for very small datasets where the data distribution is too simple to support complex routing alignments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Progressive Routing Alignment for Mixture-of-Experts
PROPOSAL: We propose an experiment where we incorporate a progressive routing alignment mechanism into the MoE model training process. This involves adding a scalar weight to the routing policy at every training iteration, starting from a uniform distribution, to gradually introduce routing diversity and allow experts to specialize progressively over the course of training. Specifically, we use a variant of the fair Moisture-of-Experts model that incorporates this progressive alignment into its design.
CONTROLS: We compare against two baselines: 1) the vanilla fair Moisture-of-Experts model, and 2) a model with a fixed routing alignment from early training iterations. 
COST: 17700
PREDICTION: We expect our progressive routing alignment to foster more effective expert specialization and improve language modeling performance as training progresses, particularly for longer sequences or those with complex structures. However, this may fail if the progressive alignment becomes too aggressive, causing the routing policy to become stuck in a suboptimal state.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pairwise Expert Regularization for Mixture-of-Experts
PROPOSAL: We propose an experiment where we introduce pairwise regularization terms between experts to promote orthogonality and diversity in their learned representations. This involves computing similarity metrics between experts, and incorporating these into the training loss to penalize redundancy and encourage specialization. Specifically, we use a modality-agnostic similarity metric that can operate on both small and large MoE models. 
CONTROLS: We compare against two baselines: 1) the vanilla Moisture-of-Experts model, and 2) a model that uses a pairwise regularization term but with a fixed similarity metric that remains constant throughout training. 
COST: 14000
PREDICTION: We expect our pairwise expert regularization to improve the expressive capacity of MoE models, reduce expert homogenization, and lead to better performance in downstream tasks. However, this may fail if the regularization strength is too strong, causing the model to over-specialize and suffer from catastrophic forgetting.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Revising Pairwise Expert Regularization for Mixture-of-Experts
PROPOSAL: We revise the pairwise expert regularization term (Proposal 3) to add an additional filtering mechanism, where we consider only the top-k most similar experts for each token. This is done to alleviate potential over-penalization of experts that may still contribute valuable diversity, even if they are slightly redundant with their peers. Specifically, we use the popularity of each expert in the routing policy to determine their priority in the filtering mechanism.
CONTROLS: We compare against the original pairwise expert regularization (Proposal 3), and a baseline model that uses a uniform routing policy. 
COST: 15000
PREDICTION: We expect our revised pairwise expert regularization to better balance the need for orthogonality and diversity in expert representations, leading to improved performance and fewer cases of catastrophic forgetting. However, this may fail if the k-filtering mechanism becomes too aggressive and starts suppressing experts that might still contribute valuable knowledge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Asymmetric Routing Loss for Mixture-of-Experts
PROPOSAL: We propose an experiment where we introduce an asymmetric routing loss function to guide the routing policy's adaptation to the data distribution. The loss involves two terms: one measuring the entropy of the routing distribution, and another assessing the alignment of the experts' diets with their corresponding representations. By controlling the strength of these terms, we can promote either random or structured routing policies according to the task's requirements. Specifically, we modify the routing policy of the fair Moisture-of-Experts model to incorporate this loss function.
CONTROLS: We compare against three baselines: 1) the vanilla fair Moisture-of-Experts model, 2) a model with a uniform routing policy, and 3) a model with a pre-defined routing policy.
COST: 20560
PREDICTION: We expect our asymmetric routing loss to improve the adaptability of MoE models to diverse domains, by optimizing the routing policy for the specific task at hand. However, this may fail if the routing loss is too late to commit to a structured routing policy, leading to suboptimal performance in tasks that require consistent routing patterns.
